source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Dynamic Programming p. 79

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\sum_{j=1}^n p_j\). For \(i\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\) and \(q\in\{0,\ldots,P\}\), define
\[
C_i(q)=\min\left\{\sum_{j=1}^{i}w_jx_j:\sum_{j=1}^{i}p_jx_j=q,\ x\in\{0,1\}^{i}\right\},
\]
with the minimum of an empty set equal to \(+\infty\). Thus \(C_0(0)=0\), \(C_0(q)=+\infty\) for \(q>0\), and \(C_i(q)=\min\{C_{i-1}(q),w_i+C_{i-1}(q-p_i)\}\), where a negative profit index has value \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A state stores the minimum weight needed to attain each exact integer profit; feasible profit states identify the knapsack optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Profit-Indexed State Spaces

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Dynamic Programming p. 79

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent profit-indexed organization using minimum weight for attaining at least a target profit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\sum_{j=1}^np_j\). For \(i\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\) and \(q\in\{0,\ldots,P\}\), define \[D_i(q)=\min\left\{\sum_{j=1}^iw_jx_j:\sum_{j=1}^ip_jx_j\ge q,\ x\in\{0,1\}^i\right\},\] with \(\min\varnothing=+\infty\). Then \(D_0(0)=0\), \(D_0(q)=+\infty\) for \(q>0\), and \(D_i(q)=\min\{D_{i-1}(q),w_i+D_{i-1}(\max\{0,q-p_i\})\}\). The optimum is \(\max\{q:D_n(q)\le W\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equivalent profit-indexed state stores the least weight needed to reach each profit threshold rather than each exact profit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{OPT}=\max\{q\in\{0,\ldots,P\}:D_n(q)\le W\}.

notation.meaning: minimum weight attaining profit at least q from the first i items

knowledge_statements.title: Profit-Threshold State Representation

children.title: Pseudo-Polynomial Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity regimes governed by numerical magnitudes rather than encoding length alone.

assumptions_latex: All weights and the capacity are nonnegative integers encoded in binary.
Arithmetic and table operations on represented numbers have unit cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The capacity-indexed algorithm runs in \(O(nW)\) time and \(O(W)\) working space, which is pseudo-polynomial rather than polynomial in the binary input length.

notation.meaning: binary encoding length of the instance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unit-cost complexity of the capacity-indexed exact dynamic program.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Dynamic Programming p. 79
Chapter 10. Sizes and the theoretical complexity of linear inequalities and linear programming p. 120
source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The capacity-indexed table has \((n+1)(W+1)\) states and constant work per state, so it requires \(O(nW)\) arithmetic operations and \(O(nW)\) stored values, reducible to \(O(W)\) working space by retaining two rows. Because binary encoding permits \(W\) to be as large as \(2^{\Theta(L)}\), this bound is polynomial in the numerical value \(W\), but not necessarily polynomial in the input length \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Capacity-indexed dynamic programming uses time proportional to the numerical capacity, which may be exponential in the capacity's binary encoding length.
knowledge_statements.title: Pseudo-Polynomial Complexity

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Dynamic Programming p. 79
Chapter 10. Sizes and the theoretical complexity of linear inequalities and linear programming p. 120
source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Magnitude-sensitive complexity of exact profit-indexed 0-1 knapsack dynamic programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\sum_{i=1}^np_i\) for nonnegative integral profits. A row-compressed profit-indexed dynamic program evaluates \(O(nP)\) states in \(O(nP)\) arithmetic operations and \(O(P)\) working storage. Under binary encoding this is pseudo-polynomial because \(P\) may be exponential in the input length; it becomes polynomial when \(P\) is polynomially bounded in that length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Profit-indexed dynamic programming is pseudo-polynomial in total profit and becomes polynomial on polynomially bounded-profit instances.
assumptions_latex: Arithmetic and table operations on represented numbers have unit cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T(n,P)=O(nP),\qquad S(P)=O(P).
knowledge_statements.title: Profit-Indexed Pseudo-Polynomial Complexity

children.title: Knapsack Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Exact search organized through explicit candidate enumeration.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact two-list enumeration for single-capacity 0-1 knapsack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the item set as \(I=I_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}I_2\), with \(|I_j|\leq\lceil n/2\rceil\). Enumerate \((w(S),p(S))\) for every \(S\subseteq I_j\). Remove from the second list every pair dominated by a pair having no greater weight and no smaller profit. For each \(S\subseteq I_1\) with \(w(S)\leq B\), combine it with a retained second-list subset of greatest profit among those of weight at most \(B-w(S)\). The best combination is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerate both half-instance subset lists, Pareto-prune one list, and combine each first-half subset with its best compatible second-half subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p(S^*)=\max\{p(S):S\subseteq I,\ w(S)\leq B\}.

notation.meaning: total weight and profit of subset S

knowledge_statements.title: Meet-in-the-Middle Knapsack Enumeration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case unit-cost bounds for balanced two-list enumeration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A balanced partition produces at most \(2^{\lceil n/2\rceil}\) pairs per list. Direct subset generation, comparison sorting, Pareto pruning, and compatible-pair queries require \(O(n2^{n/2})\) unit-cost arithmetic and comparison operations and \(O(2^{n/2})\) stored pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Balanced meet-in-the-middle enumeration uses exponential time and memory with exponent approximately half the item count.
assumptions_latex: Arithmetic and comparisons on input-derived weights and profits have unit cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Meet-in-the-Middle Enumeration Bound

assumptions_latex: The instance has \(n\) items with profits \(p_i\) and weights \(w_i\), and capacity \(W\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns an optimal solution after examining at most \(2^n\) binary vectors.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive subset enumeration for exact 0-1 knapsack optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(z^*=-\infty\) and leave \(x^*\) undefined. Enumerate every \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\). If \(\sum_{i=1}^n w_ix_i\le W\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^n p_ix_i>z^*\), set \(x^*=x\) and \(z^*=\sum_{i=1}^n p_ix_i\). Stop after all \(2^n\) vectors have been tested and output \((x^*,z^*)\); if none is feasible, report infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Test every item subset, retain the most profitable feasible subset, and return it after at most two to the number-of-items tests.
knowledge_statements.title: Knapsack Enumeration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Exhaustive enumeration is an appropriate algorithm for this leaf, but no source or locator is supplied. The assumptions also do not explicitly state domains or sign conditions for the capacity and item data.

children.title: Tree-Based Bounding Search
children.top_down_role: Exact knapsack search using branching trees with bounding.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local and global certificates for maximization tree search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^*\) be attained by a feasible incumbent and let \(U(N)\) upper-bound every feasible completion below node \(N\). If \(U(N)\leq z^*\), then \(N\) contains no strictly improving solution and may be fathomed. If covering branches have exhausted or validly fathomed every node, the incumbent is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subtree is safely pruned when its certified upper bound cannot improve the feasible incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(z^*\) is attained by a feasible binary solution.
\(U(N)\) is valid for every feasible completion represented by \(N\).
The branching disjunctions cover every binary completion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U(N)\leq z^*\Rightarrow\max_{x\in N\cap F}p^{\mathsf T}x\leq z^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Knapsack Bound-Fathoming Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exponential boundary for item-variable branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A binary search that fixes one previously unfixed item at each branching step has depth at most \(n\) and generates at most \(2^{n+1}-1\) nodes. Valid bounds may reduce the processed tree but do not imply a polynomial worst-case node bound for unrestricted 0-1 knapsack.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Item branching gives a finite but potentially exponential tree; bounding may prune it without removing the worst-case exponential regime.
assumptions_latex: No item is branched on twice along a root-to-leaf path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\leq n,\qquad |V|\leq2^{n+1}-1.
knowledge_statements.title: Worst-Case Binary Search-Tree Size

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy upper bound for a residual maximization node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(N\), add the profit of items fixed to one and solve the residual relaxation \(0\leq x_i\leq1\), \(\sum_iw_ix_i\leq R_N\), by taking unfixed items in nonincreasing \(p_i/w_i\) order, with at most one item fractional. Its value \(U(N)\) upper-bounds every binary completion of \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedy fractional filling of the residual capacity upper-bounds every binary completion below a node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max\{p^{\mathsf T}x:x\text{ is a binary completion of }N\}\leq U(N).
knowledge_statements.title: Fractional-Knapsack Node Bound

assumptions_latex: Profits and weights are nonnegative, and items are ordered by nonincreasing ratio \(p_i/w_i\), with zero-weight positive-profit items fixed in.
At every search node, the fractional-knapsack relaxation is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon termination, the incumbent is globally optimal; a node with upper bound at most the incumbent value may be discarded.

notation.meaning: fractional-relaxation upper bound at node N

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact branch-and-bound using fractional-knapsack upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\mathcal{L}\) with the root node and \(z^*\) with any feasible solution value. Repeatedly select \(N\in\mathcal{L}\), compute its fractional-knapsack bound \(U(N)\), and discard \(N\) if \(U(N)\le z^*\). Otherwise update \(z^*\) from any feasible completion; if unfixed variables remain, branch on one variable by creating the children \(x_j=0\) and \(x_j=1\). Stop when \(\mathcal{L}=\varnothing\), and output the incumbent solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on item decisions, use fractional knapsack to bound each subtree, and prune any subtree unable to improve the incumbent solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Based Bounding Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The branch-and-bound idea fits the leaf, but the exact bounding and termination specification lacks an authoritative locator. The description should also explicitly remove a selected node from the active list and justify that every generated node is eventually processed.

children.title: Knapsack Core Methods
children.top_down_role: Exact or near-exact methods focused on a restricted set of critical items.

assumptions_latex: Items have positive weights and profits and are ordered by nonincreasing efficiency \(p_i/w_i\).
The fractional-knapsack relaxation has a unique split item after a fixed tie-breaking rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The core is a restricted neighborhood of the split index within which exact search is performed while variables outside it are fixed provisionally.

notation.meaning: split-item index in the greedy fractional solution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic split-item core restriction; specific core-selection and expansion rules vary by algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve the fractional relaxation and let \(s\) be its split-item index. Choose \(k\ge 0\) and set \(C=\{i:\lvert i-s\rvert\le k\}\cap\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Provisionally fix indices below the core as in the greedy prefix and indices above the core to zero. Solve the residual binary knapsack over \(x_i\) for \(i\in C\). If the selected certification or expansion test fails, enlarge \(C\) and repeat; output only after the test certifies that excluded variables cannot improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a restricted knapsack around the fractional split item, expanding the core until the chosen test certifies that excluded items cannot improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Knapsack Core Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Core construction and exactness certification vary materially among knapsack core algorithms. No source identifies or supports this particular split-centered core, fixing convention, expansion test, or certification claim.

children.title: Core-Search Integration
children.top_down_role: Integration of core restriction with enumeration or tree-based search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract exact-search protocol coupling adaptive core optimization to full-node bounding and exhaustive branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each live node \(N\), select and solve a core \(C(N)\) to seek a full-instance-feasible incumbent, compute or verify an upper bound \(U(N)\) valid for all completions of \(N\), and prune when \(U(N)\le z^*\). Otherwise expand the core or branch so that the children are disjoint and collectively cover every unresolved completion. If the binary domains are finite, each unpruned step fixes a previously unfixed binary or otherwise finitely resolves the node, and every pruning bound is valid, termination with no live nodes certifies that the incumbent is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use cores for candidate generation, but combine them with full-node valid bounds and exhaustive finite branching to retain exactness.
assumptions_latex: The residual binary domains are finite.
Every incumbent candidate is checked against the full node and original knapsack constraints.
Every pruned node has a valid full-node upper bound.
Branching children exhaustively cover their parent's unresolved completions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{If the live-node set becomes empty, the returned incumbent is globally optimal.}
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Core-Search Integration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity requirements for using a restricted knapsack core inside exact search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node \(N\), optimizing a restricted item core \(C(N)\) may supply a feasible completion and search guidance. It supplies a pruning bound only if the reported upper bound \(U(N)\) is valid for every completion represented by \(N\), including choices involving items outside \(C(N)\). A restricted-core optimum alone is not such an upper bound unless an additional certificate proves that excluded items cannot improve it. Every incumbent update must also be feasible for the full residual knapsack instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A core may generate incumbents and guidance, but pruning requires a bound valid for all node completions, not merely the restricted-core optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) represents a residual 0-1 knapsack search node.
\(C(N)\) is a subset of the unfixed residual items.
The problem is formulated as profit maximization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U(N)\ge\max\{p(x):x\text{ completes }N\}\text{ is required before pruning by }U(N)\le z^*.

notation.meaning: restricted item core at node N
upper bound valid for every completion of N

knowledge_statements.title: Safe Core-to-Search Contract

assumptions_latex: A search node fixes some item variables and leaves a residual 0-1 knapsack instance.
The core subproblem solver returns a feasible completion and a valid upper bound or expansion certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pruning remains valid whenever the integrated bound \(U(N)\) is a valid upper bound on every completion of node \(N\).

notation.meaning: adaptive item core at node N
valid upper bound for node N

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic integration of adaptive core optimization into exact tree search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each selected node \(N\), form a core \(C(N)\) for its residual instance and solve the core subproblem to update the incumbent. Compute a valid bound \(U(N)\) using the core result and a relaxation of excluded variables. Prune \(N\) when \(U(N)\le z^*\); otherwise expand \(C(N)\) or branch on an unfixed variable. Stop when every live node has been pruned or completely resolved, and return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each search node, solve an adaptive core, use it to improve and bound the node, then prune, expand the core, or branch.
knowledge_statements.title: Core-Search Integration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local topic fit, but the integration protocol and construction of a valid bound from the core and excluded variables are left generic and have no supporting source locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical profit-scaling fully polynomial approximation scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Remove items with \(w_i>W\) and fix every zero-weight positive-profit item into the solution. If no other profitable item remains, return the fixed items. Otherwise let \(P_{\max}=\max_i p_i\), set \(K=\varepsilon P_{\max}/n\), and define \(q_i=\lfloor p_i/K\rfloor\). Use a profit-indexed dynamic program to find a capacity-feasible subset maximizing \(\sum_i q_i x_i\), and return it together with the fixed items. The result \(\widehat x\) satisfies \(p(\widehat x)\ge(1-\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}\). Since \(\sum_iq_i\le n^2/\varepsilon\), a direct implementation uses \(O(n^3/\varepsilon)\) state updates and \(O(n^2/\varepsilon)\) row-compressed states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Round profits down at an accuracy-dependent scale and solve the bounded profit-indexed dynamic program to obtain a one-minus-epsilon approximation in fully polynomial time.
assumptions_latex: Overweight items are removed and zero-weight profitable items are fixed before scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p(\widehat x)\ge(1-\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT},\qquad T=O(n^3/\varepsilon),\qquad S=O(n^2/\varepsilon).

notation.meaning: largest profit among remaining individually feasible items
scaled integral profit of item i

knowledge_statements.title: Profit-Scaling FPTAS for 0-1 Knapsack

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation-scheme terminology for profit-maximization 0-1 knapsack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A polynomial-time approximation scheme is a family \(\{A_\varepsilon:0<\varepsilon<1\}\) that returns a feasible solution satisfying \(p(A_\varepsilon(I))\ge(1-\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}(I)\) and runs in polynomial time in the encoded instance length for each fixed \(\varepsilon\). It is a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme when its running time is polynomial jointly in the encoded instance length and \(1/\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PTAS gives a feasible one-minus-epsilon approximation in polynomial time for fixed epsilon; an FPTAS is also polynomial in inverse epsilon.
assumptions_latex: The instance is a nonnegative-profit maximization 0-1 knapsack instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p(A_\varepsilon(I))\ge(1-\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}(I).
knowledge_statements.title: PTAS and FPTAS for 0-1 Knapsack

assumptions_latex: Profits and weights are nonnegative integers, \(W\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\), and \(0<\varepsilon<1\).
Items with \(w_i>W\) are removed, and zero-weight profitable items are fixed in.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output satisfies \(p(\widehat{x})\ge(1-\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}\), and the running time is polynomial in \(n\) and \(1/\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Profit-scaling FPTAS for maximization 0-1 knapsack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If no profitable item remains, output the fixed zero-weight items. Otherwise set \(P_{\max}=\max_i p_i\), \(K=\varepsilon P_{\max}/n\), and \(q_i=\lfloor p_i/K\rfloor\). Apply profit-indexed dynamic programming to the instance with profits \(q_i\), selecting a feasible vector \(\widehat{x}\) having maximum scaled profit. Return \(\widehat{x}\) together with the fixed zero-weight items. Since \(\sum_i q_i\le n^2/\varepsilon\), the dynamic program is polynomial in \(n\) and \(1/\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Round profits downward at an accuracy-dependent scale, solve the resulting profit-indexed dynamic program, and obtain a feasible solution within a factor one minus epsilon of optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Knapsack Approximation Schemes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The profit-scaling FPTAS is mathematically plausible and appropriately classified as an algorithm, but its approximation guarantee and polynomial running-time claim require an authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: Set Packing
children.top_down_role: Selection models over mutually conflicting sets.

assumptions_latex: The ground set is \(E=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and \(\mathcal{S}=\{S_1,\ldots,S_m\}\subseteq 2^E\) is a finite family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible binary vectors are exactly incidence vectors of pairwise disjoint subfamilies of \(\mathcal{S}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted finite set packing in its standard binary incidence formulation.

source_refs.locator: 2.4.1 Set Packing and Stable Sets p. 51

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(A_{ej}=1\) if \(e\in S_j\) and \(A_{ej}=0\) otherwise. The weighted set-packing problem is
\[
\max\left\{\sum_{j=1}^m c_jx_j:Ax\le\mathbf{1},\ x\in\{0,1\}^m\right\}.
\]
For every \(e\in E\), the inequality \(\sum_{j:e\in S_j}x_j\le1\) forbids selecting two sets containing the same element. Hence a feasible selection \(\{S_j:x_j=1\}\) is a pairwise disjoint subfamily, and every pairwise disjoint subfamily defines a feasible vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set packing selects a maximum-weight subfamily of pairwise disjoint sets, represented by one binary variable per set and one packing constraint per ground element.
knowledge_statements.title: Set Packing

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4.1 Set Packing and Stable Sets p. 51

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case complexity of the finite unweighted decision problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The decision problem asking whether a finite set system contains at least \(k\) pairwise disjoint members is NP-complete; it remains NP-complete when every available set has cardinality three.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set-packing decision is NP-complete, even for 3-element sets.
assumptions_latex: The set system and \(k\) are explicitly encoded.
Membership in NP is measured under the ordinary finite encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\textsc{Set Packing}\) and its 3-uniform restriction are NP-complete.
knowledge_statements.title: Computational Hardness of Set Packing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Downward closure and inclusion-wise maximality for finite set packings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal S\) is a packing, then every \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathcal C\) is a packing. Moreover, \(\mathcal C\) is inclusion-wise maximal if and only if every \(S\in\mathcal S\setminus\mathcal C\) intersects some member of \(\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set-packing feasibility is hereditary, and a packing is maximal exactly when every unselected set conflicts with a selected set.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal S\) is a finite family of sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C\text{ maximal}\iff \forall S\in\mathcal S\setminus\mathcal C\;\exists T\in\mathcal C:S\cap T\ne\varnothing.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Hereditary Feasibility and Maximality Certificate

children.title: Stable Set
children.top_down_role: Vertex-selection models governed by graph adjacency conflicts.

assumptions_latex: The graph \(G=(V,E)\) is finite and simple.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible binary vectors are exactly incidence vectors of stable sets in \(G\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted stable set with edge inequalities and binary variables.

source_refs.locator: 2.4.1 Set Packing and Stable Sets p. 51

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A set \(S\subseteq V\) is stable if no edge has both endpoints in \(S\). Its weighted optimization formulation is
\[
\max\left\{\sum_{v\in V}c_vx_v:x_u+x_v\le1\ \text{for every }\{u,v\}\in E,\ x\in\{0,1\}^{V}\right\}.
\]
For a binary vector \(x\), the edge inequalities hold exactly when \(S(x)=\{v\in V:x_v=1\}\) contains no adjacent pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stable set contains no adjacent vertices; binary edge inequalities prohibit selecting both endpoints of every edge.
knowledge_statements.title: Stable Set

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4.1 Set Packing and Stable Sets p. 51

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate for inclusion-wise maximality, not maximum weight or cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stable set \(S\subseteq V\) is inclusion-wise maximal if and only if every vertex in \(V\setminus S\) has a neighbor in \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stable set is maximal exactly when it dominates every unselected vertex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\text{ maximal}\iff \forall v\in V\setminus S\;\exists u\in S:\{u,v\}\in E.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Maximal Stable-Set Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case complexity of the cardinality decision problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite graph \(G\) and integer \(k\), deciding whether \(G\) has a stable set of cardinality at least \(k\) is NP-complete. Consequently, maximum-cardinality and general maximum-weight stable set are NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stable-set decision is NP-complete, and its optimization versions are NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\textsc{Independent Set}\) is NP-complete.
knowledge_statements.title: Computational Hardness of Stable Set

children.title: Hypergraph Matching
children.top_down_role: Selection models over pairwise compatible hyperedges.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical maximal and weighted-greedy approximation for rank-bounded hypergraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) have rank at most \(r\). In the unweighted case, repeatedly selecting any remaining hyperedge and deleting every intersecting hyperedge returns a maximal matching \(M\) with \(|M|\ge \operatorname{OPT}/r\). With nonnegative weights, repeatedly selecting a maximum-weight remaining hyperedge and deleting every intersecting hyperedge returns \(M\) with \(c(M)\ge\operatorname{OPT}/r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximal matching is a 1/r-approximation in rank-r hypergraphs; choosing a heaviest remaining edge gives the same factor for nonnegative weights.
assumptions_latex: The finite hypergraph has rank at most \(r\ge1\).
For the weighted variant, \(c_j\ge0\) for every hyperedge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c(M)\ge\frac1r\operatorname{OPT}\quad\text{(and }|M|\ge\operatorname{OPT}/r\text{ in the unweighted case)}.

notation.meaning: matching returned by the greedy procedure

knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Matching in Bounded-Rank Hypergraphs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity boundary between graph matching and higher-rank hypergraph matching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every hyperedge has cardinality at most two, maximum-weight hypergraph matching is the ordinary graph-matching problem and is solvable in polynomial time. In contrast, deciding whether a 3-uniform hypergraph has a matching of cardinality at least \(k\) is NP-complete. Hence unrestricted hypergraph matching is NP-hard, already at rank three.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank-two matching is polynomial-time graph matching, whereas matching is NP-complete in decision form already for 3-uniform hypergraphs.
assumptions_latex: The hypergraph is finite and explicitly represented.
For the hardness statement, all hyperedges have cardinality three and \(k\) is part of the input.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}(H)\le2\Rightarrow\text{polynomial-time solvable},\qquad \textsc{3-Set Matching}\text{ is NP-complete}.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank Boundary for Hypergraph Matching

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted matching in a finite, possibly nonuniform, indexed hypergraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=(V,(E_j)_{j\in J})\) be a finite indexed hypergraph. A matching is a set \(M\subseteq J\) such that \(E_j\cap E_k=\varnothing\) for all distinct \(j,k\in M\). With incidence matrix \(A_{vj}=1\) exactly when \(v\in E_j\), maximum-weight hypergraph matching is \[\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le\mathbf1,\ x\in\{0,1\}^J\}.\] Thus feasible binary vectors are exactly incidence vectors of matchings; a matching itself need not be maximum-weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hypergraph matching is any pairwise vertex-disjoint indexed subfamily of hyperedges; maximum-weight matching optimizes over all such subfamilies.
assumptions_latex: \((E_j)_{j\in J}\) is an indexed family of subsets of \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ax\le\mathbf1,\ x\in\{0,1\}^J\iff \{j:x_j=1\}\text{ indexes pairwise disjoint hyperedges}.
knowledge_statements.title: Hypergraph Matching

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hypergraph matching, covering, and vertex-packing representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions, bounds, complexity boundary, and graph representations for finite hypergraph matching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite hypergraph \(H=(V(H),E(H))\), a matching is a pairwise disjoint subfamily of \(E(H)\), with maximum cardinality \(
u(H)\). A point cover is a set \(C\subseteq V(H)\) meeting every line, with minimum cardinality \(	au(H)\), and \(
u(H)\leq	au(H)\). Determining \(
u(H)\) is NP-complete even for \(3\)-uniform hypergraphs. If \(L(H)\) is the intersection graph of the lines of \(H\), then \(
u(H)=\alpha(L(H))\). For every graph \(G\), \(\alpha(G)=
u(\operatorname{St}(G))=
u(\operatorname{Cl}(G))\). The clique-hypergraph construction can have exponentially many points and therefore need not be polynomial-time constructible. A hypergraph has the Helly property if every finite pairwise-intersecting family of its lines has nonempty total intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hypergraph matching is a family of pairwise disjoint hyperedges, while a point cover meets every hyperedge, so maximum matching size is at most minimum cover size. Hypergraph matching is NP-complete even for 3-uniform hypergraphs and is equivalent to graph vertex packing through intersection, star, and clique constructions. Clique hypergraphs can be exponentially large. The extract also defines the Helly property for hypergraphs.

u(\operatorname{St}(G))=

children.title: Conflict-Graph Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between set-packing conflicts and stable-set representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Graph Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence for binary packing systems whose infeasibility is completely determined by conflicting pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq 2^V\) be a downward-closed family, and define its conflict graph \(G_F=(V,E_F)\) by \(\{u,v\}\in E_F\) exactly when \(\{u,v\}\notin F\). Every member of \(F\) is a stable set of \(G_F\). Conversely, every stable set of \(G_F\) belongs to \(F\) if and only if every inclusion-minimal member of \(2^V\setminus F\) has cardinality two. Thus a binary packing family has an exact conflict-graph representation precisely when it has no irreducible conflict involving three or more variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A downward-closed binary packing family equals the stable sets of its conflict graph exactly when all minimal infeasible selections are pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\operatorname{Stab}(G_F)\iff \min(2^V\setminus F)\subseteq \binom{V}{2}\).

notation.meaning: pairwise conflict graph of the family
family of stable vertex sets of the graph

source_refs.locator: 2.4 Packing, Covering, Partitioning p. 51

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 Packing, Covering, Partitioning p. 51

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Irreducible Ternary Conflict Escapes Every Conflict Graph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smallest higher-order failure of exact pairwise conflict representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\{1,2,3\}\) and \(F=\{S\subseteq V:|S|\le2\}\). Then \(F\) is downward closed and every pair belongs to \(F\), so its conflict graph has no edges. Consequently \(V\) is stable in that graph although \(V\notin F\). Thus a minimal infeasible triple cannot be represented by pairwise conflict edges without auxiliary structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every pair is feasible but one triple is infeasible, the conflict graph is empty and incorrectly admits that triple.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\subsetneq\operatorname{Stab}(G_F)=2^V.
knowledge_statements.title: Irreducible Ternary Conflict Escapes Every Conflict Graph

children.title: Incidence-Hypergraph Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between packing systems and hypergraph matching structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Incidence-Hypergraph Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix–hypergraph equivalence for zero-one set-packing constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\{0,1\}^{U\times J}\), and associate with every column \(j\in J\) the hyperedge \(E_j=\{u\in U:A_{uj}=1\}\). For \(x\in\{0,1\}^J\), the packing inequalities \(Ax\leq \mathbf 1\) hold if and only if the selected hyperedges \(\{E_j:x_j=1\}\) are pairwise disjoint. Consequently, maximizing \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to these inequalities is exactly the maximum-weight matching problem in the incidence hypergraph \((U,\{E_j:j\in J\})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-one packing matrix is a hypergraph incidence matrix, and its feasible binary vectors select pairwise disjoint hyperedges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax\leq\mathbf 1\iff E_j\cap E_k=\varnothing\) for all distinct selected \(j,k\).

notation.meaning: row set and hypergraph vertex set

source_refs.locator: 2.4 Packing, Covering, Partitioning p. 51

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 Packing, Covering, Partitioning p. 51

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicity and empty-column boundary of the incidence correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matrix–hypergraph correspondence is bijective at the level of columns only when hyperedges retain their indices. If \(E_j=E_k\) for \(j\ne k\), passage to a simple hypergraph collapses two decision variables and may change objectives and feasible selections. Empty columns correspond to distinct indexed empty hyperedges, all of which satisfy every row of \(Ax\le\mathbf1\). Therefore the faithful object is an indexed hypergraph, equivalently a hypergraph with labeled parallel edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A faithful incidence correspondence retains duplicate and empty columns as distinct labeled hyperedges.
assumptions_latex: Column indices represent distinct decision variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: j\mapsto E_j\text{ preserves the packing model only for the indexed family }(E_j)_{j\in J}.
knowledge_statements.title: Indexed Hyperedges Preserve Packing Columns

children.title: Set Covering
children.top_down_role: Selection models requiring every indexed element to be covered.

knowledge_statements.title: Set Covering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted finite set covering in incidence-matrix form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite ground set \(U\), a family \(\mathcal S=(S_j)_{j\in J}\) of subsets of \(U\), and costs \(c_j\), the set-covering problem selects minimum-cost members whose union contains \(U\). With incidence coefficients \(A_{uj}=1\) when \(u\in S_j\) and \(A_{uj}=0\) otherwise, its binary formulation is \[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\geq\mathbf 1,\ x\in\{0,1\}^J\}.\] It is feasible exactly when every element of \(U\) belongs to at least one member of \(\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set covering chooses a minimum-cost subfamily whose union contains every ground-set element.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is feasible exactly when \(\bigcup_{j:x_j=1}S_j=U\).

source_refs.locator: 2.4.3 Set Covering and Transversals p. 53

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4.3 Set Covering and Transversals p. 53

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-effectiveness greedy approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(c_j\ge0\) and every element is coverable. Starting with covered set \(C=\varnothing\), repeatedly choose a set \(S_j\) minimizing \(c_j/|S_j\setminus C|\) among sets covering a new element, and update \(C\leftarrow C\cup S_j\). The returned cover has cost at most \(H_d\operatorname{OPT}\), where \(d=\max_j|S_j|\); hence it is also an \(H_{|U|}\)-approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedy selection by cost per newly covered element is an H_d-approximation when available sets have size at most d, and therefore an H_n-approximation on n elements.
assumptions_latex: The instance is finite and feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c(C_{\mathrm{greedy}})\le H_d\operatorname{OPT}\le H_{|U|}\operatorname{OPT}.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Greedy Set Cover

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical complexity of explicitly represented unweighted set cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite ground set \(U\), an explicitly listed family \(\mathcal S\subseteq2^U\), and \(k\in\mathbb Z_+\), deciding whether at most \(k\) members of \(\mathcal S\) cover \(U\) is NP-complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite unweighted set-cover decision is NP-complete.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) and \(\mathcal S\) are finite and explicitly represented.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \textsc{Set Cover}\text{ is NP-complete}.

notation.meaning: maximum allowed number of selected sets

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Cover Decision Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical LP relaxation and packing dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c\in\mathbb R_+^J\), \[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge\mathbf1,\ x\ge0\}=\max\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c,\ y\ge0\}.\] The dual assigns nonnegative prices to elements so that the total price contained in each available set does not exceed that set's cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fractional set cover is dual to packing element prices within every set's cost.
assumptions_latex: The finite covering instance is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge\mathbf1,x\ge0\}=\max\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c,y\ge0\}.

notation.meaning: dual price assigned to ground element u

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Set-Cover Dual

children.title: Hitting Set
children.top_down_role: Selection models requiring chosen elements to intersect prescribed sets.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) is a hitting set if and only if \(T\cap E\neq\varnothing\) for every \(E\in\mathcal E\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted hitting set for a finite family of subsets.

source_refs.locator: 2.4.3 Set Covering and Transversals p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite, let \(\mathcal E\subseteq 2^V\), and assign each vertex \(v\in V\) a cost \(w_v\). A hitting set is a subset \(T\subseteq V\) satisfying \(T\cap E\neq\varnothing\) for every \(E\in\mathcal E\). With \(B_{Ev}=1\) exactly when \(v\in E\), the minimum-weight hitting-set problem is \[\min\{w^{\mathsf T}y:By\geq\mathbf 1,\ y\in\{0,1\}^V\}.\] It is feasible exactly when \(\varnothing\notin\mathcal E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hitting set is a vertex subset meeting every member of the given set family; the minimum-weight hitting-set problem minimizes its total vertex cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Hitting Set

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4.3 Set Covering and Transversals p. 53

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy approximation for an explicitly listed finite family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(w_v\ge0\) and \(\varnothing\notin\mathcal E\). Starting with all edges uncovered, repeatedly choose a vertex \(v\) minimizing \(w_v/|\{E\text{ uncovered}:v\in E\}|\), delete the newly hit edges, and stop when none remain. The resulting hitting set \(T\) satisfies \(w(T)\le H_{|\mathcal E|}\operatorname{OPT}\), where \(H_m=\sum_{i=1}^m1/i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedy selection by cost per newly hit edge is an H_m-approximation for m explicitly listed edges.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal E\) is finite, explicitly listed, and contains no empty edge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w(T)\le H_{|\mathcal E|}\operatorname{OPT}.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Greedy Hitting Set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical complexity of explicitly represented unweighted hitting set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite family \(\mathcal E\subseteq2^V\) and \(k\in\mathbb Z_+\), deciding whether there exists \(T\subseteq V\) with \(|T|\le k\) and \(T\cap E\ne\varnothing\) for every \(E\in\mathcal E\) is NP-complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite unweighted hitting-set decision is NP-complete.
assumptions_latex: The instance is explicitly represented and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \textsc{Hitting Set}\text{ is NP-complete}.
knowledge_statements.title: Hitting-Set Decision Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear relaxation and its packing dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w\in\mathbb R_+^V\) and edge-by-vertex incidence matrix \(B\), \[\min\{w^{\mathsf T}y:By\ge\mathbf1,\ y\ge0\}=\max\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}z:B^{\mathsf T}z\le w,\ z\ge0\}.\] The dual assigns nonnegative weight to edges, with the total weight through each vertex bounded by its cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The fractional hitting-set LP is dual to packing edge weights subject to vertex-cost capacities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{w^{\mathsf T}y:By\ge\mathbf1,y\ge0\}=\max\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}z:B^{\mathsf T}z\le w,z\ge0\}.

notation.meaning: dual weight assigned to edge E

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Hitting-Set Dual

children.title: Hypergraph Transversals
children.top_down_role: Hypergraph viewpoints centered on vertex sets intersecting every hyperedge.

knowledge_statements.title: Hypergraph Transversals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transversals and the transversal hypergraph of a finite hypergraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite hypergraph \(H=(V,\mathcal E)\), a transversal is a set \(T\subseteq V\) such that \(T\cap E\neq\varnothing\) for every \(E\in\mathcal E\). It is minimal when no proper subset of \(T\) remains a transversal. The transversal hypergraph, also called the blocker, is \[\operatorname{Tr}(H)=\bigl(V,\{T\subseteq V:T\text{ is an inclusion-minimal transversal of }H\}\bigr).\] Thus its hyperedges are minimal under inclusion, not necessarily minimum-cardinality transversals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hypergraph transversal meets every edge; the transversal hypergraph consists of all inclusion-minimal such sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E(\operatorname{Tr}(H))=\min_{\subseteq}\{T\subseteq V:T\cap E\neq\varnothing\ \forall E\in\mathcal E\}.\)

source_refs.locator: 2.4.3 Set Covering and Transversals p. 53

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4.3 Set Covering and Transversals p. 53

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of inclusion-minimal hyperedges from minimal transversals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\min(H)\) be obtained from a finite hypergraph \(H\) by deleting every edge that properly contains another edge, and let \(\operatorname{Tr}(H)\) contain its inclusion-minimal transversals. Then \[\operatorname{Tr}(\operatorname{Tr}(H))=\min(H).\] In particular, if \(H\) is a clutter, then \(\operatorname{Tr}(\operatorname{Tr}(H))=H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking minimal transversals twice recovers the inclusion-minimal edges, and exactly recovers a clutter.
assumptions_latex: Hyperedges are subsets of a common vertex set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Tr}(\operatorname{Tr}(H))=\min(H).

notation.meaning: clutter of inclusion-minimal edges of H

knowledge_statements.title: Blocker Involution for Finite Clutters

children.title: Cover–Hitting Duality
children.top_down_role: Incidence-transpose relationship between covering and hitting-set representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Cover–Hitting Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial equivalence obtained by transposing the incidence relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be finite and \(\mathcal S=(S_j)_{j\in J}\). Form the dual hypergraph \(H^*=(J,\{E_u:u\in U\})\), where \(E_u=\{j\in J:u\in S_j\}\). A subfamily indexed by \(C\subseteq J\) covers \(U\) if and only if \(C\) is a hitting set of \(H^*\). Under identical costs on indices, the feasible vectors and objective values coincide; algebraically, set covering by the incidence matrix \(A\) is hitting set for the transposed incidence description.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choosing sets that cover every element is identical to hitting each element-indexed edge in the dual incidence hypergraph.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\{0,1\}^{U\times J}\) is the incidence matrix of \(\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigcup_{j\in C}S_j=U\iff C\cap E_u\neq\varnothing\) for every \(u\in U\).

notation.meaning: dual incidence hypergraph on set indices
indices of sets containing element u

source_refs.locator: 2.4.3 Set Covering and Transversals p. 53

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4.3 Set Covering and Transversals p. 53

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applying indexed incidence dualization twice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite indexed set system \(\mathcal S=(S_j)_{j\in J}\) on \(U\), define \(E_u=\{j\in J:u\in S_j\}\). Dualizing \((E_u)_{u\in U}\) again gives \(F_j=\{u\in U:j\in E_u\}=S_j\) for every \(j\in J\). Thus incidence dualization is involutive when row and column labels, including repeated sets, are retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transposing an indexed incidence relation twice restores the original labeled set system, including repeated members.
assumptions_latex: Equal sets with distinct indices remain distinct members of the indexed family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_j=\{u:j\in E_u\}=S_j\quad\forall j\in J.

notation.meaning: dual edge of set indices containing u
set obtained after the second dualization

knowledge_statements.title: Involutivity of Incidence Dualization

children.title: Minimal Transversal Structure
children.top_down_role: Inclusion-minimal transversal families within covering systems.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\text{ is inclusion-minimal}\iff \forall v\in T\ \exists E_v\in\mathcal E:\ E_v\cap T=\{v\}.\)

notation.meaning: private edge witnessing the necessity of v

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Private-edge characterization of inclusion-minimal hypergraph transversals.

source_refs.locator: 2.4.3 Set Covering and Transversals p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=(V,\mathcal E)\) be finite and let \(T\subseteq V\) be a transversal. Then \(T\) is inclusion-minimal if and only if every \(v\in T\) has a private edge, namely an edge \(E_v\in\mathcal E\) satisfying \(E_v\cap T=\{v\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transversal is inclusion-minimal exactly when each selected vertex uniquely hits some edge relative to that transversal.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Transversal Structure

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4.3 Set Covering and Transversals p. 53

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Antichain and upward-closure structure for finite hypergraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite hypergraph \(H=(V,\mathcal E)\), the family \(\mathcal T_{\min}\) of inclusion-minimal transversals is an antichain. Every transversal contains a member of \(\mathcal T_{\min}\), and hence \[\mathcal T(H)=\{T\subseteq V:\exists M\in\mathcal T_{\min},\ M\subseteq T\}.\] A contained minimal transversal can be obtained by repeatedly deleting a vertex whenever its removal preserves transversality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimal transversals form the unique antichain of minimal members whose upward closure is the family of all transversals; an individual transversal may contain more than one minimal transversal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal T(H)=\uparrow\mathcal T_{\min},\qquad \mathcal T_{\min}\text{ is an antichain}.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Transversals Generate All Transversals

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite set systems and their inclusion-minimal hitting sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let E be finite and \mathcal S\subseteq2^E. The family \mathcal S is a clutter if, for every two distinct S_i,S_j\in\mathcal S, both S_i\setminus S_j and S_j\setminus S_i are nonempty. A set T\subseteq E is a transversal of \mathcal S if T\cap S_i\neq\varnothing for every S_i\in\mathcal S. The family b(\mathcal S) of all inclusionwise minimal transversals of \mathcal S is itself a clutter and is called the blocker of \mathcal S.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clutter is a finite set family in which no member contains another. A transversal meets every member, and the family of all inclusion-minimal transversals is itself a clutter called the blocker.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b(\mathcal S)=\{T\subseteq E:T\text{ is an inclusionwise minimal transversal of }\mathcal S\}\text{ is a clutter}.

children.title: Exact Cover
children.top_down_role: Combinatorial exact-coverage instances over set systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Cover
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unweighted exact cover for a finite set system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite ground set \(U\) and a family \(\mathcal S\subseteq 2^U\), an exact cover is a subfamily \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal S\) such that every element of \(U\) belongs to exactly one member of \(\mathcal C\). Equivalently, the members of \(\mathcal C\) are pairwise disjoint and satisfy \(\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal C}S=U\). The exact-cover decision problem asks whether at least one such subfamily exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact cover is a pairwise-disjoint subfamily whose union equals the ground set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C\text{ is exact}\iff \sum_{S\in\mathcal C}\mathbf 1_{\{u\in S\}}=1\) for every \(u\in U\).

source_refs.locator: 2.4 Packing, Covering, Partitioning p. 51

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 Packing, Covering, Partitioning p. 51

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exact branching search for feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an uncovered element \(u\). For each available set \(S\ni u\), create a branch selecting \(S\), remove the elements of \(S\), and discard every remaining set intersecting \(S\). A branch succeeds when no elements remain and fails when a residual element belongs to no remaining set. The original instance is feasible if and only if some branch succeeds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on which available set covers a chosen element, then remove that set's elements and all intersecting alternatives.
assumptions_latex: Every branch retains only sets disjoint from previously selected sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{instance feasible}\iff\text{some recursively generated branch reaches an empty residual universe}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Cover Branching Recursion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case complexity of exact-cover feasibility and its 3-set restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The exact-cover decision problem is NP-complete. It remains NP-complete for Exact Cover by 3-Sets (X3C): \(|U|=3q\), every member of \(\mathcal S\) has cardinality three, and the question is whether \(q\) members partition \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact cover is NP-complete even when every available set has three elements.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) and \(\mathcal S\) are explicitly encoded and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\textsc{Exact Cover}\) and \(\textsc{X3C}\) are NP-complete.

notation.meaning: number of triples required in an X3C solution

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Cover and X3C Complexity

children.title: Partition–Exact-Cover Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Representational correspondence between set-partitioning models and exact-cover instances.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=\mathbf 1\iff C_x=\{j\in J:x_j=1\}\) is an indexed exact cover of \(U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equivalence between incidence-matrix partitioning and indexed exact cover.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 Packing, Covering, Partitioning p. 51

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\{0,1\}^{U\times J}\), and define \(S_j=\{u\in U:A_{uj}=1\}\) for each \(j\in J\). For \(x\in\{0,1\}^J\), let \(C_x=\{j\in J:x_j=1\}\). Then \(Ax=\mathbf 1\) if and only if every \(u\in U\) belongs to exactly one set \(S_j\) indexed by \(j\in C_x\). The mapping \(x\mapsto C_x\) is a bijection between binary solutions and indexed exact covers, including when distinct columns represent the same subset. Under column costs \(c_j\), it preserves the objective value \(c^{\mathsf T}x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary set-partitioning solutions correspond bijectively to selected column indices that cover every ground-set element exactly once.
knowledge_statements.title: Partition–Exact-Cover Correspondence

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 Packing, Covering, Partitioning p. 51

children.title: Infeasible Overlap Regimes
children.top_down_role: Overlap structures that prevent exact coverage.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl(\exists u\in U:I(u)=\varnothing\bigr)\lor\bigl(\exists p,q,S_p,S_q:\ I(p)=\{S_p\},\ I(q)=\{S_q\},\ S_p\neq S_q,\ S_p\cap S_q\neq\varnothing\bigr)\) implies that no exact cover of \(U\) by \(\mathcal S\) exists.

notation.meaning: unique sets incident to the forced elements

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncovered-element and forced-overlap obstructions to exact-cover feasibility.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 Packing, Covering, Partitioning p. 51

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be finite, let \(\mathcal S\subseteq 2^U\), and define \(I(u)=\{S\in\mathcal S:u\in S\}\) for \(u\in U\). No exact cover exists if either \(I(u)=\varnothing\) for some \(u\in U\), or there are distinct elements \(p,q\in U\) and distinct sets \(S_p,S_q\in\mathcal S\) such that \(I(p)=\{S_p\}\), \(I(q)=\{S_q\}\), and \(S_p\cap S_q\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact cover is impossible if an element belongs to no available set or if two elements force distinct available sets that overlap.
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible Overlap Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 Packing, Covering, Partitioning p. 51

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound propagation and contradiction detection for residual exact-cover instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a residual exact-cover instance, if an uncovered element \(u\) belongs to exactly one remaining set \(S\), then every exact cover extending the residual branch must select \(S\). Selecting \(S\) permits removal of its covered elements and every other remaining set intersecting \(S\). If any residual element then has no incident set, the branch is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniquely coverable element forces its sole set; propagation removes intersecting alternatives and detects empty-incidence contradictions.
assumptions_latex: The residual family contains only sets compatible with earlier selections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|I(u)|=1\Rightarrow S\text{ is forced};\quad I(v)=\varnothing\Rightarrow\text{the residual branch is infeasible}.\)

notation.meaning: remaining sets containing residual element u

knowledge_statements.title: Forced-Set Propagation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to sufficiency of the seed's initial uncovered-element and forced-overlap tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{1,2,3\}\) and \(\mathcal S=\{\{1,2\},\{2,3\},\{1,3\}\}\). Every element belongs to two available sets, so initially there is neither an uncovered element nor a uniquely forced set. Nevertheless no exact cover exists: any selected set leaves one element, and every set covering that element overlaps the selected set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A triangle of three two-element sets is infeasible although neither elementary obstruction is initially present.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal S\text{ exact},\quad |I(u)|=2\text{ for every }u\in U.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Local Obstructions Are Not Complete

children.title: Large-Row Set-System Models
children.top_down_role: Set-system models with exceptionally many constraints or indexed requirements.

assumptions_latex: \(J\) and the implicit family \(\mathcal R\) are finite.
The separation routine is exact for every \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\bar x\in\{0,1\}^J\), \(\bar x\in X\iff\) exact separation returns no violated row for \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: coefficients and right-hand side of row r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implicit representation of set-system models with prohibitively many constraint rows.

source_refs.locator: 2.4.4 Set Covering on Graphs: Many Constraints p. 55

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A large-row set-system model has a finite but implicitly represented row family \(\mathcal R\) and feasible region \[X=\{x\in\{0,1\}^J:a_r^{\mathsf T}x\geq b_r\ \text{for every }r\in\mathcal R\}.\] A separation routine, given \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^J\), either returns a row \(r\in\mathcal R\) with \(a_r^{\mathsf T}\bar x<b_r\) or certifies that no such row exists. If the routine separates the entire row family exactly, the implicit and explicit row descriptions define the same feasible binary vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A large-row model represents its constraint rows implicitly and uses exact separation to test all row inequalities; on binary vectors this preserves the full feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Large-Row Set-System Models

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4.4 Set Covering on Graphs: Many Constraints p. 55

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided and complete feasibility evidence for an implicit row system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A returned row index \(r\), together with exactly encoded \((a_r,b_r)\), is a directly checkable nonmembership certificate whenever \(a_r^{\mathsf T}\bar x<b_r\). Conversely, absence of a returned violation certifies membership only relative to a trusted exact separator or an independently checkable certificate covering the entire implicit family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One violated row directly certifies infeasibility; absence of a violation certifies feasibility only through complete exact separation.
assumptions_latex: The returned row can be verified to belong to the implicit family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a_r^{\mathsf T}\bar x<b_r\Longrightarrow\bar x\notin X.
knowledge_statements.title: Violated-Row and No-Violation Oracle Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incomplete Separation Does Not Certify Full Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp oracle boundary for an implicit row family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a separation routine searches only a proper subfamily \(\mathcal R'\subsetneq\mathcal R\), returning no violated row certifies only the searched inequalities. It does not certify membership in the full feasible set unless the searched subfamily is known to imply every row in \(\mathcal R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure of a heuristic row search to find a violation is not a full-feasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal R'\) may omit a nonredundant row of \(\mathcal R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Sep}_{\mathcal R'}(\bar x)=\mathrm{none}\not\Longrightarrow\bar x\in X.

notation.meaning: row subfamily inspected by an incomplete separator

knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Separation Does Not Certify Full Feasibility

children.title: Large-Column Set-System Models
children.top_down_role: Set-system models with exceptionally many candidate sets or variables.

assumptions_latex: \(I\) is a finite row set and \(\mathcal S\subseteq 2^I\) is a finite, possibly implicitly represented, family of columns.
Each column \(S\in\mathcal S\) has cost \(c_S\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\{\sum_{S\in\mathcal S}c_Sx_S:\sum_{S\ni i}x_S\ge 1\ (i\in I),\ x_S\in\{0,1\}\ (S\in\mathcal S)\}\) is a large-column set-system model.

notation.meaning: Implicit family of admissible sets indexing columns.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite binary set covering with an implicitly represented column family.

source_refs.locator: 2.4.5 Set Covering with Many Variables: Crew Scheduling p. 57

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A large-column set-system model has a manageable row set \(I\) but a family \(\mathcal S\) too large to enumerate. Its binary covering form is \[\min\left\{\sum_{S\in\mathcal S}c_Sx_S:\sum_{S\in\mathcal S:i\in S}x_S\ge 1\ \text{for every }i\in I,\quad x_S\in\{0,1\}\ \text{for every }S\in\mathcal S\right\}.\] The family must admit an implicit description or an oracle capable of producing relevant columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A large-column model selects sets from an implicit family so that every ground element is covered, without explicitly enumerating all selection variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Large-Column Set-System Models

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4.5 Set Covering with Many Variables: Crew Scheduling p. 57

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Implicit Size Does Not Imply Tractable Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes compact implicit representation from computational accessibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A compact description of a finite exponentially large column family \(\mathcal S\) does not by itself yield a polynomial-time solution method. For row prices \(\pi\), reduced-cost optimization over all \(S\in\mathcal S\) may be NP-hard even when membership in \(\mathcal S\) is polynomial-time testable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact implicit column family can still have an NP-hard reduced-cost optimization problem.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal S\) is finite and implicitly represented.
Membership testing and optimization over \(\mathcal S\) are treated as distinct computational tasks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{compact encoding of }\mathcal S\not\Rightarrow\text{polynomial-time optimization over }\mathcal S.\)

notation.meaning: row-price vector used in reduced-cost optimization

knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Size Does Not Imply Tractable Pricing

children.title: Row-Generation Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for models whose constraint families are generated selectively.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Generation Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact row generation for a finite binary optimization model with a complete separation oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{x\in X_0:a_r^Tx\ge b_r\text{ for every }r\in\mathcal R\}\). Initialize \(\mathcal R_0\subseteq\mathcal R\). At iteration \(k\), solve \(\min\{d^Tx:x\in X_0,\ a_r^Tx\ge b_r\text{ for every }r\in\mathcal R_k\}\), obtaining \(x^k\). If separation returns \(r_k\in\mathcal R\) with \(a_{r_k}^Tx^k<b_{r_k}\), set \(\mathcal R_{k+1}=\mathcal R_k\cup\{r_k\}\) and repeat. Otherwise stop and output \(x^k\). With exact restricted solves, finite \(\mathcal R\), and complete separation, the output belongs to \(X\) and is optimal for \(\min\{d^Tx:x\in X\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve the binary model with the currently generated rows and add a violated row. With exact solves and complete separation over a finite row family, stopping yields an optimal solution of the full model.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal R\) is finite, and each \(r\in\mathcal R\) specifies \(a_r\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(b_r\in\mathbb R\).
Every restricted model is solved exactly, and a complete separation oracle either returns a violated row or certifies that none exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k\in X\) at termination, and \(x^k\) minimizes \(d^Tx\) over \(X\).

notation.meaning: Base binary feasible set before generated rows are imposed.
Complete finite family of row indices.
Exact restricted-model optimizer at iteration k.

source_refs.locator: 2.4.4 Set Covering on Graphs: Many Constraints p. 55

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4.4 Set Covering on Graphs: Many Constraints p. 55

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-solve and separation-call bound for finite exact row generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every nonterminal iteration adds at least one row in \(\mathcal R\setminus\mathcal R_k\), then \(N_{\mathrm{add}}\le |\mathcal R\setminus\mathcal R_0|\) and \(N_{\mathrm{solve}},N_{\mathrm{sep}}\le |\mathcal R\setminus\mathcal R_0|+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At most one row-adding iteration is charged to each initially absent row, followed by at most one terminal solve and separation test.
assumptions_latex: Every nonterminal iteration adds at least one previously absent row.
Each iteration performs one restricted solve and one complete separation call.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{add}}\le |\mathcal R\setminus\mathcal R_0|,\quad N_{\mathrm{solve}},N_{\mathrm{sep}}\le |\mathcal R\setminus\mathcal R_0|+1.

notation.meaning: Numbers of restricted solves and separation calls.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Row-Generation Iteration Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure Without Complete Separation or Exact Restricted Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp necessity of the two oracle assumptions in the finite row-generation stopping claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X_0=\{0,1\}\), the full row \(x\ge1\), and objective \(\min x\), a separator that falsely reports no violation at the restricted optimizer \(x=0\) permits infeasible termination. Separately, with \(X=X_0=\{0,1\}\), no rows, and objective \(\min x\), an inexact restricted solver may return \(x=1\); separation then correctly finds no violated row although \(x=1\) is not optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incomplete separation can certify an infeasible point, while an inexact restricted solve can terminate at a feasible but nonoptimal point.
assumptions_latex: The first instance permits an incomplete separator.
The second instance permits a nonoptimal restricted-solver output.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Neither termination feasibility nor termination optimality follows after the corresponding exactness assumption is removed.}
knowledge_statements.title: Failure Without Complete Separation or Exact Restricted Optimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective bounds produced by exact row generation for a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_k=\min\{d^Tx:x\in X_0,\ a_r^Tx\ge b_r\ (r\in\mathcal R_k)\}\) and \(z^*=\min\{d^Tx:x\in X\}\). If \(\mathcal R_k\subseteq\mathcal R_{k+1}\subseteq\mathcal R\), then \(z_k\le z_{k+1}\le z^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding full-model rows can only increase the restricted minimization optimum, which remains a lower bound on the full optimum.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the complete model.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Bound Monotonicity

children.title: Column-Generation Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for models whose variable families are generated selectively.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Generation Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column generation for a feasible, bounded minimization linear relaxation with a finite implicit column family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\mathcal S_0\subseteq\mathcal S\) for which the restricted master is feasible. At iteration \(k\), solve the restriction of \(P\) to \(\mathcal S_k\) and obtain optimal row-dual multipliers \(\pi^k\). Pricing computes \[S_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{S\in\mathcal S}\left\{\bar c_S=c_S-\sum_{i\in I}\pi_i^k a_{iS}\right\}.\] If \(\bar c_{S_k}<0\), set \(\mathcal S_{k+1}=\mathcal S_k\cup\{S_k\}\) and repeat. If \(\bar c_{S_k}\ge0\), the current restricted-master solution is optimal for \(P\). This certificate concerns the linear relaxation; binary optimality requires branching or another integrality mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve a restricted covering LP and add a globally priced negative-reduced-cost column. When every implicit column has nonnegative reduced cost, the current solution is optimal for the full LP, not necessarily for the binary model.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is a finite row set, \(\mathcal S\) is a finite implicit column family, \(a_{iS}\in\mathbb R\), \(b_i\in\mathbb R\), and \(c_S\in\mathbb R\).
The full relaxation is \(P=\min\{\sum_{S\in\mathcal S}c_Sx_S:\sum_{S\in\mathcal S}a_{iS}x_S\ge b_i\ (i\in I),\ x_S\ge0\ (S\in\mathcal S)\}\), and it is feasible with a finite optimum.
Every restricted master is solved exactly, and pricing globally minimizes reduced cost over \(\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(c_S-\sum_{i\in I}\pi_i^k a_{iS}\ge0\) for every \(S\in\mathcal S\), the current restricted-master solution is optimal for \(P\).

notation.meaning: Optimal covering-row dual multipliers at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incomplete Pricing Cannot Certify Master Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness boundary for heuristic or restricted pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Failure of a heuristic or restricted pricing routine to find a negative-reduced-cost column does not imply that all admissible columns have nonnegative reduced cost. The restricted-master solution is certified optimal for the full LP only when pricing supplies a valid global lower bound of at least zero on reduced cost over every admissible omitted column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure to find an improving column heuristically is not an optimality certificate; global pricing or a valid global bound is required.
assumptions_latex: The full admissible column family may strictly contain the family searched by the routine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{heuristic failure}\not\Rightarrow\min_{S\in\mathcal S}\bar c_S\ge0.\)

notation.meaning: reduced cost of admissible column S

knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Pricing Cannot Certify Master Optimality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination with Permanent Column Retention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-column termination of exact column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mathcal S\) is finite, every restricted master and pricing problem is solved exactly, and every negative-reduced-cost column returned by pricing is permanently retained, then each nonterminal iteration adds a previously absent column. Therefore column generation terminates after at most \(|\mathcal S\setminus\mathcal S_0|\) successful additions with an optimum of the full LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact column generation over a finite family terminates finitely when every improving column is retained.
assumptions_latex: The initial restricted master is feasible.
The full master has a finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{add}}\le |\mathcal S\setminus\mathcal S_0|\), and termination certifies full-LP optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Termination with Permanent Column Retention

children.title: Simultaneous Scale Regimes
children.top_down_role: Set-system regimes with both large constraint and variable families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact alternating or batched generation for the defined finite primal-dual LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve the restricted primal-dual pair on \((\mathcal R_k,\mathcal S_k)\). Add at least one absent row violated by \(x^k\) whenever one exists and at least one absent column with \(c_s-\sum_rA_{rs}y_r^k<0\) whenever one exists. Stop only when neither exists. If every encountered restricted pair has an attained finite optimum, then termination yields the joint certificate, with at most \(|\mathcal R\setminus\mathcal R_0|+|\mathcal S\setminus\mathcal S_0|\) nonterminal iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly refresh both separation and pricing, adding new offending indices; finiteness gives termination and the two simultaneous oracle tests certify the full LP.
assumptions_latex: Every encountered restricted primal-dual pair has an attained common finite optimum.
Separation and pricing are complete and exact.
Each nonterminal iteration adds at least one previously absent offending index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{nonterminal}}\le |\mathcal R\setminus\mathcal R_0|+|\mathcal S\setminus\mathcal S_0|\text{, and the terminal pair is full-LP optimal.}
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Joint Row-and-Column Generation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate for the full finite LP from an optimal restricted primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^k,y^k)\) be an optimal primal-dual pair for the restricted LP on \((\mathcal R_k,\mathcal S_k)\), extended by zero. If \(\sum_sA_{rs}x_s^k\ge b_r\) for every \(r\in\mathcal R\) and \(\bar c_s=c_s-\sum_rA_{rs}y_r^k\ge0\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\), then \(x^k\) and \(y^k\) are optimal for the full primal and dual LPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted optimum certifies the full LP only when it passes both complete row separation and complete column pricing.
assumptions_latex: The restricted primal and dual have an attained common finite optimum.
\(x^k\) and \(y^k\) are extended by zero outside \(\mathcal S_k\) and \(\mathcal R_k\).
Both full-family oracle tests are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^k\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}(P),\qquad y^k\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}(D).

notation.meaning: Reduced cost, equivalently slack of dual inequality s.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Row-Separation and Column-Pricing Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Either Oracle Test Alone Is Insufficient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite examples separating the row-feasibility and column-pricing requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{x:x\ge1,\ x\ge0\}\), a restricted model with its sole row omitted has solution \(x=0\) and passes nonnegative-cost pricing, but violates the missing row. Conversely, for \(\min\{x_1: x_1+x_2\ge1,\ x\ge0\}\), the restricted column set \(\{x_1\}\) gives \(x_1=1\) and dual value \(y=1\), which passes full-row separation, while the omitted zero-cost column \(x_2\) has reduced cost \(-1\) and improves the full optimum to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Passing pricing does not imply satisfaction of omitted rows, and passing separation does not rule out an improving omitted column.
assumptions_latex: The first restricted model omits the only row.
The second restricted model omits column \(x_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Neither full separation nor full pricing alone certifies full-LP optimality.}
knowledge_statements.title: Either Oracle Test Alone Is Insufficient

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full Primal-Dual Model for Simultaneous Implicit Rows and Columns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite covering-form LP whose row and column index families are both implicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite \(\mathcal R,\mathcal S\), define \((P)\) by \(\min\{\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}c_sx_s:\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}A_{rs}x_s\ge b_r\ (r\in\mathcal R),\ x\ge0\}\). Its dual \((D)\) is \(\max\{\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}b_ry_r:\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}A_{rs}y_r\le c_s\ (s\in\mathcal S),\ y\ge0\}\). A restricted pair uses \(\mathcal R_k\subseteq\mathcal R\) and \(\mathcal S_k\subseteq\mathcal S\), with absent primal and dual coordinates extended by zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The simultaneous regime is a finite primal-dual LP in which both primal rows and primal columns may be omitted from the current restricted pair.
assumptions_latex: All displayed coefficients are finite real numbers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (P)\text{ and }(D)\text{ provide a common model in which row separation tests primal feasibility and column pricing tests dual feasibility.}

notation.meaning: Coefficient of column s in row r.
Primal column variables and dual row variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Full Primal-Dual Model for Simultaneous Implicit Rows and Columns

assumptions_latex: Both the row family \(\mathcal R\) and column family \(\mathcal S\) are finite but may be implicit.
Restricted masters, row separation, and column pricing are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A restricted solution is certified for the full relaxation only after both full-row feasibility and nonnegative reduced costs over all columns hold.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize restricted families \(\mathcal R_0\subseteq\mathcal R\) and \(\mathcal S_0\subseteq\mathcal S\). At iteration \(k\), solve the restricted linear master, obtaining \((x^k,\pi^k)\). Apply full-row separation to \(x^k\) and full-column pricing to \(\pi^k\); add every selected violated row and negative-reduced-cost column, then repeat. Under the assumptions, the output is feasible and optimal for the full linear relaxation; this alone does not certify binary optimality.
