knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Monotone Relation Between Size and Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary constructions showing that formulation size alone neither determines nor guarantees projected strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from any formulation \(Q\), redundant inequalities or auxiliary variables fixed by equations can increase its displayed size without changing its projection. Conversely, adding a nonredundant valid inequality can increase displayed size while strictly shrinking the projected relaxation. Hence inequality count alone neither determines projected strength nor varies monotonically with it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A larger formulation can have the same projection because of redundancy, or a stronger projection because of added valid structure; size alone does not determine strength.
assumptions_latex: Formulations are compared after projection to a common original-variable space.
Displayed size counts explicit inequalities under a fixed convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s(Q_1)<s(Q_2)\text{ implies neither }\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_1)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_2)\text{ nor the reverse inclusion}.

notation.meaning: projected relaxation in the common variable space

knowledge_statements.title: No Monotone Relation Between Size and Strength

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-objective characterization of containment for nonempty compact convex projected relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_1,R_2\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty compact convex relaxations in a common variable space. Then \[R_1\subseteq R_2\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \min_{x\in R_1}c^\top x\ge \min_{x\in R_2}c^\top x\quad\text{for every }c\in\mathbb R^n.\] Thus failure of \(R_1\subseteq R_2\) is witnessed by a linear objective for which the asserted bound dominance fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For compact convex relaxations, containment is equivalent to providing at least as strong a minimization bound for every linear objective.
assumptions_latex: \(R_1,R_2\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) are nonempty compact convex sets.
Both sets are expressed in the same original-variable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_1\subseteq R_2\iff \left(\forall c\in\mathbb R^n,\ \min_{x\in R_1}c^\top x\ge\min_{x\in R_2}c^\top x\right).
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Characterization of Relaxation Strength

children.title: Minimal Cover Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Cover inequalities associated with inclusion-minimal infeasible selections.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonminimal Cover Inequalities Are Dominated by Minimal Subcovers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Redundancy of basic inequalities generated by nonminimal covers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every finite cover \(C\) contains an inclusion-minimal cover \(C'\subseteq C\). On \([0,1]^n\), the inequality \(x(C')\le |C'|-1\), together with \(x_i\le1\) for \(i\in C\setminus C'\), implies \(x(C)\le |C|-1\). Thus the basic inequality of a nonminimal cover is dominated by that of a minimal subcover relative to the binary-cube relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Removing redundant cover members yields a minimal subcover whose basic inequality is at least as strong.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a cover in a finite ground set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(C'\subseteq C\) is a minimal cover, then \(x(C')\le |C'|-1\) dominates \(x(C)\le |C|-1\) on \([0,1]^n\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nonminimal Cover Inequalities Are Dominated by Minimal Subcovers

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Facet of the Restricted Minimal-Cover Polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facet property on the coordinates of a nontrivial minimal cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a minimal cover with \(|C|\ge2\), and define \(P_C=\operatorname{conv}\{x_C\in\{0,1\}^{C}:\sum_{i\in C}a_ix_i\le b\}\). Then \(P_C=\{x_C\in[0,1]^C:x(C)\le |C|-1\}\), and \(x(C)\le |C|-1\) defines a facet of \(P_C\). The \(|C|\) points \(\mathbf1_C-e^i\), \(i\in C\), are feasible, tight, and affinely independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the coordinates of a nontrivial minimal cover, only the all-ones binary vector is excluded, and the cover inequality is facet-defining.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x(C)\le |C|-1\) is facet-defining for \(P_C\).

notation.meaning: convex hull of feasible binary assignments on the cover coordinates

review_flags: The nontriviality assumption excludes the zero-dimensional singleton-cover case.
knowledge_statements.title: Facet of the Restricted Minimal-Cover Polytope
Minimal Cover Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic valid inequality generated by an inclusion-minimal cover of a binary knapsack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(K=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le b\}\), where \(a_i>0\). A set \(C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is a minimal cover when \[\sum_{i\in C}a_i>b\quad\text{and}\quad \sum_{i\in C\setminus\{k\}}a_i\le b\ \text{ for every }\ k\in C.\] Its minimal-cover inequality is \[\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le |C|-1,\] which is valid for every \(x\in K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimal cover exceeds knapsack capacity but ceases to do so after deleting any member; at most all but one of its variables may equal one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le |C|-1\) for every \(x\in K\).

children.title: Extended Cover Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Cover inequalities strengthened through eligible extensions beyond a base cover.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Validity Test for a Unit-Coefficient Cover Extension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient validity condition for extending a cover inequality to a prescribed index set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:a^\top x\le b\}\) with \(a_i>0\), let \(C\) be a cover, and let \(E\supseteq C\). The inequality \(x(E)\le |C|-1\) is valid for \(K\) if and only if every \(S\subseteq E\) with \(|S|=|C|\) satisfies \(a(S)>b\). Equivalently, if \(a_{(1)}(E)\le\cdots\le a_{(|E|)}(E)\), validity is equivalent to \(\sum_{k=1}^{|C|}a_{(k)}(E)>b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unit-coefficient extension is valid exactly when its lightest cover-sized subset exceeds capacity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x(E)\le |C|-1\) is valid if and only if the \(|C|\) lightest weights in \(E\) sum to more than \(b\).

notation.meaning: kth-smallest weight among indices in E

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Validity Test for a Unit-Coefficient Cover Extension

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Threshold Extension Need Not Be Maximal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to necessity of the conventional heaviest-cover-item threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b=10\), let a two-item cover \(C\) have weights \(6,6\), and let an outside item have weight \(5\). The conventional threshold \(a_j\ge\max_{i\in C}a_i=6\) excludes the outside item, but extending to all three indices is valid because the two lightest extended weights sum to \(5+6=11>b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outside item lighter than every cover item can still validly receive unit coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conventional coefficient threshold is sufficient but not necessary for a valid unit-coefficient extension.
knowledge_statements.title: Threshold Extension Need Not Be Maximal
Extended Cover Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-threshold extension of a minimal-cover inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a minimal cover for \(K=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_i a_i x_i\le b\}\), with \(a_i>0\), and define \[E(C)=C\cup\{j\notin C:a_j\ge \max_{i\in C}a_i\}.\] Then the extended-cover inequality \[\sum_{j\in E(C)}x_j\le |C|-1\] is valid for \(K\). Indeed, any \(|C|\) selected indices from \(E(C)\) have total weight at least \(\sum_{i\in C}a_i>b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimal cover can be extended by variables at least as heavy as its heaviest member; at most one fewer than the original cover size may be selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j\in E(C)}x_j\le |C|-1\) is valid for \(K\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity Region for Lifted Cover Coefficients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasible region of nonnegative lifting vectors for a fixed cover inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), let \(C\) be a cover, and put \(J=N\setminus C\). A vector \(\alpha\in\mathbb R_+^J\) defines a valid inequality \(x(C)+\alpha^\top x_J\le |C|-1\) if and only if \(\alpha^\top x_J\le |C|-1-x(C)\) for every \(x\in K\), equivalently \(\max_{x\in K}\{x(C)+\alpha^\top x_J\}\le |C|-1\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid extension of a cover inequality by coefficients on variables outside the cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a cover for the binary knapsack set \(K\), and let \(J=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus C\). children.title: Cover-Inequality Strength Relations

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dominance Tests for Lifted Cover Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxation-relative comparison of lifted inequalities sharing a base cover and right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a cover \(C\), outside index set \(J\), and relaxation \(R\subseteq[0,1]^n\). For two valid liftings \(x(C)+\alpha^\top x_J\le |C|-1\) and \(x(C)+\gamma^\top x_J\le |C|-1\), \(\alpha\ge\gamma\) componentwise is sufficient for the \(\alpha\)-inequality to dominate the \(\gamma\)-inequality on \(R\). Dominance is strict exactly when dominance holds and some \(\bar x\in R\) satisfies the \(\gamma\)-inequality but violates the \(\alpha\)-inequality. The two cuts are incomparable exactly when each admits such a witness against the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficientwise larger lifting coefficients give a sufficient dominance relation; witness points determine strictness and incomparability on a fixed relaxation.
assumptions_latex: Both lifted inequalities are valid for the same integer-feasible set.
Both use the same base cover and right-hand side.
All comparisons use the same relaxation \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Componentwise coefficient order is sufficient for dominance, while strictness and incomparability require the stated relaxation witnesses.
knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Tests for Lifted Cover Inequalities
Cover-Inequality Strength Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance relations among basic, extended, and lifted cover inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a cover \(C\), the basic inequality is \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le |C|-1\). Any valid lifted inequality \[\sum_{i\in C}x_i+\sum_{j\notin C}\alpha_jx_j\le |C|-1\] with \(\alpha_j\ge0\) implies the basic inequality on \([0,1]^n\) and therefore dominates it. The threshold extended-cover inequality is the special lifted inequality with \(\alpha_j=1\) for \(j\in E(C)\setminus C\) and \(\alpha_j=0\) otherwise. A lifted inequality dominates that extended-cover inequality whenever \(\alpha_j\ge1\) on \(E(C)\setminus C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative lifting dominates the basic cover inequality. Threshold extension is a particular lifting, and any valid lifting with coefficients at least one on extended indices dominates it.
assumptions_latex: The compared lifted inequalities are valid for the underlying knapsack set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha\ge0\) yields dominance over the basic cover inequality; \(\alpha_j\ge1\) on \(E(C)\setminus C\) yields dominance over the extended-cover inequality.

Sequential Lifting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive exact up-lifting of binary variables in a prescribed order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\{0,1\}^{I\cup J}\), and suppose \(c^Tx_I\le\beta\) is valid on \(K\cap\{x_J=0\}\). Choose an order \(j_1,\ldots,j_q\) of \(J\). At step \(t\), set \[\alpha_{j_t}=\beta-\max\left\{c^Tx_I+\sum_{s<t}\alpha_{j_s}x_{j_s}:x\in K,\ x_{j_t}=1,\ x_{j_s}=0\text{ for }s>t\right\}.\] Assuming each maximization set is nonempty, append \(\alpha_{j_t}x_{j_t}\). After \(q\) steps, output \(c^Tx_I+\sum_{t=1}^q\alpha_{j_t}x_{j_t}\le\beta\), which is valid for \(K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sequence-Independent Lifting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order invariance of recursively computed lifting coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a binary set \(K\), a valid base inequality \(c^Tx_I\le\beta\) on \(K\cap\{x_J=0\}\), and a specified sequential lifting rule. The lifting is sequence-independent when there exists \(\bar\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^J\) such that, for every permutation \(\pi\) of \(J\), the rule terminates with \[c^Tx_I+\sum_{j\in J}\bar\alpha_jx_j\le\beta.\] Equality is coefficientwise for the labeled variables, not merely equality up to permuting the output vector.

Every permutation of \(J\) is admissible for the rule.

children.title: Lifting-Order Sensitivity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Order-Dependent Outputs Need Not Be Strength-Ordered
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength consequence of order-dependent labeled lifting coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix the binary set, base inequality, lifting rule, and reference relaxation \(R\). If two admissible orders produce valid inequalities \(p^\top x\le\beta\) and \(q^\top x\le\beta\), distinct coefficient vectors alone imply neither dominance nor incomparability. If there exist \(x^p,x^q\in R\) with \(p^\top x^p\le\beta<q^\top x^p\) and \(q^\top x^q\le\beta<p^\top x^q\), then the two order-dependent outputs are mutually incomparable on \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different lifting orders can yield distinct valid cuts, but strength ordering must be established by relaxation inclusion or witness points.
assumptions_latex: The binary set, base inequality, sequential lifting rule, and reference relaxation are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Opposing relaxation witnesses certify mutual incomparability of two order-dependent lifted inequalities.

Lifting-Order Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of sequential lifting coefficients on the variable permutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(K\), base inequality, and sequential lifting rule, let \(\alpha^{\pi}\) denote the labeled coefficient vector produced under permutation \(\pi\) of the lifted index set \(J\). The instance is lifting-order sensitive precisely when there exist permutations \(\pi\) and \(\sigma\) and an index \(j\in J\) such that \[\alpha_j^{\pi}\ne\alpha_j^{\sigma}.\] The resulting inequalities can both be valid even though their coefficient vectors differ; order sensitivity therefore concerns the recursive construction, not validity alone.

children.title: Order-Invariance Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Problem classes where sequence independence holds or breaks down.

knowledge_statements.title: Order-Invariance Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A commutation condition separating guaranteed order invariance from possible sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_j\) denote the deterministic operation that exactly lifts variable \(x_j\) into the current valid inequality. If, for every inequality reachable from the base inequality and every pair of remaining indices \(j,k\), \[T_j(T_k(g))=T_k(T_j(g)),\] with equality of all labeled coefficients, then every admissible lifting order produces the same final inequality. Thus pairwise commutation on the reachable family is a sufficient boundary for order invariance. If this commutation equality fails at a reachable inequality, sequence independence is no longer guaranteed and the two local orders may produce distinct coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise commutation of all reachable lifting steps guarantees order invariance. Once two reachable lifting operations fail to commute, order independence has no such guarantee.
assumptions_latex: Each \(T_j\) is deterministic and defined on every reachable inequality.
The lifted index set is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_jT_k=T_kT_j\) on all reachable inequalities implies invariance under every lifting permutation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine correspondence between covering-knapsack pack inequalities and packing-knapsack cover inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(a_i>0\), \(A=\sum_{i\in N}a_i\), and \(X=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_i a_i x_i\ge b\}\). If \(P\subseteq N\) satisfies \(a(P)<b\), then \[\sum_{i\notin P}x_i\ge1\] is valid for \(X\). Under the affine complementation \(z_i=1-x_i\), the row becomes \(\sum_i a_i z_i\le A-b\), the set \(C=N\setminus P\) satisfies \(a(C)>A-b\), and the pack inequality becomes \[\sum_{i\in C}z_i\le |C|-1.\]

otin P\), and the pack-to-cover interface produces the valid inequalities \[\sum_{i\in P}x_i+x_j\le |P|,\qquad j
otin P.\] These inequalities expose the same infeasible simultaneous selections as the corresponding cover inequalities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order structure of relative dominance among valid-inequality families on one relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(R\), define \(\mathcal F\succeq_R\mathcal G\) when \(R(\mathcal F)\subseteq R(\mathcal G)\). This relation is reflexive and transitive. Moreover, \(\mathcal F\succeq_R\mathcal G\) and \(\mathcal G\succeq_R\mathcal F\) exactly when \(R(\mathcal F)=R(\mathcal G)\). Consequently, dominance becomes a partial order after families inducing the same strengthened relaxation are identified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative family dominance is a preorder and becomes a partial order after identifying families with the same closure on the fixed relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Preorder and Equivalence Classes
Cross-Family Dominance Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance of cut families relative to a fixed relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a relaxation and let \(\mathcal F\) and \(\mathcal G\) be families of inequalities valid for the same integer set. Write \(R(\mathcal H)=R\cap\bigcap_{h\in\mathcal H}\{x:h(x)\le0\}\). Family \(\mathcal F\) dominates \(\mathcal G\) relative to \(R\) precisely when \[R(\mathcal F)\subseteq R(\mathcal G).\] Dominance is strict when the inclusion is proper. The families are equivalent on \(R\) when both inclusions hold, and incomparable when neither inclusion holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One inequality family dominates another when adding the first to a fixed relaxation leaves a subset of the points left by the second.
assumptions_latex: All inequalities in \(\mathcal F\cup\mathcal G\) are defined on \(R\) and valid for the same integer set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F\) dominates \(\mathcal G\) on \(R\) if and only if \(R(\mathcal F)\subseteq R(\mathcal G)\).

notation.meaning: relaxation obtained after imposing family \(\mathcal H\)

children.title: Cover Recognition
children.top_down_role: Structural identification of cover configurations within binary constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear-Time Recognition of a Given Cover and Minimal Cover
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition of one specified subset for a positive-coefficient binary knapsack row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(C\subseteq N\), \(C\ne\varnothing\), and \(s=\sum_{i\in C}a_i\). For \(a_i>0\), \(C\) is a cover exactly when \(s>b\), and it is a minimal cover exactly when \(s>b\) and \(s-\min_{i\in C}a_i\le b\). Computing the sum and minimum in one scan uses \(O(|C|)\) arithmetic operations and \(O(1)\) auxiliary space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single scan computing the total and smallest member weight recognizes a supplied cover and its minimality.
assumptions_latex: Arithmetic additions and comparisons have unit cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is a minimal cover if and only if \(s>b\) and \(s-\min_{i\in C}a_i\le b\).

notation.meaning: total weight of the supplied subset

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Time Recognition of a Given Cover and Minimal Cover

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary under which an overweight subset yields an unconditional cover inequality for the full row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:a^\top x\le b\}\), nonnegative coefficients ensure that \(a(C)>b\) makes simultaneous selection of every member of \(C\) infeasible, so \(x(C)\le |C|-1\) is valid. A zero-coefficient item cannot belong to a minimal cover. If a coefficient outside \(C\) is negative, selecting that outside item may offset \(a(C)>b\); consequently the overweight-subset test alone need not imply the cover inequality unless the negative contribution is excluded or otherwise bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard unconditional cover inference requires a nonnegative packing row; negative outside coefficients can restore feasibility.
assumptions_latex: Variables are binary and otherwise unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The implication \(a(C)>b\Rightarrow x(C)\le |C|-1\) is guaranteed by coefficient nonnegativity but can fail with negative outside coefficients.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Sign Boundary for Cover Recognition
Cover Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition predicate for covers of one binary knapsack row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the knapsack set \(X=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le b\}\), with \(a_i>0\), a subset \(C\subseteq N\) is a cover exactly when \[\sum_{i\in C}a_i>b.\] It is a minimal cover exactly when it is a cover and \[\sum_{i\in C\setminus\{j\}}a_i\le b\qquad\text{for every }j\in C.\] Recognition therefore consists of evaluating these sums; a recognized cover certifies validity of \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le |C|-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set is a cover when its total weight exceeds capacity, and is minimal when deleting any member restores capacity feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is a cover if and only if \(a(C)>b\), and it is minimal under the displayed deletion tests.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cover and minimal-cover tests are standard, but no supporting source is supplied and N is not explicitly defined.

children.title: Cover Separation
children.top_down_role: Search regimes for violated cover inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Cover Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact separation of unlifted cover inequalities by minimum-cost cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and let \(\bar x\in[0,1]^n\). Solve \[\theta^*=\min\left\{\sum_{i\in N}(1-\bar x_i)z_i:\sum_{i\in N}a_i z_i>b,\ z\in\{0,1\}^n\right\}.\] If this problem is infeasible or \(\theta^*\ge 1\), no unlifted cover inequality is violated by \(\bar x\). Otherwise, let \(z^*\) be an optimizer, set \(C^*=\{i\in N:z_i^*=1\}\), and output the violated inequality \[\sum_{i\in C^*}x_i\le |C^*|-1.\] Its violation condition is \(\sum_{i\in C^*}(1-\bar x_i)<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize costs equal to one minus the fractional values over all covers. An optimum below one identifies a violated unlifted cover inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A violated unlifted cover inequality exists if and only if the separation problem is feasible and \(\theta^*<1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Knapsack Complexity of Exact Cover Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity of exact unlifted-cover separation for integral packing weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), exact separation of unlifted cover inequalities is a minimum-cost covering-knapsack problem and is weakly NP-hard. With \(A=\sum_i a_i\) and \(c_i=1-\bar x_i\), a dynamic program storing the minimum subset cost for each attainable weight \(w\in\{0,\ldots,A\}\) computes \(\min\{c^\top z:a^\top z>b,\ z\in\{0,1\}^n\}\) in \(O(nA)\) time and \(O(A)\) space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact unlifted-cover separation is weakly NP-hard but pseudo-polynomially solvable for integral weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact separation is weakly NP-hard and admits an \(O(nA)\)-time, \(O(A)\)-space dynamic program.
knowledge_statements.title: Knapsack Complexity of Exact Cover Separation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restricted Search Cannot Certify Global Nonviolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate boundary between exact separation and restricted or heuristic cover searches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal C\) be the covers examined by a restricted search. The inequality \(\min_{C\in\mathcal H}\sum_{i\in C}(1-\bar x_i)\ge1\) certifies only that no member of \(\mathcal H\) is violated. It certifies absence of every violated unlifted cover inequality only if \(\mathcal H=\mathcal C\) or an independent exactness argument proves that \(\mathcal H\) contains a global minimum-cost cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A failed restricted or greedy search is not a global nonviolation certificate without an exactness guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) is the full cover family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Family-wide nonviolation requires exhaustive or otherwise exact optimization over \(\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Search Cannot Certify Global Nonviolation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Separation algorithm for lifted cover inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Searches for a violated lifted cover inequality, using a remove-and-lift-back fallback when direct lifting finds none.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x^*\) and a cover \(C\), first apply the lifting heuristic and stop if it finds a violated inequality. Otherwise choose \(k\in\arg\max_{j\in C}a_jx_j^*\), set \(C_2=\{k\}\), and use \(C\setminus\{k\}\) to generate a facet-defining inequality for \(\operatorname{conv}(S^k)\), where \(S^k=\{x\in\{0,1\}^{n-1}:\sum_{j\in N\setminus\{k\}}a_jx_j\le b-a_k\}\). Lift \(x_k\) back to obtain a facet-defining inequality of form (2.3) for \(S\), then test it for violation at \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The procedure first tries direct cover lifting. If that finds no violated inequality, it removes the cover variable with largest weighted value at the target point, constructs a facet inequality for the residual knapsack set, lifts the removed variable back, and tests the result for violation.
assumptions_latex: x^*\text{ is the point to be separated}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure returns a violated lifted cover inequality if either tested construction is violated; otherwise it terminates without one.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sequential Up-Lifting of a Cover Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact stagewise computation of maximal coefficients for variables initially fixed to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(j_1,\ldots,j_m\) order \(N\setminus C\). Initially impose \(x_{j_1}=\cdots=x_{j_m}=0\) and use \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le |C|-1\). At stage \(k\), assuming the subproblem is nonempty, set \[\alpha_{j_k}=|C|-1-\max\left\{\sum_{i\in C}x_i+\sum_{\ell<k}\alpha_{j_\ell}x_{j_\ell}:x\in X,\ x_{j_k}=1,\ x_{j_\ell}=0\ (\ell>k)\right\}.\] Free \(x_{j_k}\) and continue. The final inequality \[\sum_{i\in C}x_i+\sum_{k=1}^m\alpha_{j_k}x_{j_k}\le |C|-1\] is valid for \(X\), and each \(\alpha_{j_k}\) is the largest coefficient preserving validity conditional on the earlier coefficients and the current lifting order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential lifting frees outside variables one at a time and obtains each maximal conditional coefficient from an exact knapsack optimization subproblem.
assumptions_latex: Every stage subproblem with \(x_{j_k}=1\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{i\in C}x_i+\sum_{k=1}^m\alpha_{j_k}x_{j_k}\le |C|-1\text{ is valid for }X.

notation.meaning: maximal coefficient conditional on earlier stages

review_flags: empty_stage_requires_separate convention because no finite largest coefficient exists
knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Up-Lifting of a Cover Inequality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite subproblem count and knapsack structure of exact coefficient computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Sequential lifting processes each of the \(m=|N\setminus C|\) outside variables once and therefore solves exactly \(m\) coefficient-optimization subproblems. Each stage is a binary knapsack optimization problem with some variables fixed. For integral nonnegative weights and integral capacity, it admits the standard pseudo-polynomial dynamic-programming treatment; polynomial running time in the binary input length does not follow merely from the number of stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential cover lifting solves one binary-knapsack optimization problem per outside variable; integral data permit pseudo-polynomial dynamic programming, not an automatic polynomial bit-complexity bound.
assumptions_latex: There are \(m\) variables outside the cover.
The pseudo-polynomial statement assumes integral weights and capacity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The algorithm uses }m\text{ exact knapsack subproblems and is finite; its bit complexity depends on how those subproblems are solved.}

notation.meaning: number of variables outside the cover

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Order Dependence of Sequential Cover Lifting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit knapsack showing incomparable lifted inequalities from two variable orders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(X=\{x\in\{0,1\}^6:4x_1+4x_2+4x_3+4x_4+6x_5+3x_6\le13\}\) and \(C=\{1,2,3,4\}\). The base inequality is \(x_1+x_2+x_3+x_4\le3\). Lifting \(x_5\) before \(x_6\) yields coefficients \((\alpha_5,\alpha_6)=(2,0)\), whereas lifting \(x_6\) before \(x_5\) yields \((\alpha_5,\alpha_6)=(1,1)\). Thus the valid inequalities \[\sum_{i=1}^4x_i+2x_5\le3\quad\text{and}\quad\sum_{i=1}^4x_i+x_5+x_6\le3\] are order dependent and coefficientwise incomparable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A six-variable knapsack produces coefficients (2,0) or (1,1) under two lifting orders, so sequential lifting is order dependent and neither result dominates the other coefficientwise.
assumptions_latex: The displayed six-variable binary knapsack set is used.
Sequential coefficients are computed by exact up-lifting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha^{(5,6)}=(2,0)\ne(1,1)=\alpha^{(6,5)},\text{ and the two lifted inequalities are incomparable.}

notation.meaning: coefficient vectors under the two lifting orders

knowledge_statements.title: Order Dependence of Sequential Cover Lifting

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cover inequality strengthened by coefficients on variables outside the cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_i a_i x_i\le b\}\) with \(a_i\ge0\), and let \(C\) satisfy \(\sum_{i\in C}a_i>b\). A lifted cover inequality has the form \[\sum_{i\in C}x_i+\sum_{j\notin C}\alpha_jx_j\le |C|-1,\] with coefficients \(\alpha_j\) chosen so that the inequality is valid for \(X\). Setting every \(\alpha_j=0\) recovers the basic cover inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted cover inequality validly adds coefficients for variables outside a knapsack cover while retaining the cover right-hand side.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a binary packing-knapsack set with nonnegative weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{i\in C}x_i+\sum_{j\notin C}\alpha_jx_j\le |C|-1\text{ is a lifted cover inequality when it is valid for }X.

notation.meaning: lifting coefficient for an outside variable

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Cover Inequality
Cover Lifting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential lifting of a binary knapsack cover inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a cover and start from \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le |C|-1\). For an ordering \(j_1,\ldots,j_m\) of \(N\setminus C\), define successively \[\alpha_{j_k}=|C|-1-\max\left\{\sum_{i\in C}x_i+\sum_{\ell<k}\alpha_{j_\ell}x_{j_\ell}:x\in X,\ x_{j_k}=1\right\}.\] After all variables are processed, output \[\sum_{i\in C}x_i+\sum_{k=1}^m\alpha_{j_k}x_{j_k}\le |C|-1.\] Each coefficient is the largest value preserving validity given the previously lifted coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential lifting adds outside variables one at a time, choosing each largest coefficient that preserves validity over the knapsack set.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a cover, and each lifting subproblem has a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The final sequentially lifted cover inequality is valid for \(X\).

notation.meaning: lifting order for variables outside the cover

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sequential lifting heuristic for a cover inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructs a lifted cover inequality with \(C_2=\varnothing\), prioritizing coefficients by their contribution at a target point \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x^*\), obtain a cover \(C\), set \(L^1=N\setminus C\), and set \(\alpha_i=1\) for \(i\in C\). At iteration \(k\), for each \(j\in L^k\), compute the largest \(\beta_j\) for which \(\beta_jx_j+\sum_{i\in N\setminus L^k}\alpha_ix_i\le |C|-1\) is valid. Choose \(j^*\in\arg\max_{j\in L^k}\beta_jx_j^*\), set \(\alpha_{j^*}=\beta_{j^*}\), and remove \(j^*\) from \(L^k\). After all variables have been lifted, add \(\sum_{j\in N}\alpha_jx_j\le |C|-1\) if it is violated by \(x^*\). The coefficient satisfies \(\beta_j=|C|-1-\zeta_j\), where \(\zeta_j=\max\{\sum_{i\in N\setminus L^k}\alpha_ix_i:\sum_{i\in N\setminus L^k}a_ix_i\le b-a_j,\ x\in\{0,1\}^{|N\setminus L^k|}\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a cover, the heuristic lifts one outside variable at a time. It computes the largest valid coefficient for each candidate, selects one with maximum contribution at the target point, and adds the completed valid inequality only when the target point violates it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{j\in N}\alpha_jx_j\le |C|-1\text{ is valid and is added when }\sum_{j\in N}\alpha_jx_j^*>|C|-1

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sequential lifting of a cover inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computes maximal sequential lifting coefficients in a fixed ordering by solving residual-capacity binary knapsack problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a cover and let \(j_1,\ldots,j_r\) order \(N\setminus C\). At step \(t\), after fixing \(\alpha_{j_1},\ldots,\alpha_{j_{t-1}}\), compute \[\zeta_t=\max\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{t-1}\alpha_{j_i}x_{j_i}+\sum_{j\in C}x_j:\sum_{i=1}^{t-1}a_{j_i}x_{j_i}+\sum_{j\in C}a_jx_j\le b-a_{j_t},\ x\in\{0,1\}^{|C|+t-1}\right\}\] and set \(\alpha_{j_t}=|C|-1-\zeta_t\). This is the largest coefficient preserving validity at that step. Repeating for \(t=1,\ldots,r\) yields a valid lifted cover inequality \[\sum_{j\in C}x_j+\sum_{j\in N\setminus C}\alpha_jx_j\le |C|-1.\] If \(C\) is minimal and \(a_j\le b\) for every \(j\in N\), the resulting inequality is facet-defining for \(\operatorname{conv}(X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order the variables outside the cover and lift them sequentially. At each step, solve a residual-capacity knapsack problem and subtract its optimum from the cover bound to obtain the largest valid coefficient for that step. Under minimal-cover and item-capacity assumptions, the resulting inequality defines a facet.
assumptions_latex: C\text{ is minimal and }a_j\le b\ \forall j\in N\text{ for the facet conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha_{j_t}=|C|-1-\zeta_t\text{ is maximal at step }t;\text{ the completed lifted inequality is valid for }X;\text{ under the additional assumptions it is facet-defining for }\operatorname{conv}(X)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coefficient restrictions for facet-defining lifted cover inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Individual lifted-coefficient restrictions for a minimal cover of a binary knapsack set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K:=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_{j=1}^na_jx_j\le b\}\), where \(b\ge a_j>0\) for all \(j\), and let \(C\) be a minimal cover. After relabeling, suppose \(C=\{1,\ldots,t\}\) and \(a_1\ge\cdots\ge a_t\). Define \(\mu_0:=0\), \(\mu_h:=\sum_{\ell=1}^ha_\ell\), and \(\lambda:=\mu_t-b>0\). If \[\sum_{j\in C}x_j+\sum_{j\in N\setminus C}\alpha_jx_j\le |C|-1\] is a facet-defining lifting, then for every \(j\in N\setminus C\): if \(\mu_h\le a_j\le\mu_{h+1}-\lambda\) for some \(h\), then \(\alpha_j=h\); and if \(\mu_{h+1}-\lambda<a_j<\mu_{h+1}\) for some \(h\), then \(h\le\alpha_j\le h+1\). Moreover, in the latter case there exists a facet-defining lifting of this form with \(\alpha_j=h+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a facet-defining lifting of a minimal-cover inequality, the weight of each outside variable restricts its coefficient through intervals determined by the ordered cover weights and the cover excess. Some intervals force the coefficient to h; transition intervals permit values between h and h+1, with the upper value attainable in some facet-defining lifting.
assumptions_latex: \sum_{j\in C}x_j+\sum_{j\notin C}\alpha_jx_j\le|C|-1\text{ defines a facet of }\operatorname{conv}(K)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mu_h\le a_j\le\mu_{h+1}-\lambda\Rightarrow\alpha_j=h;\quad \mu_{h+1}-\lambda<a_j<\mu_{h+1}\Rightarrow h\le\alpha_j\le h+1,\text{ and some facet-defining lifting attains }\alpha_j=h+1.

children.title: Recognition-to-Separation Interface
children.top_down_role: How recognized cover structure supports separation and subsequent strengthening.

knowledge_statements.title: Recognition-to-Separation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted cover recognition as the optimization core of separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\bar x\in[0,1]^n\), assign item cost \(c_i=1-\bar x_i\). The recognized covers are exactly the incidence vectors in \(\mathcal C=\{z\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_i a_i z_i>b\}\). Consequently, separation of unlifted cover inequalities is represented by \[\min_{z\in\mathcal C}c^\top z.\] A cover inequality is violated at \(\bar x\) if and only if this minimum is less than \(1\); an optimal recognized cover supplies the separating inequality. Thus recognition becomes separation by attaching point-dependent costs and optimizing over recognized objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cover separation is weighted cover recognition: optimize point-dependent costs over all recognized covers and test whether the minimum is below one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A violated cover inequality exists if and only if \(\min_{z\in\mathcal C}(1-\bar x)^\top z<1\).

children.title: Conflict-Graph Representations
children.top_down_role: Graph representations of pairwise incompatibility in binary set systems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of pairwise conflict graphs to encode higher-order infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{x\in\{0,1\}^3:x_1+x_2+x_3\le2\}\). Every pair of variables can simultaneously equal one, so the conflict graph of \(X\) has no edges. Nevertheless, \((1,1,1)\notin X\). Thus the stable sets of the conflict graph strictly contain the feasible supports of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cardinality-at-most-two system on three variables has an empty conflict graph even though selecting all three variables is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E=\varnothing\) but \(X\subsetneq\{0,1\}^3\).

notation.meaning: edge set of the conflict graph of X

knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Order Conflict Loss
Conflict-Graph Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph representation of pairwise-incompatible binary assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\). Its conflict graph is \(G=(N,E)\), where \(\{i,j\}\in E\) exactly when no \(x\in X\) satisfies \(x_i=x_j=1\). Every feasible support \(S(x)=\{i:x_i=1\}\) is therefore a stable set of \(G\), so \[X\subseteq\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:x_i+x_j\le1\ \text{for every }\{i,j\}\in E\}.\] The graph records all certified pairwise conflicts, although higher-order infeasibilities need not be represented by edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vertices represent binary selections and edges represent pairs that cannot both equal one; every feasible support is a graph stable set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in X\), its support is stable in \(G\), and every edge inequality is valid.
review_flags: The supplied graph-theory locator does not specifically certify conflict-graph modeling.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pairwise-conflict representation is coherent and appropriately notes its higher-order limitation, but no supporting conflict-graph locator is supplied and N is not explicitly introduced.

children.title: Clique Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Strengthening derived from mutually incompatible vertex sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique inequalities strengthen collections of pairwise conflict inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(N,E)\) be a conflict graph for \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\). If \(Q\subseteq N\) is a clique, every two distinct vertices in \(Q\) conflict, so at most one associated variable can equal one. Hence \[\sum_{i\in Q}x_i\le1\] is valid for \(X\). For \(|Q|\ge3\), this inequality is generally stronger over \([0,1]^n\) than imposing only the edge inequalities \(x_i+x_j\le1\) for \(i,j\in Q\), since the all-one-half vector satisfies every edge inequality but violates the clique inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All variables indexed by a conflict-graph clique are mutually exclusive, so their sum is at most one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i\in Q}x_i\le1\) is valid for \(X\).
review_flags: Standard clique strengthening lacks a supplied polyhedral source locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clique inequality and strengthening comparison are mathematically standard, but the record has no inspectable polyhedral source locator.

children.title: Odd-Cycle Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Strengthening associated with odd cycles in conflict structures.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct validity and strict edge-relaxation strengthening for the exact vertex set of a simple odd cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(N,E)\) be a conflict graph for \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^N\), and let \(C\subseteq N\) be exactly the vertex set of a simple cycle of length \(2k+1\), where \(k\ge1\). Then every feasible support meets \(C\) in at most \(k\) vertices, so \[\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le k\] is valid for \(X\). The vector with \(x_i=\tfrac12\) for \(i\in C\) satisfies every edge inequality of that cycle but violates this inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The vertices of a simple odd conflict cycle have stability number at most half their number rounded down, and the resulting inequality cuts off the all-one-half cycle point.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is exactly the vertex set of a simple cycle of length \(2k+1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le k=\lfloor |C|/2\rfloor\) is valid for \(X\).

notation.meaning: exact vertex set of the specified simple odd cycle
one half of the cycle length rounded down

Odd-Cycle Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Odd-cycle inequality for stable supports in a conflict graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(N,E)\) be a conflict graph for \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), and let \(C\) be the vertex set of a simple odd cycle of length \(2k+1\), where \(k\ge1\). Any stable set contains at most \(k\) cycle vertices; therefore \[\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le k=\left\lfloor\frac{|C|}{2}\right\rfloor\] is valid for \(X\). The inequality strengthens the cycle's edge relaxation because assigning \(x_i=1/2\) on every cycle vertex satisfies all cycle-edge inequalities but violates the displayed bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stable set selects at most half, rounded down, of the vertices of an odd conflict cycle.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) induces or contains a simple cycle of odd length \(2k+1\).

children.title: Graph-to-Inequality Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Links between conflict-graph substructures and polyhedral inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Graph-to-Inequality Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stable-set inequalities transferred from a conflict graph to a binary model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(N,E)\) be a conflict graph for \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), so every feasible support is stable. If \(\alpha^\top z\le\beta\) is valid for every stable-set incidence vector \(z\in\{0,1\}^n\) of \(G\), then \[\alpha^\top x\le\beta\] is valid for every \(x\in X\). Thus any valid inequality for the stable-set polytope \(\operatorname{STAB}(G)\) transfers to the original binary model. The converse need not hold because the conflict graph retains pairwise conflicts but may omit higher-order constraints defining \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every valid stable-set inequality of a conflict graph transfers to the original binary feasible set, but the graph may omit higher-order restrictions.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible support of \(X\) is a stable set of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\subseteq\operatorname{STAB}(G)\) implies \(\alpha^\top x\le\beta\) for every \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: convex hull of stable-set incidence vectors of \(G\)

children.title: Packing Lifting
children.top_down_role: Lifting structures specialized to set-packing polyhedra.

assumptions_latex: \sum_{i\in S}a_i x_i\le b\text{ is valid for }X
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{i\in S}a_i x_i+\sum_{t=1}^k\alpha_{j_t}x_{j_t}\le b\quad\forall x\in X
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential lifting of a valid inequality for a downward-closed binary packing set.

source_refs.locator: 2.4.2 Strengthening Set Packing Formulations p. 52

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be downward closed, let \(S\subseteq[n]\), and let \(a\in\mathbb{R}^S\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}\) be such that \(\sum_{i\in S}a_i x_i\le b\) is valid for \(X\). Order \([n]\setminus S\) as \(j_1,\ldots,j_k\). At step \(t\), set \[\alpha_{j_t}=b-\max\left\{\sum_{i\in S}a_i x_i+\sum_{s<t}\alpha_{j_s}x_{j_s}:x\in X,\ x_{j_t}=1\right\},\] assuming the maximization set is nonempty. After the final step, output \(\sum_{i\in S}a_i x_i+\sum_{t=1}^k\alpha_{j_t}x_{j_t}\le b\). Each intermediate and final inequality is valid for \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a valid inequality on a downward-closed binary packing set, sequentially maximize the current left-hand side with each new variable fixed to one. The residual slack defines that variable's lifting coefficient, and every intermediate and final lifted inequality is valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Packing Lifting

children.title: Rank Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Inequalities derived from rank restrictions on packing substructures.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{i\in S}x_i\le r_X(S)\quad\forall x\in X
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank inequalities for restrictions of a binary packing set.

source_refs.locator: 2.4.2 Strengthening Set Packing Formulations p. 52

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(\varnothing\ne X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be a binary packing set, and let \(S\subseteq[n]\). Define its packing rank by \[r_X(S)=\max\left\{\sum_{i\in S}x_i:x\in X\right\}.\] The rank inequality induced by \(S\) is \[\sum_{i\in S}x_i\le r_X(S).\] It is valid for \(X\), and \(r_X(S)\) is the smallest integer right-hand side for which the unit-coefficient inequality supported on \(S\) is valid for \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty binary packing set, the rank of a subset is the largest number of its elements selected by a feasible packing. The associated rank inequality bounds every feasible packing by this value, which is the smallest valid integer right-hand side for unit coefficients on that subset.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank Inequalities

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank Constraints for the Vertex-Packing Polytope

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a graph \(G\), every \(x\in VP(G)\), and every \(U\subseteq V(G)\), the inequality \(x(U)\le \alpha(G[U])\) is valid. These inequalities are called rank constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every vertex subset U, a vertex-packing vector has total value over U at most the stability number of the induced subgraph G[U]; these inequalities are called rank constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x(U)\le \alpha(G[U])

children.title: Lifted Rank Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Interactions between lifting mechanisms and rank-based inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Rank Strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and dominance of nonnegative liftings of a rank inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be downward closed, let \(S\subseteq[n]\), and let \(r=r_X(S)\). If coefficients \(\alpha_j\ge0\) for \(j\notin S\) are obtained by valid sequential packing lifting, then \[\sum_{i\in S}x_i+\sum_{j\notin S}\alpha_jx_j\le r\] is valid for \(X\). On \([0,1]^n\), this inequality implies the original rank inequality \(\sum_{i\in S}x_i\le r\); hence it dominates that inequality, and the dominance can be strict when some lifted coefficient is positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative lifting adds outside variables to a rank inequality without changing its right side, preserving validity and producing a constraint at least as strong.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{i\in S}x_i+\sum_{j\notin S}\alpha_jx_j\le r

children.title: Covering Polyhedra

knowledge_statements.title: Covering Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative polyhedra defined by covering inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a matrix \(A\in\mathbb{R}_+^{m\times n}\), the covering polyhedron associated with \(A\) is \[Q(A)=\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:Ax\ge\mathbf{1}\right\}.\] Thus every row \(a_i^\top\) imposes \(a_i^\top x\ge1\). The polyhedron is upward closed: if \(x\in Q(A)\) and \(z\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\), then \(x+z\in Q(A)\). When \(A\) is a binary incidence matrix, its binary points represent covers of the indexed set system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A covering polyhedron contains nonnegative vectors that cover every row of a nonnegative matrix to level one and is closed under coordinatewise increases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q(A)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:Ax\ge\mathbf{1}\},\qquad Q(A)+\mathbb{R}_+^n=Q(A)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact nonemptiness condition and recession cone for a finite nonnegative unit-demand covering system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}_+^{m\times n}\) and \(Q(A)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:Ax\ge\mathbf 1\}\). Then \(Q(A)\neq\varnothing\) if and only if no row of \(A\) is identically zero. Whenever \(Q(A)\neq\varnothing\), \[\operatorname{rec}(Q(A))=\mathbb{R}_+^n.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite nonnegative unit-demand covering system is feasible exactly when every row has a positive coefficient; its recession cone is the nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(A)\neq\varnothing\iff A\text{ has no zero row}\), and then \(\operatorname{rec}(Q(A))=\mathbb{R}_+^n\).

children.title: Blocking Polyhedra
children.top_down_role: Blocking structures associated with upward-closed set systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Blocking Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex blocking sets in the nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonempty set \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^n\) is a blocking polyhedron if it is a polyhedron and is upward closed, equivalently \[P+\mathbb{R}_+^n=P.\] Its blocker is \[B(P)=\left\{y\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:y^\top x\ge1\text{ for every }x\in P\right\}.\] The blocker is itself closed, convex, and upward closed. Covering polyhedra \(Q(A)=\{x\ge0:Ax\ge\mathbf{1}\}\) are basic examples of blocking polyhedra whenever they are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A blocking polyhedron is a nonempty polyhedron in the nonnegative orthant that remains feasible after any coordinatewise increase; its blocker collects all normalized valid covering inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\text{ is blocking}\iff P+\mathbb{R}_+^n=P

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integrality and Min–Max Equivalence for Blocking Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equates integrality of the associated blocking polyhedra with two symmetric min–max identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the polyhedra Q and Q_B associated with a clutter \mathcal F, the following are equivalent:
\[
Q\text{ is integral};\qquad Q_B\text{ is integral};
\]
\[
(\forall w\in\mathbb R_+^n)\quad
\max\left\{\sum_{F\in\mathcal F}y_F:\sum_{F\in\mathcal F}y_Fx^F\leq w,\ y\in\mathbb R_+^{|\mathcal F|}\right\}
=\min_{H\in B(\mathcal F)}a^Hw;
\]
and
\[
(\forall w\in\mathbb R_+^n)\quad
\max\left\{\sum_{H\in B(\mathcal F)}y_H:\sum_{H\in B(\mathcal F)}y_Ha^H\leq w,\ y\in\mathbb R_+^{|B(\mathcal F)|}\right\}
=\min_{F\in\mathcal F}x^Fw.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the blocking polyhedra associated with a clutter, integrality of Q, integrality of Q_B, and each of the two symmetric min–max identities for every nonnegative weight vector are equivalent.
assumptions_latex: Q,Q_B,x^F,a^H\text{ are the section-defined associated objects}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reciprocal equivalence between universal min–max identities induced by two nonnegative row families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\in\mathbb R_+^{m\times n}\) have rows \(c_1^\top,\ldots,c_m^\top\), and let \(D\in\mathbb R_+^{t\times n}\) have rows \(d_1^\top,\ldots,d_t^\top\). Then \[\forall w\in\mathbb R_+^n:\quad \min_{1\le i\le m}w^\top c_i=\max\{\mathbf1^\top y:y\in\mathbb R_+^t,\ D^\top y\le w\}\] if and only if \[\forall w\in\mathbb R_+^n:\quad \min_{1\le j\le t}w^\top d_j=\max\{\mathbf1^\top y:y\in\mathbb R_+^m,\ C^\top y\le w\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonnegative matrices C and D, the universal identity equating the minimum weighted row of C with a packing maximum over D holds if and only if the symmetric identity obtained by exchanging C and D holds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lehman's length–width characterization of blocking pairs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes blocking pairs by cross-validity and a universal length–width inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P,R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be polyhedra of blocking type. They form a blocking pair if and only if both conditions hold: (i) \(z^\top x\ge1\) for every \(x\in P\) and \(z\in R\); and (ii) for every \(\ell,w\in\mathbb R_+^n\), \[\min_{x\in P}\ell^\top x\;\min_{z\in R}w^\top z\le \ell^\top w.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two blocking-type polyhedra form a blocking pair exactly when every cross inner product is at least one and, for every pair of nonnegative weight vectors, the product of their respective minimum weighted values is at most the inner product of the weights.
assumptions_latex: P,R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ are polyhedra of blocking type}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R=B(P)\iff\left[\forall x\in P,\forall z\in R,\ z^\top x\ge1\right]\land\left[\forall \ell,w\in\mathbb R_+^n,\ \min_{x\in P}\ell^\top x\cdot\min_{z\in R}w^\top z\le\ell^\top w\right].

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure under blocking, blocker involution, membership recovery, and the generator–inequality correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a polyhedron of blocking type. Then \(B(P)\) is of blocking type, \(B(B(P))=P\), and \(x\in P\) if and only if \(x\ge0\) and \(z^\top x\ge1\) for every \(z\in B(P)\). Moreover, for \(c_1,\ldots,c_m\in\mathbb R_+^n\), \(P=\{c_1,\ldots,c_m\}^{\dagger}\) if and only if \(B(P)=\{z\in\mathbb R_+^n:z^\top c_i\ge1\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The blocker of a blocking-type polyhedron is again blocking type, and taking the blocker twice recovers the original polyhedron. Membership is characterized by all blocker inequalities, while a finite dominant representation corresponds to an inequality representation of the blocker.
assumptions_latex: P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is a polyhedron of blocking type}
c_1,\ldots,c_m\in\mathbb R_+^n\text{ for the finite-representation assertion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B(P)\text{ is of blocking type},\quad B(B(P))=P,\quad x\in P\iff\bigl(x\ge0\land \forall z\in B(P),\ z^\top x\ge1\bigr),\quad P=\{c_1,\ldots,c_m\}^{\dagger}\iff B(P)=\{z\ge0:z^\top c_i\ge1\ \forall i\}.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficientwise dominance among normalized inequalities on the nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a,b\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\). On \(\mathbb{R}_+^n\), the normalized covering inequality \(a^\top x\ge1\) dominates \(b^\top x\ge1\) whenever \(a\le b\) componentwise, because \(a^\top x\le b^\top x\) for every \(x\ge0\). Dually, the packing inequality \(b^\top x\le1\) dominates \(a^\top x\le1\). Consequently, minimal coefficient vectors are the potentially essential normalized covering inequalities of a blocking polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For covering inequalities over nonnegative variables, smaller coefficients give the stronger normalized constraint; the direction reverses for packing inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x\ge0:a^\top x\ge1\}\subseteq\{x\ge0:b^\top x\ge1\}

knowledge_statements.title: Redundancy Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas-type redundancy criterion for a normalized nonnegative covering system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a^1,\ldots,a^m,b\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\), and assume \(P=\{x\ge0:(a^i)^\top x\ge1,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) is nonempty. The inequality \(b^\top x\ge1\) is valid for, and hence redundant in a description of, \(P\) if and only if there exists \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\) such that \[\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i a^i\le b\qquad\text{and}\qquad\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\ge1.\] Equivalently, some convex combination of the existing coefficient vectors is componentwise no larger than \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized covering row is redundant exactly when it componentwise dominates a convex combination of existing normalized rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b^\top x\ge1\text{ is valid for }P\iff\exists\lambda\ge0:\ \sum_i\lambda_i a^i\le b,\ \sum_i\lambda_i\ge1

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), and let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^n\) be a nonempty blocking polyhedron such that \(0\notin P\). Define \(B(P)=\{y\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:y^\top x\ge1\text{ for every }x\in P\}\). Then \(B(P)\) is a nonempty blocking polyhedron and \[B(B(P))=P.\] Moreover, membership has the symmetric characterization \[x\in P\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y^\top x\ge1\text{ for every }y\in B(P).\] Thus the points of the blocker are precisely the normalized nonnegative valid covering inequalities that recover \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty blocking polyhedron that does not contain the origin, its blocker is nonempty and taking the blocker twice recovers the original polyhedron. Blocker points encode exactly its normalized nonnegative valid covering inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Covering–Blocking Duality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order reversal of the blocker on proper nonempty blocking polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P,Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^n\) be nonempty blocking polyhedra with \(0\notin P\cup Q\). If \(P\subseteq Q\), then \[B(Q)\subseteq B(P).\] Together with blocker involution, the blocker is an inclusion-reversing involution on proper nonempty blocking polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking blockers reverses containment and is an involution on proper nonempty blocking polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B(Q)\subseteq B(P)\) and \(B(B(P))=P\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of normalized blocker involution when a blocking polyhedron contains the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a nonempty blocking set \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^n\) contains \(0\), then upward closure gives \(P=\mathbb{R}_+^n\). Its normalized blocker is empty because no \(y\ge0\) satisfies \(y^\top0\ge1\). Hence the condition \(0\notin P\) is necessary for nonempty normalized blocker involution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A blocking set containing the origin is the entire nonnegative orthant and has an empty normalized blocker.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\mathbb{R}_+^n\) and \(B(P)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Origin Degeneracy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Covering Rows and Their Blocking Hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact blocker correspondence between a finite normalized covering system and the blocking hull of its rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a^1,\ldots,a^m\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\setminus\{0\}\), let \(A\) have rows \((a^i)^\top\), and set \[R=\operatorname{conv}\{a^1,\ldots,a^m\}+\mathbb{R}_+^n.\] Then \[B(R)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:Ax\ge\mathbf 1\}=Q(A),\qquad B(Q(A))=R.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized covering system and the blocking hull of its coefficient rows are mutual blockers.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the blocker of a clutter as its clutter of inclusion-minimal transversals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \mathcal F be a clutter. Its blocking clutter is

B(\mathcal F)=\left\{H:\ (\forall F\in\mathcal F)\ H\cap F\neq\varnothing,\quad (\forall H'\subsetneq H)(\exists F\in\mathcal F)\ H'\cap F=\varnothing\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The blocking clutter of F consists of the sets that intersect every member of F and are inclusion-minimal among sets having this property.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\in B(\mathcal F)\iff \bigl[(\forall F\in\mathcal F)\ H\cap F\neq\varnothing\bigr]\land\bigl[(\forall H'\subsetneq H)(\exists F\in\mathcal F)\ H'\cap F=\varnothing\bigr].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subset Characterization of Blocking Clutter Pairs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes a pair of blocking clutters by an exclusive alternative for every subset of their common ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \mathcal F and \mathcal H be clutters on N. They are a pair of blocking clutters if and only if, for every T\subseteq N, exactly one of the following holds:
\[
(\exists F\in\mathcal F)\ F\subseteq T,
\qquad
(\exists H\in\mathcal H)\ H\subseteq N\setminus T.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clutters F and H form a blocking pair exactly when every subset T either contains a member of F or has a complement containing a member of H, but not both.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal F\text{ and }\mathcal H\text{ are clutters on the common ground set }N
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal F\text{ and }\mathcal H\text{ are a blocking pair}\iff (\forall T\subseteq N)\left[((\exists F\in\mathcal F)\ F\subseteq T)\mathbin{\oplus}((\exists H\in\mathcal H)\ H\subseteq N\setminus T)\right].

knowledge_statements.title: Partitioning Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex hull of binary exact covers of a set-system incidence matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a binary matrix \(A\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\), the set-partitioning polytope is \[P_{=}(A)=\operatorname{conv}\left\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:Ax=\mathbf{1}\right\}.\] Its binary points select columns so that every row is covered exactly once. The linear set-partitioning relaxation is \(R_{=}(A)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:Ax=\mathbf{1}\}\), and always \(P_{=}(A)\subseteq R_{=}(A)\). Equality holds precisely when the relaxation has no fractional points outside the binary convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The set-partitioning polytope is the convex hull of binary column selections that cover every row exactly once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{=}(A)=\operatorname{conv}\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:Ax=\mathbf{1}\}\subseteq\{x\ge0:Ax=\mathbf{1}\}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient matrix condition under which the natural set-partitioning relaxation equals the binary hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\) be totally unimodular and suppose every column contains a one. Since \(\mathbf 1\) is integral, every vertex of \(R_{=}(A)=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:Ax=\mathbf1\}\) is integral. The nonzero-column assumption also gives \(x_j\le1\) for every \(j\), so every vertex is binary and \(R_{=}(A)=P_{=}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a totally unimodular incidence matrix without zero columns, the natural exact-cover relaxation is integral and equals the set-partitioning polytope.
knowledge_statements.title: Total-Unimodularity Integrality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundedness boundary for the natural nonnegative relaxation, contrasted with the always-bounded binary hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(R_{=}(A)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(R_{=}(A)\) is bounded if and only if every column of \(A\) contains a one. A zero column gives the recession ray \(e_j\), whereas a nonzero column gives \(x_j\le1\) throughout the relaxation. Since \(P_{=}(A)\subseteq[0,1]^n\), a zero column implies \(P_{=}(A)\ne R_{=}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The natural relaxation is bounded exactly when there are no zero columns; the binary partitioning hull is always bounded.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Column Boundedness Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Balanced-matrix specialization of integrality for the exact-cover face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A\) is balanced, the set-packing polytope \(\{x\ge0:Ax\le\mathbf1\}\) is integral. The set \(R_{=}(A)=\{x\ge0:Ax=\mathbf1\}\) is a face of that polytope and is therefore integral. If every column is nonzero, its integral points are binary, and hence \(R_{=}(A)=P_{=}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a balanced incidence matrix without zero columns, the exact-cover equality face is integral and equals the binary partitioning hull.
knowledge_statements.title: Balanced-Matrix Integrality

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\), and for each \(j\in[n]\) define the indexed column support \(S_j=\{i\in[m]:A_{ij}=1\}\). A vector \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) satisfies \(Ax=\mathbf{1}\) if and only if the indexed family \(\bigl((j,S_j):x_j=1\bigr)\) has pairwise disjoint supports and their union is \([m]\). Consequently, binary feasible points are in one-to-one correspondence with indexed exact covers of \([m]\) by columns of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible binary partitioning vector selects an indexed family of columns whose supports are pairwise disjoint and cover every row. Retaining column indices makes this correspondence one-to-one even when distinct columns have identical supports.
knowledge_statements.title: Partitioning Column Structure

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Deciding whether }\exists x\in\{0,1\}^n:Ax=\mathbf 1\text{ is }\mathcal{NP}\text{-complete}.

children.title: Degenerate Column Regimes
children.top_down_role: Repeated, dominated, or structurally indistinguishable columns affecting polyhedral quality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes columns that occur in no binary exact cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a column \(j\), let \(A^{(j)}\) be the residual matrix obtained after selecting \(j\). Then \[F_j=\{x\in P_{=}(A):x_j=1\}\ne\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\{y\in\{0,1\}^{n'}:A^{(j)}y=\mathbf1\}\ne\varnothing.\] If the residual instance is infeasible, then \(x_j=0\) throughout \(P_{=}(A)\), and deleting column \(j\) leaves the projection onto the remaining coordinates unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A column belongs to a feasible exact cover exactly when its residual exact-cover instance is feasible. Otherwise its selected-column face is empty and the column is fixed to zero in the binary hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_j\ne\varnothing\iff A^{(j)}y=\mathbf1\text{ has a binary solution}

notation.meaning: residual exact-cover matrix after selecting column j

knowledge_statements.title: Unusable-Column Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates zero-column behavior in the continuous equality relaxation from behavior in the binary partitioning hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_{\cdot j}=0\). If \(Q(A)=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:Ax=\mathbf1\}\) is nonempty, then \(e_j\in\operatorname{rec}(Q(A))\), so \(Q(A)\) is unbounded. In contrast, for \(P_{=}(A)=\operatorname{conv}\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:Ax=\mathbf1\}\), deletion of column \(j\) gives \[P_{=}(A)=P_{=}(A_{-j})\times[0,1]\] under the natural coordinate identification, provided the reduced exact-cover set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero column creates a recession direction in the nonnegative continuous equality relaxation, but in the binary hull it creates a free binary coordinate and hence a product with an interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e_j\in\operatorname{rec}(Q(A))\quad\text{and}\quad P_{=}(A)\cong P_{=}(A_{-j})\times[0,1]

notation.meaning: matrix obtained by deleting column j

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Column Ambient-Space Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes the geometry of two indexed partitioning columns with the same nonempty support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_{\cdot j}=A_{\cdot k}\ne0\) with \(j\ne k\). Coordinate transposition \(x_j\leftrightarrow x_k\) is an automorphism of \(P_{=}(A)\). Moreover, \(x_j+x_k\le1\) is valid, and the faces \(F_j=\{x\in P_{=}(A):x_j=1\}\) and \(F_k=\{x\in P_{=}(A):x_k=1\}\) are carried onto one another by that automorphism. They are symmetric coordinate faces, not necessarily the same subset of the indexed coordinate space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicate nonzero columns are interchangeable under a coordinate-swap symmetry. Their selected-column faces are isomorphic but remain distinct indexed faces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{=}(A)\text{ is invariant under }x_j\leftrightarrow x_k,\quad x_j+x_k\le1,\quad F_j\cong F_k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers zero and duplicate columns, the principal degeneracies affecting column-face correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^n:Ax=\mathbf 1\}\), a zero column \(A_{\cdot j}=0\) creates the recession ray \(x+te_j\in P\) for every \(x\in P\) and \(t\ge 0\). If two columns coincide, \(A_{\cdot j}=A_{\cdot k}\), then replacing \((x_j,x_k)\) by any nonnegative pair having the same sum preserves feasibility. Consequently, a zero column destroys boundedness, whereas duplicate columns make the column representation nonunique and can prevent distinct columns from corresponding to distinct geometric faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero partitioning column creates an unbounded coordinate ray; duplicate columns create interchangeable coefficients, so distinct columns need not determine distinct faces.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty rational polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formulation-independent rank-one closure for a rational pure-integer polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(c\in\mathbb Z^n\) for which \(h_P(c)=\max\{c^Tx:x\in P\}\) is finite, the Chvatal-Gomory inequality is \(c^Tx\le\lfloor h_P(c)\rfloor\). The rank-one closure is \[P^{\mathrm{CG}}=P\cap\bigcap_{\substack{c\in\mathbb Z^n\\h_P(c)<+\infty}}\{x:c^Tx\le\lfloor h_P(c)\rfloor\}.\] This equals the closure obtained by all nonnegative row aggregations having integral left-hand side and is independent of a particular inequality description of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The CG closure imposes, in every integral direction, the strongest valid support bound rounded down to the integer lattice.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support-Function Form of the Chvátal-Gomory Closure
knowledge_statements.title: Support-Function Form of the Chvátal-Gomory Closure

assumptions_latex: All coordinates use the pure-integer convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^{\mathrm{CG}}\) is a rational polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a rational polyhedron, then \(P^{\mathrm{CG}}\) is a rational polyhedron. Hence finitely many Chvatal-Gomory inequalities suffice to describe the rank-one closure together with a finite description of \(P\), despite the definition ranging over infinitely many integral directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The rank-one CG closure of a rational polyhedron is itself a rational polyhedron.

Each \(L_i(P)\) is obtainable by lifting the two disjunctive terms into separate multiplier variables and projecting the resulting linear system back to \(x\)-space. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e_0,e_1,\ldots,e_n\) be the coordinate vectors of \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\). The Lovasz-Schrijver set \(N(P)\) consists of those \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) for which a symmetric matrix \(Y\in\mathbb S^{n+1}\) exists with \(Ye_0=\operatorname{diag}(Y)=(1,x)\) and \(Ye_i,Y(e_0-e_i)\in K(P)\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Define \(N^0(P)=P\) and \(N^{q+1}(P)=N(N^q(P))\) for every integer \(q\ge0\). Then, for every \(r\in\{0,1,\ldots,n\}\), \[P_I\subseteq N^n(P)\subseteq N^r(P)\subseteq P,\qquad N^n(P)=P_I.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex-body N-plus operator and recursive hierarchy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extends the positive-semidefinite Lovász–Schrijver operator to convex bodies in the pure binary setting. This extension is needed because N-plus need not be polyhedral, so the earlier polyhedral presentation cannot directly be iterated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K\subseteq[0,1]^n be a convex body, let S:=K\cap\{0,1\}^n, and define \widetilde K:=\{\lambda(1,x)^T:x\in K,\ \lambda\ge0\}. Let M_+(K) consist of all Y\in\mathbb{R}^{(n+1)\times(n+1)} such that Y\succeq0, y_{00}=1, y_{0j}=y_{j0}=y_{jj} for j=1,\ldots,n, and Ye^j,\,Ye^0-Ye^j\in\widetilde K for j=1,\ldots,n. Define N_+(K):=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:(1,x)^T=Ye^0\text{ for some }Y\in M_+(K)\}. Then S\subseteq N_+(K). If K is a polytope, this definition agrees with the earlier Lov\'asz--Schrijver N_+ operator. Define its iterates by N_+^1:=N_+(K) and N_+^t:=N_+(N_+^{t-1}) for every integer t\ge2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex body in the binary cube, N-plus is obtained by projecting positive-semidefinite matrices whose relevant columns and complementary columns lie in the body's homogenization cone. It contains all binary points of the body, agrees with the earlier construction on polytopes, and its convex-body formulation permits recursive iteration even when N-plus is not polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_+(K)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:(1,x)^T=Ye^0\text{ for some }Y\in M_+(K)\},\qquad S\subseteq N_+(K),\qquad N_+^1=N_+(K),\qquad N_+^t=N_+(N_+^{t-1})\ \text{for }t\ge2.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One application of the positive-semidefinite Lovász–Schrijver operator to a mixed zero-one linear set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^{n+p}:Ax\ge b\} include 0\le x_j\le1 for j=1,\ldots,n, and let S=P\cap(\{0,1\}^n\times\mathbb R_+^p). Multiply Ax-b\ge0 by x_j and 1-x_j for every j\le n, linearize the products using x_j^2=x_j, and impose Y\succeq0 on the lifted binary moment matrix. If M_+(P) is the resulting lifted convex set and N_+(P)=\operatorname{proj}_x M_+(P), then S\subseteq N_+(P) and S=\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,y)\in M_+(P):\operatorname{rank}(Y)=1\}. Hence N_+(P) is obtained by relaxing the rank-one condition. Linear optimization over N_+(P) is representable as a semidefinite program and can be performed to arbitrary precision in polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiply every defining inequality by each binary variable and its complement, linearize the products, impose positive semidefiniteness on the binary moment matrix, and project back to the original variables. The resulting Lovász–Schrijver set contains the mixed zero-one feasible set. Its rank-one lifted points project exactly onto that feasible set; waiving rank one gives an SDP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\subseteq N_+(P),\qquad S=\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,y)\in M_+(P):\operatorname{rank}(Y)=1\}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial size of a Boolean-quotient Lasserre level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After Boolean reduction, a Gram basis through degree \(r\) contains \[s_{\rm B}(n,r)=\sum_{k=0}^{\min(r,n)}\binom nk\] squarefree monomials. The principal Gram matrix has this order, and degree-shifted constraint multipliers use no larger bases. Thus, for fixed \(r\) and a polynomially encoded bounded-degree constraint list, the level has polynomial combinatorial size in \(n\). When \(r\) grows with \(n\), the basis can approach all \(2^n\) squarefree monomials, so finite convergence does not imply a polynomial-size terminal SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boolean reduction leaves the squarefree degree-at-most-r basis; fixed levels are polynomial-size, but terminal levels can require exponentially many monomials.
