children.title: Clique-Web Facet Families
children.top_down_role: Related facet classes based on clique-web combinatorics.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Web Facet Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orbit-based description pending selection of a specific clique-web parameter convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a clique-web parameter tuple \(\theta\) and its seed inequality \(a^\theta x\le\beta_\theta\) in cut coordinates. Its clique-web family is the orbit \[\mathcal F_\theta=\{(a^\theta P)x\le\beta_\theta:P\text{ is induced by an admissible vertex permutation or cut switching}\}.\] If the seed supports a facet of the relevant cut polytope, every member of \(\mathcal F_\theta\) supports a facet because these transformations are affine automorphisms. Through the standard affine correspondence between cut and Boolean-quadric coordinates, the orbit gives an equivalent binary-quadratic facet family. The precise seed coefficients and admissible parameter restrictions depend on the selected clique-web convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clique-web family is the symmetry orbit of a parameterized seed facet; affine cut–binary transformations preserve its facet status.
assumptions_latex: A specific clique-web seed and admissible parameter tuple \(\theta\) have been fixed.
The stated permutations and switchings act as polytope automorphisms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every inequality in \(\mathcal F_\theta\) is facet-defining whenever the seed inequality is facet-defining.

notation.meaning: Parameters selecting a clique-web seed inequality.
Symmetry orbit of the selected seed inequality.
Coordinate action induced by an admissible symmetry.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This gives a generic symmetry-orbit representation rather than a clique-web inequality, its admissible parameters, and its facet conditions. An authoritative clique-web source is needed before the mathematical record and its exact knowledge kind can be determined.

children.title: Facet-Family Dominance Relations
children.top_down_role: Containment, implication, and incomparability across major facet families.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Witness Certificates for Strict Dominance and Incomparability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Point certificates for failed reverse containment between two explicitly specified family closures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R(\mathcal F)\) and \(R(\mathcal G)\) use common coordinates and the same base relaxation. A point \(x\in R(\mathcal G)\setminus R(\mathcal F)\), together with an inequality of \(\mathcal F\) violated by \(x\), certifies \(R(\mathcal G)\nsubseteq R(\mathcal F)\). If \(R(\mathcal F)\subseteq R(\mathcal G)\) is independently established, it certifies strict dominance by \(\mathcal F\). Witnesses in both set differences certify incomparability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point admitted by one family closure but cut off by the other certifies failed containment; witnesses in both directions certify incomparability.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal F\text{ and }\mathcal G\text{ use common coordinates and one fixed base relaxation }R
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in R(\mathcal G)\setminus R(\mathcal F)\Rightarrow R(\mathcal G)\nsubseteq R(\mathcal F)
knowledge_statements.title: Witness Certificates for Strict Dominance and Incomparability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order structure induced by complete inequality families over one fixed base relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(R\), and write \(\mathcal F\succeq_R\mathcal G\) when \(R(\mathcal F)\subseteq R(\mathcal G)\). Then \(\succeq_R\) is reflexive and transitive. With \(\mathcal F\sim_R\mathcal G\) defined by \(R(\mathcal F)=R(\mathcal G)\), dominance induces a partial order on the equivalence classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Family dominance is a preorder and becomes a partial order after closure-equivalent families are identified.
assumptions_latex: R(\mathcal F),R(\mathcal G),R(\mathcal H)\text{ use common coordinates and the same base relaxation }R
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \succeq_R\text{ is a preorder, and its quotient by }\sim_R\text{ is a partial order}
knowledge_statements.title: Preorder and Closure-Equivalence Quotient

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary closure laws for valid-inequality families over one fixed base relaxation in common coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a base relaxation \(R\), and define \(R(\mathcal F)=R\cap\bigcap_{(a,\beta)\in\mathcal F}\{x:a^\top x\le\beta\}\). Then \[R(\mathcal F\cup\mathcal G)=R(\mathcal F)\cap R(\mathcal G).\] Consequently, \(\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F\) implies \(R(\mathcal F)\subseteq R(\mathcal G)\). The converse need not hold, and strict family inclusion need not give strict dominance because added inequalities can be redundant over \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A union of valid-inequality families produces the intersection of their strengthened relaxations. Family inclusion suffices for dominance but is neither necessary nor sufficient for strict dominance.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal F\text{ and }\mathcal G\text{ are valid-inequality families in the coordinates of }R
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R(\mathcal F\cup\mathcal G)=R(\mathcal F)\cap R(\mathcal G),\qquad \mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F\Rightarrow R(\mathcal F)\subseteq R(\mathcal G)

notation.meaning: Base relaxation strengthened by every inequality in family F

knowledge_statements.title: Family Inclusion and Union Laws

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of family dominance on the common base relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R'\subseteq R\) be base relaxations in common coordinates. If \(R(\mathcal F)\subseteq R(\mathcal G)\), then \(R'(\mathcal F)\subseteq R'(\mathcal G)\). Enlargement need not preserve dominance: with \(P=R=\{0\}\), \(\mathcal F=\{x\le1\}\), and \(\mathcal G=\{x\le0\}\), the closures over \(R\) coincide, whereas over \(\widetilde R=[0,1]\), \(\widetilde R(\mathcal F)=[0,1]\not\subseteq\{0\}=\widetilde R(\mathcal G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dominance persists when the common base is tightened but may disappear when it is enlarged.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal F\text{ and }\mathcal G\text{ are valid for the same }P\subseteq R'
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R(\mathcal F)\subseteq R(\mathcal G)\Longrightarrow R'(\mathcal F)\subseteq R'(\mathcal G)

notation.meaning: Closure generated by family F relative to the tighter base.

knowledge_statements.title: Base-Relaxation Monotonicity and Enlargement Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-optimization test for explicitly represented finite inequality families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(R(\mathcal F)\) has a finite rational linear description and \(\mathcal G\) is finite and rationally encoded. If \(R(\mathcal F)=\varnothing\), then \(R(\mathcal F)\subseteq R(\mathcal G)\) vacuously. Otherwise, for each \((a,\beta)\in\mathcal G\), solve \(\sup\{a^\top x:x\in R(\mathcal F)\}\). The containment holds exactly when every supremum is at most \(\beta\). A finite optimizer exceeding \(\beta\), or a point obtained along an unbounded improving ray, witnesses failure of dominance. Thus explicit finite-family dominance is decidable using feasibility plus at most \(|\mathcal G|\) rational linear programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dominance of finite rational families can be tested by checking every target inequality over the source closure; a violated test yields a counterexample point.
assumptions_latex: \(R(\mathcal F)\) has a finite rational linear description.
\(\mathcal G\) is finite and rationally encoded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R(\mathcal F)\subseteq R(\mathcal G)\iff \sup_{x\in R(\mathcal F)}a^\top x\le\beta\quad\forall(a,\beta)\in\mathcal G.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Polyhedral Dominance Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent implication characterization over a fixed base relaxation in common coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Using the convention \(\sup\varnothing=-\infty\), \[R(\mathcal F)\subseteq R(\mathcal G)\iff \sup_{x\in R(\mathcal F)}a^\top x\le\beta\quad\text{for every }(a,\beta)\in\mathcal G.\] Thus \(\mathcal F\) dominates \(\mathcal G\) exactly when every inequality in \(\mathcal G\) is valid on the relaxation strengthened by \(\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One family dominates another exactly when all inequalities of the second are valid on the closure generated by the first.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\) and \(\mathcal G\) use common coordinates and the same base relaxation \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R(\mathcal F)\subseteq R(\mathcal G)\iff\forall(a,\beta)\in\mathcal G:\ \sup_{x\in R(\mathcal F)}a^\top x\le\beta.
knowledge_statements.title: Inequalitywise Characterization of Family Dominance
Facet-Family Dominance Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance between families of valid inequalities for a fixed relaxation space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and let \(R\supseteq P\) be a common base relaxation. For a family \(\mathcal F\) of inequalities valid for \(P\), define \[R(\mathcal F)=R\cap\bigcap_{(a,\beta)\in\mathcal F}\{x\in\mathbb R^d:a^\top x\le\beta\}.\] A family \(\mathcal F\) dominates a family \(\mathcal G\) relative to \(R\) when \(R(\mathcal F)\subseteq R(\mathcal G)\). Dominance is strict when this inclusion is proper, and the families are relaxation-equivalent when equality holds. These relations compare the complete closures, so they are invariant under positive rescaling, duplication, and symmetry-equivalent rewriting of individual inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One facet family dominates another when adding the first to the same base relaxation yields a contained, hence at least as strong, relaxation.
assumptions_latex: Every inequality in \(\mathcal F\cup\mathcal G\) is valid for \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F\) dominates \(\mathcal G\) exactly when \(R(\mathcal F)\subseteq R(\mathcal G)\).

notation.meaning: Base relaxation strengthened by every inequality in family F.
Families of valid inequalities in common coordinates.

children.title: Complementation Views
children.top_down_role: Roof-dual representations obtained through variable complementation.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is a quadratic pseudo-Boolean function with each \(q_{ij}\) indexed once for \(i<j\).
\(S\subseteq[n]\) is the set of variables to complement.
Any transported roof-dual formulation relabels every occurrence of the corresponding literal coordinates consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(d+sz)=f'(z)\quad\text{for every }z\in\{0,1\}^n,

notation.meaning: offset and sign of the complementation substitution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coefficient action and representation covariance under binary variable complementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=c+\sum_i a_i x_i+\sum_{i<j}q_{ij}x_ix_j\). Set \(x_i=d_i+s_i z_i\), with \((d_i,s_i)=(1,-1)\) for \(i\in S\) and \((0,1)\) otherwise. Then \(q'_{ij}=q_{ij}s_is_j\), \(a'_i=s_i\bigl(a_i+\sum_{j<i}q_{ji}d_j+\sum_{j>i}q_{ij}d_j\bigr)\), and \(c'=c+\sum_i a_id_i+\sum_{i<j}q_{ij}d_id_j\). This Boolean bijection preserves every objective value and transports optimizers bijectively. A literal-coordinate roof relaxation is transported by the same relabeling when all occurrences of complemented literals are changed consistently. The coefficient update takes \(O(n+m)\) time for \(m\) stored interactions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementing any subset of binary variables gives an explicit affine coefficient transformation that preserves all objective values and optimizers; consistently relabeled literal formulations represent the same relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Complementation Coefficient Action
Complementation Views
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable complementation as an exact symmetry of quadratic pseudo-Boolean optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=c+\sum_i a_i x_i+\sum_{i<j}q_{ij}x_ix_j\) on \(\{0,1\}^n\). Choose \(S\subseteq[n]\), and set \(x_i=d_i+s_i z_i\), where \((d_i,s_i)=(1,-1)\) for \(i\in S\) and \((d_i,s_i)=(0,1)\) otherwise. Then \(f(x)=f'(z)\), where \[q'_{ij}=q_{ij}s_is_j,\qquad a'_i=s_i\left(a_i+\sum_{j<i}q_{ji}d_j+\sum_{j>i}q_{ij}d_j\right),\qquad c'=c+\sum_i a_id_i+\sum_{i<j}q_{ij}d_id_j.\] The map is a Boolean bijection, preserves objective values and optima, and transports a roof-dual relaxation consistently when its corresponding literal coordinates are complemented.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementing selected binary variables gives an exact coefficient transformation that preserves objective values and optima; correspondingly complemented literal coordinates give the equivalent roof-dual view.

\(S\subseteq[n]\) is the set of complemented variables.

children.title: Majorization Views

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boolean Agreement Does Not Characterize a Roof-Dual Extension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of Boolean-point agreement alone to identify or control a roof-dual extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=[0,1]\), \(f(0)=f(1)=0\), and \(r_M(x)=-4Mx(1-x)\) for \(M>0\). Then \(r_M(0)=f(0)\) and \(r_M(1)=f(1)\), whereas \(\min_{x\in Q}r_M(x)=-M\). Thus agreement on Boolean points neither characterizes a roof-dual extension nor controls the resulting relaxation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boolean-preserving extensions can have arbitrarily poor continuous minima, so Boolean agreement alone does not define the roof-dual majorization view.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_M|_{\{0,1\}}=f\quad\text{and}\quad\min_{x\in Q}r_M(x)=-M.

notation.meaning: Family of continuous extensions with the same Boolean trace.

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Agreement Does Not Characterize a Roof-Dual Extension
Majorization Views
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound orientation of roof-dual envelopes under minimization and maximization conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R\), and let \(Q\subseteq[0,1]^n\) contain every Boolean point. A roof-dual lower envelope for minimization is a function \(r:Q\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(r(x)=f(x)\) on \(\{0,1\}^n\) and yielding \[\min_{x\in Q}r(x)\le \,\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}f(x).\] Equivalently, \(-r\) is a majorizing relaxation for maximizing \(-f\), since \[\max_{x\in Q}(-r(x))\ge \,\max_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}(-f(x)).\] Thus descriptions of roof duality as majorization or minorization differ by objective sign and optimization direction, not by the resulting bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A roof-dual lower envelope for minimization becomes a majorizing upper relaxation after negating the objective; the two views encode the same bound.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation agrees with \(f\) at Boolean points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_Q r\le\min_{\{0,1\}^n}f\), equivalently \(\max_Q(-r)\ge\max_{\{0,1\}^n}(-f)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two optimization inequalities follow from domain inclusion and sign reversal, but equality with f on Boolean points alone does not identify r as a roof-dual envelope. A roof-duality source must establish the intended envelope construction and the convention-dependent use of “majorization.”

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-coordinate linearization of the basic pairwise roof-dual LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each retained product introduce \(y_{ij}\) and impose \(0\le x_i\le1\), \(y_{ij}\ge0\), \(y_{ij}\ge x_i+x_j-1\), \(y_{ij}\le x_i\), and \(y_{ij}\le x_j\). At Boolean \(x\), these inequalities force \(y_{ij}=x_ix_j\). For continuous variables they are affinely equivalent, interaction by interaction, to the binary local-marginal coordinates through \(x_i=\mu_i(1)\), \(y_{ij}=\mu_{ij}(1,1)\), \(\mu_{ij}(1,0)=x_i-y_{ij}\), \(\mu_{ij}(0,1)=x_j-y_{ij}\), and \(\mu_{ij}(0,0)=1-x_i-x_j+y_{ij}\). Consequently the full termwise formulation is the product-coordinate form of the standard basic roof-dual LP for pairwise binary energies. It uses \(O(n+|E|)\) variables and inequalities and can be emitted in the same order of time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fortet-McCormick product variables give an exact binary formulation and, after relaxation, an affine product-coordinate representation of the standard basic roof-dual local LP for pairwise binary energies.

At Boolean \(x\), these constraints force \(y_{ij}=x_ix_j\), so the formulation is exact before integrality is relaxed. Its continuous optimum supplies the termwise-envelope LP view associated with the basic roof-dual bound, subject to the chosen roof-dual formulation convention.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural criterion for exact transformations among roof-dual representation views.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(T:Q_1\to Q_2\) is an affine bijection and \(g_2(Tu)=g_1(u)+\kappa\) for all \(u\in Q_1\), then feasible and optimal points correspond and the two normalized optimal values agree. If \(T\) also maps corresponding integral assignments, their integral restrictions are equivalent. Persistency conclusions transport only when the map preserves the relevant literal labels, up to declared complementation or relabeling, and the persistency criterion is invariant under that map. A nonbijective enlargement is a relaxation, and equality for one objective alone does not certify equivalent formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two roof-dual views are exactly equivalent under an affine feasible-set bijection that preserves the objective up to a constant. Integral solutions and persistency require the corresponding stronger label-preservation conditions.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Equivalence Criterion
Equivalent-View Transformations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion for transformations between equivalent roof-dual formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two roof-dual formulations \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) with feasible sets \(Q_1,Q_2\), objectives \(g_1,g_2\), and the same optimization direction \(\operatorname{opt}\in\{\min,\max\}\). Suppose there is an affine bijection \(T:Q_1\to Q_2\) such that \(g_2(Tu)=g_1(u)+\kappa\) for every \(u\in Q_1\), where \(\kappa\) is constant, and \(T\) maps integral literal assignments to their corresponding integral assignments. Then \[\operatorname{opt}_{v\in Q_2}g_2(v)=\operatorname{opt}_{u\in Q_1}g_1(u)+\kappa.\] Thus the formulations have the same normalized roof-dual bound, and their optimal and integral solutions correspond. If, in addition, \(T\) preserves the labeled literal coordinates used by the persistency criterion, up to the stated complementation or relabeling, and that criterion is invariant under this correspondence, then persistent assignments also correspond.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine feasible-set bijection preserving the objective up to a constant gives equivalent normalized bounds and corresponding solutions. Persistent assignments also correspond when the transformation preserves the labeled literal coordinates and persistency criterion.
assumptions_latex: Both formulations use the same optimization direction.
For the persistency conclusion, \(T\) preserves the labeled literal coordinates used by an invariant persistency criterion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two formulations have equal normalized optimal bounds and corresponding optimal solutions; under the additional coordinate-preservation hypothesis, their persistent assignments correspond.

knowledge_statements.title: Network-Flow Views
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed minimum-cut representation of a nonnegative quadratic literal form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[\phi(x)=c+\sum_i\bigl(\alpha_i x_i+\bar\alpha_i(1-x_i)\bigr)+\sum_{i\ne j}w_{ij}x_i(1-x_j),\] where all displayed coefficients except \(c\) are nonnegative. Construct a directed network with source \(s\), sink \(t\), arc \((i,t)\) of capacity \(\alpha_i\), arc \((s,i)\) of capacity \(\bar\alpha_i\), and arc \((i,j)\) of capacity \(w_{ij}\). Associate \(x_i=1\) with vertex \(i\) on the source side. Then every cut has capacity \(\phi(x)-c\), and therefore \[\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}\phi(x)=c+\operatorname{mincut}(s,t).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative directed-literal quadratic form is exactly a source–sink cut-capacity function, so its minimum is obtained by one minimum-cut computation.
assumptions_latex: Each binary assignment is identified with an source-side vertex set containing \(s\) and excluding \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_x\phi(x)=c+\operatorname{mincut}(s,t)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Immediate lower bound and equality certificate from nonnegative posiform terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi(x)=c+\sum_T a_Tm_T(x)\), where \(a_T\ge0\) and each literal monomial \(m_T(x)\in\{0,1\}\). Then \(\phi(x)\ge c\). Moreover, \[\phi(x)=c\iff m_T(x)=0\quad\text{for every }T\text{ with }a_T>0.\] Thus simultaneous falsification of all positive monomials certifies that \(c\) is the exact minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A posiform's constant is a lower bound, and an assignment zeroing every positive monomial certifies exactness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi(x)\ge c,\qquad \phi(x)=c\iff m_T(x)=0\ \forall T\text{ with }a_T>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Posiform Constant Lower Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of a nonnegative-literal representation for every quadratic pseudo-Boolean function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every finite real-valued quadratic pseudo-Boolean function admits a representation \[f(x)=c+\sum_{|T|\le2}a_Tm_T(x)\qquad(x\in\{0,1\}^n),\] where each \(a_T\ge0\), each \(m_T\) is a unary or quadratic literal monomial, and no monomial contains both complementary literals of one variable. The representation need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every quadratic pseudo-Boolean function has a quadratic posiform representation, generally nonunique and with a shifted constant.
assumptions_latex: The multilinear degree of \(f\) is at most two.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists c,\ a_T\ge0:\quad f(x)=c+\sum_{|T|\le2}a_Tm_T(x)\quad\forall x\in\{0,1\}^n.

notation.meaning: literal monomial of degree at most two

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Posiform Existence
Posiform Views
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic posiforms over literals and complementary literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For binary variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), a literal is either \(x_i\) or \(\bar x_i=1-x_i\). A quadratic posiform is a function \[\phi(x)=c+\sum_{	au}a_\tau\tau(x)+\sum_{\tau,\sigma}a_{\tau\sigma}\tau(x)\sigma(x),\] where \(a_\tau\ge0\), \(a_{\tau\sigma}\ge0\), and no product contains both literals of the same variable. Terms that vanish identically or combine algebraically may be removed. A posiform represents a pseudo-Boolean function \(f\) when \(f(x)=\phi(x)\) for every \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), possibly after isolating the constant \(c\). Different posiforms can represent the same Boolean function because \(x_i+\bar x_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic posiform is a constant plus nonnegative weighted literals and literal products; complementary-literal identities allow multiple representations of the same Boolean function.
assumptions_latex: All nonconstant posiform coefficients are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi\) is a quadratic posiform, and it represents \(f\) when \(f(x)=\phi(x)\) at every Boolean assignment.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the oriented posiform \[\phi(x)=c+\sum_i\bigl(\alpha_ix_i+\bar\alpha_i\bar x_i\bigr)+\sum_{i\ne j}w_{ij}x_i\bar x_j,\qquad \alpha_i,\bar\alpha_i,w_{ij}\ge0,\] assign respectively the arcs \((i,t)\), \((s,i)\), and \((i,j)\) with the same capacities. Hence assignment cost minus \(c\) equals cut capacity term by term. Conversely, every nonnegative capacitated directed source–sink network on the variable vertices induces such a posiform.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the stated direct term-incidence convention, the network has \(n+2\) vertices and at most \(u+m\) capacitated arcs, and it can be emitted in \(O(n+u+m)\) time and combinatorial storage. knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Views
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial Lagrangian representation of a feasible, bounded roof-dual LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,r\in\mathbb N\), let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a nonempty polytope, and let \(c\in\mathbb R^m\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{r\times m}\), and \(d\in\mathbb R^r\). Consider the roof-dual LP \(v_{\mathrm{RD}}=\min\{c^\top z:Bz=d,\ z\in P\}\), and define \(L(\lambda)=\min_{z\in P}\{c^\top z+\lambda^\top(Bz-d)\}\) for \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^r\). If the LP is feasible and has finite optimal value, finite-dimensional LP duality gives \[v_{\mathrm{RD}}=\max_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^r}L(\lambda).\] Hence every multiplier supplies a lower bound \(L(\lambda)\le v_{\mathrm{RD}}\), and maximizing these bounds recovers the LP value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing selected equalities of a feasible roof-dual LP with finite optimal value yields Lagrangian lower bounds whose maximum equals the LP value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{RD}}=\max_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^r}L(\lambda)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic local-marginal LP representation of the roof-dual relaxation for a pairwise binary energy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(E(x)=\sum_i\theta_i(x_i)+\sum_{ij\in E}\theta_{ij}(x_i,x_j)\), introduce nonnegative \(\mu_i(a)\) and \(\mu_{ij}(a,b)\), \(a,b\in\{0,1\}\), impose \(\sum_a\mu_i(a)=1\), \(\sum_b\mu_{ij}(a,b)=\mu_i(a)\), and \(\sum_a\mu_{ij}(a,b)=\mu_j(b)\), and minimize the corresponding expected unary and pairwise cost. Every Boolean assignment induces an integral feasible marginal vector, so this basic LP is a lower bound for minimization. Under the standard pairwise-energy convention, it is the basic roof-dual LP. It has \(O(n+|E|)\) variables and constraints. Additional global constraints require an explicitly enlarged formulation and are not silently included.

Introduce variables \(y_i\) and \(y_{ij}\), replace \(x_i\) and \(x_ix_j\) by them, and impose the local Boolean-product polytope constraints \[0\le y_i\le1,\qquad \max\{0,y_i+y_j-1\}\le y_{ij}\le\min\{y_i,y_j\}.\] Minimizing \(\alpha+\sum_i a_i y_i+\sum_{i<j}a_{ij}y_{ij}\) over these constraints is an LP relaxation and therefore gives a lower bound on \(\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}f(x)\).

children.title: Lagrangian–LP Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Dual relationships linking Lagrangian and linear-programming representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian–LP Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value correspondence between an extended roof-dual LP and its partial Lagrangian dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,r\in\mathbb N\), let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a nonempty polytope, and let \(c\in\mathbb R^m\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{r\times m}\), and \(d\in\mathbb R^r\). Define \(v_{\mathrm{RD}}=\min\{c^\top z:Bz=d,\ z\in P\}\) and its partial Lagrangian-dual value by \[d_{\mathrm{Lag}}=\max_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^r}\min_{z\in P}\bigl(c^\top z+\lambda^\top(Bz-d)\bigr).\] If the primal LP is feasible and has finite optimal value, finite-dimensional LP strong duality gives \(d_{\mathrm{Lag}}=v_{\mathrm{RD}}\). Under the displayed sign convention, an optimal multiplier \(\lambda\) is an optimal LP-dual variable associated with the equality \(Bz=d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible roof-dual LP with finite optimal value and its corresponding partial Lagrangian dual have equal values; under the stated sign convention, the multipliers are the LP-dual variables of the dualized equalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{\mathrm{Lag}}=v_{\mathrm{RD}}\).

notation.meaning: unrestricted multiplier for the equality Bz=d under the displayed sign convention

children.title: Dual-Equivalence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural extensions where the standard correspondence weakens or requires modification.

assumptions_latex: The comparison uses the minimization LP \(\min\{x:x=1,\ 0\le x\le1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{\lambda\in\mathbb R}L(\lambda)=1,\qquad \min_{0\le x\le1}x=0,\qquad \max_{\lambda\ge0}L(\lambda)=0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal witness separating retained or unrestricted dualization from omission and an invalid multiplier restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The LP \(\min\{x:x=1,\ 0\le x\le1\}\) has value \(1\). Its unrestricted equality Lagrangian dual has value \(1\). If the equality is omitted, the remaining LP has value \(0\); if the equality is dualized but its multiplier is incorrectly restricted to \(\lambda\ge0\) under the displayed sign convention, the maximum Lagrangian value is also \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-variable LP shows that retaining or correctly dualizing an equality gives value one, while omitting it or using the wrong multiplier sign gives value zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Witnesses

assumptions_latex: The original model is a finite-dimensional LP.
Every row not dualized remains enforced in the inner polyhedron.
Equality rows use unrestricted multipliers; inequality rows use the sign domain dictated by the chosen primal convention.
The compared primal LP is feasible with finite optimum for a finite-value equality statement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Retaining an undualized row preserves the LP, whereas deleting it or restricting its multiplier generally changes the relaxation and its dual value.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precise formulation changes that delimit partial Lagrangian-LP equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dualizing only a subset of an LP's coupling rows does not by itself weaken the LP correspondence: rows outside that subset may remain in the inner polyhedron, and partial Lagrangian duality then represents the same feasible LP under the usual finite strong-duality hypotheses. By contrast, deleting a row enlarges the primal relaxation, while restricting the valid multiplier domain changes the dual family. Either change can alter the value. Primal infeasibility or an infinite primal optimum must be handled through the corresponding extended-value alternatives rather than the asserted finite equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial dualization remains exact when all nondualized rows stay enforced. Deleting rows, imposing the wrong multiplier domain, or leaving the finite feasible regime changes or invalidates the claimed correspondence.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Handling Boundary
Dual-Equivalence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions limiting equality between a roof-dual LP and a Lagrangian construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The equality between a roof-dual LP and a Lagrangian dual applies only when both formulations use the same extended variables, the same undualized polytope \(P\), and multipliers unrestricted with the signs dictated by the dualized constraints. Dualizing only a proper subset of the intended coupling constraints yields the value of that weaker relaxation, not automatically the full roof-dual value. Likewise, infeasibility or an unbounded primal value prevents the finite strong-duality equality, and imposing nonconvex restrictions on \(z\) changes the inner problem from the LP correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual equivalence can fail after changing constraints, multiplier domains, or variable restrictions, or when primal feasibility and finite boundedness are absent.
assumptions_latex: The comparison concerns a proposed Lagrangian representation of a roof-dual LP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality is guaranteed only for matched formulations satisfying the hypotheses of finite-dimensional LP strong duality.

notation.meaning: polytope of constraints retained inside the Lagrangian subproblem

children.title: Weak Persistency
children.top_down_role: Partial-optimality certificates tied to the existence of a compatible optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Persistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak persistency certified by integral coordinates of a roof-dual optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R\), and let \(\hat y\in\{0,\tfrac12,1\}^n\) be an optimal labeling of its roof-dual relaxation. Put \(I=\{i:\hat y_i\in\{0,1\}\}\). Weak persistency means that there exists at least one global minimizer \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}f(x)\) satisfying \[x_i^\star=\hat y_i\qquad\text{for every }i\in I.\] Hence the integral coordinates can be fixed simultaneously without eliminating all globally optimal binary solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weakly persistent roof-dual labeling agrees on all its integral coordinates with at least one global binary minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is a finite-valued quadratic pseudo-Boolean objective.
\(\hat y\) is an optimal roof-dual labeling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\ \forall i\in I:\ x_i^\star=\hat y_i\).

notation.meaning: coordinates integral in the relaxation labeling
global binary minimizer agreeing with the certificate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The existential agreement formula matches the usual weak-persistency sense and certificate fits the leaf, but no source supports its applicability to an arbitrary optimal roof-dual labeling.

children.title: Strong Persistency
children.top_down_role: Partial-optimality certificates shared across all relevant optima.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Persistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong persistency requires agreement with every global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(\hat y\in\{0,\tfrac12,1\}^n\) be a roof-dual optimum, and set \(I=\{i:\hat y_i\in\{0,1\}\}\). Strong persistency holds when \[x_i^\star=\hat y_i\qquad\text{for every }x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}f(x)\text{ and every }i\in I.\] Thus every certified integral coordinate has the same value in all globally optimal binary solutions and may be fixed without discarding any optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strongly persistent roof-dual labeling agrees on every integral certified coordinate with every global binary minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is a finite-valued quadratic pseudo-Boolean objective.
\(\hat y\) is an optimal roof-dual labeling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\ \forall i\in I:\ x_i^\star=\hat y_i\).

notation.meaning: coordinates integral in the relaxation labeling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The universal agreement formula clearly states the proposed strong-persistency convention, but this convention and its roof-dual applicability require an authoritative source.

children.title: Persistency-Strength Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Logical implication and strictness relations between weak and strong persistency.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistency-Strength Hierarchy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical hierarchy of strong and weak persistency for a fixed certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed roof-dual labeling \(\hat y\) and its integral index set \(I\), strong persistency implies weak persistency whenever the binary problem has a global minimizer: agreement of every \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\) with \(\hat y_I\) implies agreement of at least one such minimizer. The converse is false in general because weak persistency permits other global minimizers to disagree on \(I\). Consequently, strong persistency preserves the entire optimal set after fixing \(x_I=\hat y_I\), whereas weak persistency preserves only its nonemptiness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong persistency implies weak persistency, but weak persistency need not preserve every optimum and therefore does not imply strong persistency.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{strong persistency}\Rightarrow\text{weak persistency}\), while the reverse implication fails in general.

notation.meaning: coordinates fixed by the persistency certificate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The implication is logically correct under the preceding existential and universal definitions, but those specialized persistency conventions and the claimed failure of the converse are uncited.

children.title: Weak-Only Persistency Regimes
children.top_down_role: Instances where weak certificates exist without corresponding strong certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Only Persistency Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate optima separate weak from strong persistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the one-variable quadratic pseudo-Boolean function \(f:\{0,1\}\to\mathbb R\) defined by \(f(x)=0\). Its exact roof relaxation is constant on \([0,1]\), so \(\hat y=0\) is an integral optimal relaxation labeling. The certificate \(x=0\) is weakly persistent because \(0\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\). It is not strongly persistent because \(1\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\) also and disagrees with \(\hat y\). Thus degeneracy of the binary optimum permits an integral relaxation optimum to provide only weak persistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant one-bit objective has an integral relaxation optimum agreeing with one binary optimum but not with all binary optima.
assumptions_latex: Weak and strong persistency are evaluated for the selected optimal labeling \(\hat y=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected certificate is weakly persistent but not strongly persistent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The example separates existential from universal agreement for a selected relaxation optimum, but a source is needed to establish that this selected-optimum interpretation is the intended roof-dual persistency convention.

children.title: Autarky Certificates
children.top_down_role: Partial assignments whose local replacement behavior certifies compatibility with optimal solutions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of objective-nonincreasing overwrite certificates under compatible simultaneous fixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_a\) and \(p_b\) overwrite coordinate sets \(I\) and \(J\), and suppose \(a_i=b_i\) for all \(i\in I\cap J\). If \(f(p_a(x))\le f(x)\) and \(f(p_b(x))\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), then \(p_a\circ p_b=p_b\circ p_a=p_{a\cup b}\) and \(f(p_{a\cup b}(x))\le f(x)\) for every \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible objective-nonincreasing overwrite certificates compose into a certificate for their combined partial assignment.
assumptions_latex: Each overwrite map is objective-nonincreasing on the entire binary domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(p_{a\cup b}(x))\le f(x)\quad\text{for all }x\in\{0,1\}^n.

notation.meaning: Overwrite map induced by the compatible union of the partial assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: Composition of Compatible Autarky Overwrites
Autarky Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial assignments certified by an objective-nonincreasing overwrite operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R\), choose \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let \(a\in\{0,1\}^I\). Define the overwrite map \(p_a\) by \((p_a(x))_i=a_i\) for \(i\in I\) and \((p_a(x))_i=x_i\) otherwise. The partial assignment \(a\) is an autarky certificate if \[f(p_a(x))\le f(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in\{0,1\}^n.\] Applying \(p_a\) to any global minimizer produces a global minimizer agreeing with \(a\), thereby certifying weak persistency of the fixed coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An autarky is a partial assignment whose overwrite operation never increases the objective and therefore preserves at least one optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}f:\ x_I^\star=a\).

notation.meaning: coordinates fixed by the partial assignment
map overwriting coordinates I by a

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The overwrite inequality does imply preservation of at least one optimum, and certificate is the correct role, but no source establishes that this is the intended autarky definition in roof-dual persistency theory.

children.title: Improving-Mapping Certificates
children.top_down_role: Mappings that certify objective-preserving or objective-improving variable transformations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closure of Improving Maps Under Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition rule for globally objective-nonincreasing self-maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p,q:X\to X\) satisfy \(f(p(x))\le f(x)\) and \(f(q(x))\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). Then \(f((p\circ q)(x))\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). If additionally \(p^2=p\), \(q^2=q\), and \(p\circ q=q\circ p\), then \((p\circ q)^2=p\circ q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective-nonincreasing maps compose, and commuting idempotent improving maps compose to another idempotent map.
assumptions_latex: \(f\circ p\le f\) and \(f\circ q\le f\) pointwise.
Idempotence of the composition additionally assumes \(p^2=p\), \(q^2=q\), and \(p\circ q=q\circ p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\circ p\circ q\le f;\qquad p^2=p,\ q^2=q,\ pq=qp\Longrightarrow(pq)^2=pq.

notation.meaning: Objective-nonincreasing self-maps of the feasible domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure of Improving Maps Under Composition
Improving-Mapping Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective comparison certifying a discrete improving map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=\{0,1\}^n\), a map \(p:X\to X\) is an improving-mapping certificate for \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) if it is idempotent and \[f(p(x))\le f(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in X.\] Its fixed-point set \(\operatorname{Fix}(p)=\{x:p(x)=x\}\) contains a global minimizer, because applying \(p\) to any minimizer cannot increase its value. If the inequality is strict whenever \(p(x)\ne x\), every global minimizer belongs to \(\operatorname{Fix}(p)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An idempotent objective-nonincreasing map preserves some optimum; strict improvement outside its fixed points forces every optimum to be fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Fix}(p)\cap\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\); under strict improvement, \(\operatorname*{argmin}f\subseteq\operatorname{Fix}(p)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-point conclusions follow for the stated finite, idempotent map, but the specialized improving-mapping definition and its certificate interpretation are uncited.

children.title: Autarky–Mapping Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relationship between autarky interpretations and improving-mapping certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Autarky–Mapping Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between overwrite autarkies and coordinate-fixing improving maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}^I\). The overwrite map \(p_a\) satisfies \(p_a\circ p_a=p_a\) and has fixed-point set \(\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:x_I=a\}\). Therefore \(a\) is an autarky for \(f\) exactly when \(p_a\) is an improving map: \[f(p_a(x))\le f(x)\quad\text{for all }x\in\{0,1\}^n.\] Conversely, every improving map that only overwrites a fixed coordinate set by constant binary values is uniquely the overwrite map of the corresponding autarky.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial-assignment autarky is exactly an improving map that overwrites a fixed coordinate set by constant binary values.
assumptions_latex: The converse is restricted to constant coordinate-overwrite maps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a\text{ is an autarky}\Longleftrightarrow p_a\text{ is an improving map}\).

notation.meaning: constant coordinate-overwrite map induced by a

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The overwrite equivalence is algebraically plausible, but it is a representation correspondence rather than mathematical duality. Sources are also required for both specialized definitions before the exact correspondence can be validated.

children.title: Certificate-Strength Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where one certificate viewpoint is strictly more expressive than the other.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A General Fixed-Point Set Need Not Encode Coordinate Fixings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a general idempotent map's fixed-point set to be a coordinate face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=\{0,1\}^2\), define \(p(00)=p(01)=00\) and \(p(10)=p(11)=11\), and let \(f\equiv0\). Then \(p\) is idempotent and objective-nonincreasing, with \(\operatorname{Fix}(p)=\{00,11\}\). This fixed-point set is not of the form \(\{x:x_I=a\}\) for any partial assignment \(a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An improving map may have a fixed-point set that is not a coordinate face and therefore does not directly encode persistent coordinate values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Fix}(p)=\{00,11\}\ne\{x:x_I=a\}\quad\text{for every partial assignment }a.

notation.meaning: Set of binary points unchanged by the map.

knowledge_statements.title: A General Fixed-Point Set Need Not Encode Coordinate Fixings

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Non-Strict Improvement Does Not Force All Optima to Be Fixed
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal separation between non-strict improvement and the conclusion that every optimum is fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{0,1\}\), let \(f(0)=f(1)=0\), and define \(p(0)=p(1)=0\). Then \(p\circ p=p\) and \(f(p(x))\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), but \(1\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\) and \(1\notin\operatorname{Fix}(p)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant objective shows that non-strict improvement can leave a global optimum outside the fixed-point set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\circ p\le f\quad\text{but}\quad\operatorname*{argmin}f\nsubseteq\operatorname{Fix}(p).

notation.meaning: Idempotent map sending both binary points to zero.

knowledge_statements.title: Non-Strict Improvement Does Not Force All Optima to Be Fixed

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective Nonincrease Without Idempotence Need Not Yield Fixed Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of a fixed-point-producing hypothesis for conclusions stated through the fixed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{0,1\}\), let \(f(0)=f(1)=0\), and define \(p(0)=1\), \(p(1)=0\). Then \(f(p(x))\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), but \(p\) has no fixed point and \(p^2\ne p\). Hence objective nonincrease alone cannot imply that an optimum lies in \(\operatorname{Fix}(p)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A value-preserving two-cycle is objective-nonincreasing but has no fixed point, so fixed-set persistency requires an additional hypothesis such as idempotence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\circ p\le f\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{Fix}(p)=\varnothing

notation.meaning: Set of points unchanged by p

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Nonincrease Without Idempotence Need Not Yield Fixed Points

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Improvement Is Sufficient but Not Necessary for Fixed Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the converse from fixed global minimizers to strict improvement at every moved point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{00,01,10\}\), define \(f(00)=0\) and \(f(01)=f(10)=1\), and set \(p(00)=00\), \(p(01)=10\), and \(p(10)=10\). Then \(p\) is idempotent and objective-nonincreasing, and every global minimizer is fixed. Nevertheless, \(p(01)\ne01\) and \(f(p(01))=f(01)\), so strict improvement at every moved point fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All global minimizers may be fixed even when a moved nonoptimal point is not strictly improved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \arg\min f\subseteq\operatorname{Fix}(p)\centernot\Longrightarrow[p(x)\ne x\Rightarrow f(p(x))<f(x)]
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Improvement Is Sufficient but Not Necessary for Fixed Optimality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Set Strength Theorem for Improving Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimal-set conclusions for non-strict and strict idempotent improving maps, without equating a general fixed set with coordinate persistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X
e\varnothing\) be finite, let \(f:X	o\mathbb R\), and let \(p:X	o X\) satisfy \(p\circ p=p\). If \(f(p(x))\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), then \[\operatorname*{argmin}f\cap\operatorname{Fix}(p)
e\varnothing.\] If additionally \(p(x)
e x\Rightarrow f(p(x))<f(x)\), then \[\operatorname*{argmin}f\subseteq\operatorname{Fix}(p).\] Coordinate persistency follows only when the map or its fixed set separately enforces specified coordinate values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An idempotent non-strict improving map fixes at least one optimum, whereas strict improvement of every moved point forces every optimum to be fixed; coordinate conclusions require additional structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\circ p\le f\Rightarrow\arg\min f\cap\operatorname{Fix}(p)\ne\varnothing;\quad[p(x)\ne x\Rightarrow f(p(x))<f(x)]\Rightarrow\arg\min f\subseteq\operatorname{Fix}(p)

notation.meaning: Set of points unchanged by the improving map.

review_flags: Fixed-set conclusions alone do not establish coordinate persistency.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Set Strength Theorem for Improving Maps
Certificate-Strength Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Non-strict and strict improving inequalities certify different persistency strengths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p:X\to X\) be idempotent on \(X=\{0,1\}^n\). The non-strict certificate \(f(p(x))\le f(x)\) guarantees only that some global minimizer lies in \(\operatorname{Fix}(p)\); equality may map one optimum to another while leaving additional optima outside the fixed-point set. Strong persistency follows from the stricter condition \[p(x)\ne x\Longrightarrow f(p(x))<f(x),\] because no global minimizer can then be moved by \(p\). Hence non-strict improvement generally certifies weak persistency, while strict improvement outside fixed points certifies strong persistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Non-strict improvement preserves some optimum; strict improvement of every moved point forces all optima into the map's fixed-point set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Non-strict improvement implies weak persistency; strict improvement outside \(\operatorname{Fix}(p)\) implies strong persistency.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The optimal-set statements for strict and non-strict improving maps are valid, but a general fixed-point set need not define fixed coordinate values. Its identification with weak or strong roof-dual persistency therefore requires additional hypotheses and a source.

children.title: Partial-Optimality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates identifying variable values compatible with global optimality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existential and universal partial optimality for a simultaneous binary assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E:X\to\mathbb R\) on a nonempty finite set \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), and let \(p\in\{0,1\}^S\). The pair \((S,p)\) is a weak partial-optimality certificate if \(\exists x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}E(x)\) with \(x_S^\star=p\). It is a strong partial-optimality certificate if every \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}E(x)\) satisfies \(x_S^\star=p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weak certificate matches at least one global optimum; a strong certificate matches every global optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{strong partial optimality}\Longrightarrow\text{weak partial optimality}.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak and Strong Partial-Optimality Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimal-Value Tests for Weak and Strong Partial Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-domain tests for a proposed simultaneous partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be finite and nonempty, let \(v=\min_{x\in X}E(x)\), and let \(F=\{x\in X:x_S=p\}\). With \(\min\varnothing=+\infty\), \((S,p)\) is weakly partially optimal exactly when \(\min_{x\in F}E(x)=v\). It is strongly partially optimal exactly when \(\min_{x\in X\setminus F}E(x)>v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixing is weak precisely when its face attains the optimum, and strong precisely when every point outside that face is strictly worse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{weak}\iff\min_{x\in F}E(x)=v,\qquad\text{strong}\iff\min_{x\in X\setminus F}E(x)>v

notation.meaning: Coordinate face selected by the proposed assignment.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Value Tests for Weak and Strong Partial Optimality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Partial-Optimality Certificates Are Closed Under Union
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistent aggregation of coordinate assignments shared by every global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\arg\min E\ne\varnothing\) and each \((S_k,p^k)\) is a strong partial-optimality certificate, then the assignments agree on overlaps and their union on \(S=\bigcup_kS_k\) is a strong partial-optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any collection of strong certificates combines into one consistent strong certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x^\star\in\arg\min E:\ x^\star_{\cup_kS_k}=\bigcup_kp^k
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Partial-Optimality Certificates Are Closed Under Union

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hereditary behavior under deletion of certified coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \((S,p)\) is a weak partial-optimality certificate, then \((T,p_T)\) is weak for every \(T\subseteq S\). If \((S,p)\) is strong, every such restriction is strong. The converses fail for weak certificates: separately certified restrictions need not share a common optimal witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting coordinates preserves weak and strong partial optimality, but separately witnessed weak restrictions need not recombine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (S,p)\text{ weak or strong}\Rightarrow(T,p_T)\text{ has the same respective status}.
knowledge_statements.title: Restriction Closure of Partial-Optimality Certificates
Partial-Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Roof-dual weak-persistency certificate for a quadratic pseudo-Boolean minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R\) be quadratic, let \(R\) be its roof-dual relaxation, and let \(y^\star\in\{0,\tfrac12,1\}^n\) minimize \(R\). Define \(S=\{i:y_i^\star\in\{0,1\}\}\) and \(p_i=y_i^\star\) for \(i\in S\). The pair \((S,p)\) is a partial-optimality certificate when roof-dual persistency establishes
\[\exists x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}E(x)\quad\text{such that}\quad x_i^\star=p_i\ \text{for every }i\in S.\]
Thus the certificate asserts compatibility with at least one global minimizer, not necessarily with every global minimizer.

\(R\) is the standard roof-dual relaxation of \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x^\star\in\arg\min E\) with \(x_S^\star=p\).

children.title: Variable-Fixing Consequences
children.top_down_role: Reductions in the unresolved variable set justified by partial-optimality information.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Fixing Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduction obtained by fixing labels supplied by a weak-persistency certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((S,p)\) be a valid partial-optimality certificate for \(E:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R\), and let \(T=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus S\). Define the reduced energy by \(E_p(z)=E(x)\), where \(x_S=p\) and \(x_T=z\). Then
\[\min_{z\in\{0,1\}^{T}}E_p(z)=\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}E(x).\]
Consequently, fixing every certified coordinate to its certified value preserves the global optimum value. Any minimizer \(z^\star\) of the reduced problem lifts to a global minimizer \((p,z^\star)\) of the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixing certified variables preserves the optimal value, and every optimum of the resulting reduced problem lifts to an original optimum.
assumptions_latex: \((S,p)\) certifies compatibility with a global minimizer of \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min E_p=\min E\), and every reduced minimizer lifts to a global minimizer.

notation.meaning: energy after substituting the certified assignment

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Separate Weak Certificates Need Not Combine into a Valid Fixing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of coordinatewise combination when weak certificates use different optimal witnesses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(E:\{0,1\}^2\to\mathbb R\) by \(E(0,0)=E(1,1)=0\) and \(E(0,1)=E(1,0)=1\). The fixing \(x_1=0\) is compatible with the optimum \((0,0)\), and \(x_2=1\) is compatible with the optimum \((1,1)\). Nevertheless, the combined fixing \((x_1,x_2)=(0,1)\) excludes every global optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two separately witnessed weak fixings need not have any common optimal completion.
assumptions_latex: Weak persistence means compatibility with at least one global minimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Separate Weak Certificates Need Not Combine into a Valid Fixing
Certificate-to-Fixing Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence between integral roof-dual coordinates and admissible partial variable fixings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an optimal half-integral roof-dual vector \(y^\star\), define
\[\Phi(y^\star)=\{(i,y_i^\star):y_i^\star\in\{0,1\}\}.\]
Under weak persistency, \(\Phi(y^\star)\) represents the simultaneous variable fixing \(x_i=y_i^\star\) for every integral coordinate. Conversely, the fixing represented by this particular relaxation solution contains no coordinate with \(y_i^\star=\tfrac12\): such a coordinate is outside the certificate and must remain free unless another valid certificate fixes it. The correspondence is solution-dependent when the roof-dual relaxation has multiple optimal solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each integral roof-dual coordinate corresponds to one certified fixing; half-integral coordinates contribute no fixing from that relaxation solution.
assumptions_latex: \(y^\star\) is an optimal half-integral roof-dual solution.
Weak roof-dual persistency holds for the chosen formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi(y^\star)\) is exactly the fixing set represented by \(y^\star\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable structure exposed after certified substitution in a quadratic binary energy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_p(z)=c_p+\sum_{i\in T}a'_iz_i+\sum_{\{i,j\}\subseteq T}b_{ij}z_iz_j\) be the exact residual energy, and form \(H_p=(T,\{\{i,j\}:b_{ij}\ne0\})\). Dynamic programming over a nice form of the decomposition stores, for each bag assignment, the minimum processed-subtree energy consistent with that assignment. It returns an exact residual optimum using \(O(B2^{\tau+1})\) table entries and \(O(B2^{\tau+1})\) arithmetic operations up to polynomial preprocessing and rational bit-complexity factors.

After fixing any coordinate set \(S\) and substituting its values, every quadratic coefficient between two remaining variables is still \(b_{ij}\le0\); only the constant and unary coefficients change. Hence the residual energy remains pairwise submodular.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit constant, unary, and pairwise coefficients after substituting a certified simultaneous fixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[E(x)=c+\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i+\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}b_{ij}x_ix_j.\] Fix \(x_S=p\), put \(T=[n]\setminus S\), and write \(z=x_T\). Then \[E_p(z)=c_p+\sum_{j\in T}a'_jz_j+\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in T}}b_{ij}z_iz_j,\] where \[c_p=c+\sum_{i\in S}a_ip_i+\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in S}}b_{ij}p_ip_j,\qquad a'_j=a_j+\sum_{\substack{i\in S\\i<j}}b_{ij}p_i+\sum_{\substack{i\in S\\j<i}}b_{ji}p_i.\] Thus substitution changes only the constant and surviving unary coefficients; interactions between two unfixed variables remain unchanged.

\[E_p(z)=c_p+\sum_{j\in T}\left(a_j+\sum_{i\in S}b_{\min\{i,j\},\max\{i,j\}}p_i\right)z_j+\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in T}}b_{ij}z_iz_j,\]
with \(c_p=c+\sum_{i\in S}a_ip_i+\sum_{i<j,\ i,j\in S}b_{ij}p_ip_j\). This residual QPBO contains precisely the unfixed variables and has the same optimum value as the original problem.

children.title: Basic QPBO Formulations
children.top_down_role: Core quadratic pseudo-Boolean optimization formulations underlying roof-dual computation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit conversion of a binary pairwise table into its unique multilinear contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\theta_{ij}:\{0,1\}^2\to\mathbb R\), \[\theta_{ij}(x_i,x_j)=\theta_{ij}(0,0)+[\theta_{ij}(1,0)-\theta_{ij}(0,0)]x_i+[\theta_{ij}(0,1)-\theta_{ij}(0,0)]x_j+b_{ij}x_ix_j,\] where \[b_{ij}=\theta_{ij}(0,0)-\theta_{ij}(1,0)-\theta_{ij}(0,1)+\theta_{ij}(1,1).\] Summing and collecting coefficients gives the unique global multilinear quadratic polynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A four-entry binary pairwise table has an explicit unique constant, unary, and product expansion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b_{ij}=\theta_{ij}(0,0)-\theta_{ij}(1,0)-\theta_{ij}(0,1)+\theta_{ij}(1,1).
knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise-Table Coefficient Conversion
Basic QPBO Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent pairwise-table and quadratic-polynomial forms of a binary quadratic objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A quadratic pseudo-Boolean optimization problem has the pairwise form
\[\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}E(x),\qquad E(x)=c+\sum_{i=1}^n\theta_i(x_i)+\sum_{\{i,j\}\in\mathcal E}\theta_{ij}(x_i,x_j).\]
Because each variable is binary, the same objective has a unique multilinear quadratic form after collecting coefficients,
\[E(x)=\alpha+\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i+\sum_{\{i,j\}\in\mathcal E}b_{ij}x_ix_j.\]
Conversely, every such quadratic polynomial defines pairwise tables, with constants and unary contributions distributable among the tables without changing \(E\). QPBO seeks a minimizing binary labeling; roof duality relaxes this formulation to obtain a lower bound and partial labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: QPBO minimizes a binary energy containing unary and pairwise terms, equivalently represented as a multilinear quadratic polynomial.
assumptions_latex: Every interaction involves at most two variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pairwise-table and multilinear quadratic forms represent the same class of objectives.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a pairwise binary energy \(E\). Construct its doubled symmetric directed network \(G=(V,A)\), with source \(s\), sink \(t\), complementary variable vertices, nonnegative capacities, and a constant \(\kappa\), so that every admissible symmetric cut \(C\) encodes a half-integral vector \(y(C)\) and satisfies \(R(y(C))=\kappa+\operatorname{cap}(C)\). Initialize any feasible flow, compute a maximum \(s\)-\(t\) flow, and extract a minimum cut from residual reachability. Output the relaxation value \(\kappa+\operatorname{cap}(C)\), the half-integral labeling \(y(C)\), and integral-coordinate persistency candidates; coordinates whose complementary vertices do not determine opposite orientations remain unlabeled.

knowledge_statements.title: QPBO–Flow Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value and solution correspondence between roof-dual QPBO and symmetric minimum cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a correctly constructed QPBO network with representation constant \(\kappa\), the roof-dual and flow values satisfy
\[\min_y R(y)=\kappa+\min_C\operatorname{cap}(C)=\kappa+\max_f\operatorname{val}(f),\]
where \(C\) ranges over admissible \(s\)-\(t\) cuts and \(f\) over feasible \(s\)-\(t\) flows. A minimum cut decodes to an optimal half-integral roof-dual labeling. Oppositely oriented complementary vertices encode an integral label, whereas a nonseparating orientation encodes \(\tfrac12\). Conversely, every optimal roof-dual labeling admits an optimal cut representation, subject to the network's symmetry convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum cuts solve the roof-dual relaxation: cut value equals relaxation value up to a constant, and cut orientations encode partial labels.
assumptions_latex: The doubled network exactly represents the roof-dual objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min R=\kappa+\min\operatorname{cap}(C)=\kappa+\max\operatorname{val}(f)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive boundary complementary to the unlabeled-variable regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y^\star\in\{0,\tfrac12,1\}^n\) minimize a valid roof-dual relaxation \(R\) that agrees with \(E\) on binary labelings. If \(y^\star\) is integral, then \[R(y^\star)=E(y^\star)=\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}E(x).\] Thus a completely labeled QPBO solution is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If QPBO labels every variable, the decoded labeling is globally optimal and the roof bound is exact.

knowledge_statements.title: Complete-Label Exactness
Unlabeled-Variable Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Meaning and limitation of half-integral coordinates returned by QPBO.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(y^\star\) be the half-integral labeling decoded from a QPBO minimum cut. The unlabeled set is
\[U=\{i:y_i^\star=\tfrac12\}.\]
For \(i\in U\), the selected cut does not orient the two complementary variable representatives in the manner required to encode either binary value. Roof-dual weak persistency therefore supplies no fixing for \(x_i\) from this solution. Unlabeled does not mean that both values occur in global optima, nor that the variable is intrinsically unfixable: another optimal cut, probing, or a stronger relaxation may label it. The residual problem retains every coordinate in \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A half-integral QPBO coordinate is unlabeled and receives no fixing, but it may still be fixed by another certificate or stronger procedure.
assumptions_latex: \(y^\star\) is decoded using a fixed QPBO cut convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i\in U\) implies that this QPBO solution certifies neither \(x_i=0\) nor \(x_i=1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_{i,b}\) be a valid lower bound on \(\min\{E(x):x_i=b\}\), and let \(U\) be the value of a feasible incumbent. If \(L_{i,b}>U\), no global minimizer lies in the branch \(x_i=b\). Equality \(L_{i,b}=U\) does not in general permit deletion because the branch may contain a global minimizer of value \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict lower-bound dominance excludes a probed branch; equality with the incumbent does not.

L_{i,b}>U\Rightarrow x_i

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for the branch fixing x_i=b

knowledge_statements.title: Strictness of Probe Exclusion

assumptions_latex: Each \(L_{i,b}\) is a valid lower bound for the forced branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every excluded branch contains no global minimizer with objective at most \(U\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branchwise roof-dual tests used to derive additional fixings and implications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a quadratic binary energy \(E\), a feasible labeling \(\bar x\) with \(U=E(\bar x)\), and a set of variables to probe. For each selected \(i\) and \(b\in\{0,1\}\), solve the roof-dual relaxation of the restricted problem \(x_i=b\), obtaining a lower bound \(L_{i,b}\) and its partial labels. If \(L_{i,b}>U\), delete that branch and fix \(x_i=1-b\). Record any conditional labels as implications, substitute unconditional fixings, and repeat until a complete sweep adds no fixing or implication. Output the accumulated certificates and the reduced unfixed QPBO.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: QPBO probing solves roof relaxations under forced values, excludes branches whose lower bounds exceed an incumbent, and accumulates valid fixings or implications.
knowledge_statements.title: QPBO Probing

children.title: QPBO Improvement
children.top_down_role: Postprocessing families that improve a complete assignment using QPBO structure.

knowledge_statements.title: QPBO Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Energy-monotonic guarantee of QPBO-I relative to a supplied complete labeling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R\) be a pairwise binary energy and let \(x^{(0)}\) be a complete input labeling. Apply the standard QPBO-I construction, retaining \(x_i^{(0)}\) on coordinates left unlabeled by its cut and applying the labels certified by its improving-map construction on the remaining coordinates. If \(x^{(1)}\) denotes the resulting complete labeling, then
\[E(x^{(1)})\le E(x^{(0)}).\]
Thus QPBO-I certifies improvement or equality relative to the supplied labeling. The inequality alone is not a global-optimality certificate unless the returned value also matches a valid global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: QPBO-I completes unlabeled coordinates from an input labeling and returns a labeling whose energy is no greater, without thereby proving global optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite pairwise binary energy.
The standard QPBO-I improving-map construction is used.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotonicity property and its distinction from optimality fit the leaf, but the exact QPBO-I construction and guarantee require a primary or authoritative source.

children.title: Probing-Induced Persistency
children.top_down_role: Additional persistency information obtained through conditional analysis.

assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is feasible for the unrestricted binary problem.
\(L_{i,b}\) is a valid lower bound for the branch \(x_i=b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{i,b}>E(\bar x)\Rightarrow x_i^\star=1-b\) for every global minimizer \(x^\star\).

notation.meaning: lower bound for the forced branch

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent fixing certified by a forced-branch lower bound and a feasible upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U=E(\bar x)\) for a feasible binary labeling \(\bar x\), and let \(L_{i,b}\) be a valid lower bound on
\[\min\{E(x):x\in\{0,1\}^n,\ x_i=b\}.\]
If \(L_{i,b}>U\), then every global minimizer satisfies \(x_i=1-b\). The triple \((i,b,L_{i,b}>U)\), together with verifiable lower- and upper-bound certificates, is a strong-persistency certificate for fixing \(x_i=1-b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the lower bound for one forced value exceeds a feasible objective value, that value is impossible in every global optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Probing-Induced Persistency

children.title: Improvement–Optimality Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on the optimality guarantees supplied by QPBO-based improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Improvement–Optimality Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Energy improvement is weaker than certification of global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inequality \(E(P(x))\le E(x)\) for an improvement map \(P\) does not imply that \(P(x)\) is globally optimal. For example, let \(E:\{0,1\}\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(E(0)=0\) and \(E(1)=1\), and let \(P\) be the identity map. Then \(E(P(x))=E(x)\) for every \(x\), but from \(x=1\) the output is not optimal. Accordingly, a QPBO-I monotonicity guarantee becomes an optimality certificate only when accompanied by a valid lower bound \(L\) satisfying \(E(x^{(1)})=L\); unlabeled variables otherwise delimit the unresolved subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonincreasing energy does not prove optimality; equality with a valid global lower bound is additionally required.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is known only to satisfy \(E(P(x))\le E(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Improvement alone is insufficient; \(E(x^{(1)})=L\) with a global lower bound \(L\) certifies optimality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate, and the counterexample correctly separates monotonic improvement from global optimality. A source is still required for the QPBO-I-specific boundary claim and its connection to unlabeled variables.

children.title: Higher-Order Roof Duality
children.top_down_role: Roof-dual extensions for pseudo-Boolean terms beyond quadratic degree.

assumptions_latex: There exists a quadratic extension \(q:\{0,1\}^{n+m}\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(f(x)=\min_{z\in\{0,1\}^m}q(x,z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathrm{HRD}}\le \min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}f(x)\), and every original variable fixed persistently by the quadratic roof relaxation is fixed in at least one optimum of \(f\).

notation.meaning: A quadratic extension, or quadratization, of the higher-order objective.
The roof-dual lower bound obtained from the quadratic extension.

review_flags: exact higher-order roof-duality convention and persistency strength require an authoritative source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratization-based extension of quadratic roof duality to higher-order pseudo-Boolean objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(L_{\mathrm{HRD}}\) as the minimum of the standard quadratic roof relaxation of \(q\), in which each binary variable, including every auxiliary variable, is replaced by its roof-dual relaxation. Since this relaxation contains every point \((x,z)\in\{0,1\}^{n+m}\),
\[
L_{\mathrm{HRD}}\le \min_{(x,z)\in\{0,1\}^{n+m}}q(x,z)=\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}f(x).
\]
If the chosen quadratic roof-duality theorem persistently labels an original coordinate \(x_i\), then there exists an optimizer \(x^*\) of \(f\) having that label. Labels of auxiliary coordinates do not themselves assert properties of the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Higher-order roof duality applies quadratic roof relaxation to a quadratization, producing a valid lower bound and persistent original-variable labels, but both can depend on the chosen quadratization.
knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Order Roof Duality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the higher-order roof-duality leaf, and the lower-bound argument is coherent. However, no source is supplied for the construction-specific persistency claim or for its dependence on the chosen quadratization. Those details vary across higher-order roof-duality formulations and require an authoritative locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representation of Tiles for Polynomial Terms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tile representation under the source-defined polynomial form (10.1.5) and its positive- and negative-term notation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p_k\) be a tile of a nonlinear term of a polynomial \(f\) in the source-defined form (10.1.5). Then
\[
p_k(x)=\begin{cases}
\sum_{j\in Q_k}\lambda_k^j x_j,&k\in N^+,\\
v_k\bar{x}_{t_k}+\sum_{j\in R_k}\mu_k^j x_j,&k\in N^-,
\end{cases}
\]
with
\[
\sum_{j\in Q_k}\lambda_k^j=d_k,\qquad
v_k+\sum_{j\in R_k}\mu_k^j=e_k,\qquad
(\lambda,\mu,v)\ge0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the source-defined polynomial representation, a tile has one of two nonnegative-coefficient forms according to whether its term is in the positive or negative index class, and its coefficients satisfy the stated sum equality.
assumptions_latex: p_k\text{ is a tile of a nonlinear term of }f
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_k(x)=\begin{cases}\sum_{j\in Q_k}\lambda_k^j x_j,&k\in N^+,\\v_k\bar{x}_{t_k}+\sum_{j\in R_k}\mu_k^j x_j,&k\in N^-,\end{cases}\quad \sum_{j\in Q_k}\lambda_k^j=d_k,\quad v_k+\sum_{j\in R_k}\mu_k^j=e_k,\quad(\lambda,\mu,v)\ge0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assembly of local upper planes into an affine upper-plane construction for a polynomial pseudo-Boolean function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A paved upper plane is defined by
\[
p(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n c_i x_i+\sum_{k\in N}p_k(x)
=\sum_{k\in N}\lambda_k^0+\sum_{i=1}^n\left(c_i+\sum_{k\in S^{-1}(i)}\lambda_k^i\right)x_i,
\]
where \(p_k(x)=\lambda_k^0+\sum_{i\in S_k}\lambda_k^i x_i\), \(S^{-1}(i)=\{k\in N\mid i\in S_k\}\), and the coefficients satisfy the source-defined local-upper-plane constraints (10.1.1)–(10.1.3).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A paved upper plane combines the original linear terms with all local upper planes. After coefficients are collected, each variable receives contributions from every nonlinear term containing it.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-total-slack local upper planes and roofs assembled from them.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A tile of \(f_k\) is a local upper plane \(p_k\) minimizing
\[
\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^{s_k}}\bigl(p_k(x)-f_k(x)\bigr)
\]
over all local upper planes of \(f_k\); equivalently, it minimizes the total slack in the source-defined inequalities (10.1.1)–(10.1.3). A paved upper plane of \(f\) is a roof when all of its local upper planes are tiles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tile is a local upper plane having minimum total overestimation across all binary assignments. A paved upper plane composed entirely of tiles is called a roof.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_k\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\widetilde p_k\,\text{a local upper plane of }f_k}\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^{s_k}}\bigl(\widetilde p_k(x)-f_k(x)\bigr),\qquad p\text{ is a roof iff every local upper plane }p_k\text{ is a tile}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear majorants of pseudo-Boolean functions and individual polynomial monomial terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A linear function \(p(x)\) is an upper plane of \(f(x)\) if \(p(x)\ge f(x)\) for every \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\). For \(f_k(x)=q_k\prod_{i\in S_k}x_i\), a local upper plane is a linear function \(p_k(x)=\lambda_k^0+\sum_{i\in S_k}\lambda_k^i x_i\) such that \(p_k(x)\ge f_k(x)\) for every binary assignment to the variables indexed by \(S_k\).
