children.title: Generalized Roof Duality
children.top_down_role: Broader roof-dual frameworks extending the standard quadratic setting.

assumptions_latex: \(\widehat f:\{0,\tfrac12,1\}^n\to\mathbb R\) agrees with \(f\) on \(\{0,1\}^n\) and is bisubmodular on the half-integral domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{u\in\{0,1/2,1\}^n}\widehat f(u)\le\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}f(x)\), with labeled coordinates admitting a persistency interpretation under the selected generalized roof-duality theorem.

notation.meaning: A bisubmodular half-integral relaxation extending the pseudo-Boolean objective.

review_flags: generalized roof duality has multiple formulations in the literature
exact maximality and persistency theorem require a source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Half-integral bisubmodular formulation; no maximality claim is made without a selected theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A generalized roof relaxation of \(f\) is a bisubmodular function \(\widehat f\) on \(\{0,\tfrac12,1\}^n\) whose restriction to binary points equals \(f\). Its generalized roof-dual value is
\[
L_{\mathrm{GRD}}:=\min_{u\in\{0,1/2,1\}^n}\widehat f(u).
\]
Because every binary point is feasible in the relaxed domain and \(\widehat f(x)=f(x)\) there,
\[
L_{\mathrm{GRD}}\le\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}f(x).
\]
Coordinates with \(u_i\in\{0,1\}\) are labeled; the precise weak or strong persistency conclusion attached to those labels depends on the selected generalized roof-duality construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generalized roof duality minimizes a bisubmodular half-integral extension of a pseudo-Boolean objective, yielding a lower bound; its integral coordinates may support a construction-specific persistency claim.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Roof Duality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality role and half-integral bisubmodular formulation fit the leaf, and the lower-bound inequality follows from the stated extension property. No source identifies the intended generalized roof-duality construction or the theorem supporting any persistency interpretation, so the record cannot yet be accepted.

children.title: Quadratization Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Connections between higher-order objectives and auxiliary quadratic representations.

assumptions_latex: \(q:\{0,1\}^{n+m}\to\mathbb R\) is quadratic and satisfies \(f(x)=\min_{z\in\{0,1\}^m}q(x,z)\) for every \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Quadratization transfers minimization exactly on binary points, whereas its continuous or roof-dual relaxation need not project to a representation-independent relaxation of \(f\).

notation.meaning: Auxiliary binary variables introduced by quadratization.

review_flags: roof-specific projection behavior needs dedicated source support
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact binary quadratization interface and its noncommutation with relaxation.

source_refs.locator: 5.7 Computing relaxations of mixed linear quadratic programs p. 69
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The equality
\[
f(x)=\min_{z\in\{0,1\}^m}q(x,z)
\]
defines an exact quadratization interface. It implies
\[
\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}f(x)=\min_{(x,z)\in\{0,1\}^{n+m}}q(x,z).
\]
If integrality is relaxed, however, the projected epigraph
\[
\{(x,t):\exists z\text{ relaxed with }q(x,z)\le t\}
\]
is determined by the particular extension \(q\). Consequently, exact equality on binary points alone does not imply that two quadratizations produce the same roof-dual bound or the same persistent labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratization preserves the binary optimum exactly, but relaxing its auxiliary formulation can produce bounds and persistent labels that depend on the chosen extension.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratization Interfaces

source_witnesses.locator: 5.7 Computing relaxations of mixed linear quadratic programs p. 69
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the quadratization-interface leaf, and exact preservation of the binary optimum is stated correctly. The cited mixed-linear-quadratic relaxation section does not specifically establish the claimed dependence of roof-dual bounds and persistent labels on the quadratization. A dedicated quadratization or roof-duality source is required.

children.title: Generalization-Equivalence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where extended constructions cease to retain standard roof-dual equivalences.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R\) has two exact quadratic extensions \(q_1(x,z^1)\) and \(q_2(x,z^2)\).
\(R_1\) and \(R_2\) are the corresponding roof-relaxed feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Binary equivalence of \(q_1\) and \(q_2\) does not imply equality of their relaxed values or labeled-coordinate sets; equality follows if their projected relaxed epigraphs coincide.

notation.meaning: The projected relaxed epigraph induced by extension k.
The roof-relaxed feasible set for extension k.

review_flags: exact generalized-roof equivalence criteria require an authoritative source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between binary equivalence and equivalence after roof relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(k\in\{1,2\}\), define the projected relaxed epigraph
\[
E_k:=\{(x,t):\exists z^k\text{ with }(x,z^k)\in R_k\text{ and }q_k(x,z^k)\le t\}.
\]
The identities \(f(x)=\min_{z^k\in\{0,1\}}q_k(x,z^k)\) imply only equality of the binary restrictions of \(E_1\) and \(E_2\). They do not imply \(E_1=E_2\), equality of relaxed minima, or equality of labeled original coordinates. A sufficient equivalence condition is \(E_1=E_2\); under this condition both relaxations induce the same value function on the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two extensions can represent the same binary objective yet differ after relaxation. Their generalized roof bounds agree when their projected relaxed epigraphs coincide.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalization-Equivalence Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, and equality of projected relaxed epigraphs is a coherent sufficient condition for value-function equivalence. No source supports the asserted non-equivalence phenomenon or connects projected epigraph equivalence to labeled-coordinate behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent optimization of connected components remaining after persistent labels are substituted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G[U]\) be the interaction graph induced by the unlabeled coordinates of the residual quadratic objective, and let \(U_1,\ldots,U_k\) be its connected components. Then there exist a constant \(c'\) and component objectives \(f_r:\{0,1\}^{U_r}\to\mathbb R\) such that \(f_U(x_U)=c'+\sum_{r=1}^k f_r(x_{U_r})\). Consequently, \[\min_{x_U}f_U(x_U)=c'+\sum_{r=1}^k\min_{x_{U_r}}f_r(x_{U_r}),\] and concatenating component minimizers yields a residual minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After fixing labeled variables, connected components of the remaining interaction graph can be optimized independently.
assumptions_latex: \(f_U\) is the quadratic residual after substitution.
\(U_1,\ldots,U_k\) are the connected components of its nonzero pair-interaction graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min f_U=c'+\sum_{r=1}^k\min f_r\), with componentwise minimizers combining into a global residual minimizer.

notation.meaning: interaction graph induced by unlabeled variables
a connected component of the residual interaction graph

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Component Decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit coefficient representation after substituting all persistently labeled variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write \(f(x)=c+\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i+\sum_{i<j}b_{ij}x_ix_j\), extend \(b_{ij}=b_{ji}\), and partition the indices into labeled coordinates \(L\) with fixed values \(u_L\) and unlabeled coordinates \(U\). Then \(f_U(x_U)=f(x_U,u_L)\) is quadratic with \[f_U(x_U)=c'+\sum_{i\in U}\left(a_i+\sum_{j\in L}b_{ij}u_j\right)x_i+\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in U}}b_{ij}x_ix_j,\] where \(c'=c+\sum_{j\in L}a_ju_j+\sum_{\substack{i<j\\i,j\in L}}b_{ij}u_iu_j\). Thus fixing labels deletes labeled vertices and converts every labeled-to-unlabeled interaction into a unary coefficient adjustment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substitution preserves interactions among unlabeled variables, turns crossing interactions into unary terms, and absorbs fully labeled terms into the constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_U\) has the displayed updated constant and unary coefficients and retains the original pair coefficients induced on \(U\).
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Quadratic Coefficient Update

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is a binary quadratic objective and \(u\in\{0,\tfrac12,1\}^n\) is an optimal roof-dual labeling.
\(U:=\{i:u_i=\tfrac12\}\) and the labeled coordinates are fixed to \(u_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The residual problem over \(U\) retains all interactions induced by the fixed labels and generally remains a binary optimization problem requiring additional optimization.

notation.meaning: Indices left unlabeled by the roof relaxation.
The objective after substituting labeled coordinates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual binary problem obtained after substituting roof-dual labels.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Optimality Conditions for Unconstrained Binary Quadratic Problems p. 38

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L:=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus U\) and substitute \(x_i=u_i\) for every \(i\in L\). The residual objective is
\[
f_U(x_U):=f(x_U,u_L),\qquad x_U\in\{0,1\}^{U}.
\]
Under weak persistency, some global minimizer of \(f\) agrees with \(u_L\), so
\[
\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}f(x)=\min_{x_U\in\{0,1\}^{U}}f_U(x_U).
\]
Roof duality alone supplies no binary values for coordinates in \(U\); unless \(U\) is empty or the residual has additional tractable structure, completing the solution requires a separate exact or approximate method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixing persistent labels leaves a binary optimization problem on half-integrally labeled variables; roof duality alone does not determine those remaining values.
knowledge_statements.title: Unlabeled-Variable Residual Problems

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Optimality Conditions for Unconstrained Binary Quadratic Problems p. 38

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual-problem representation fits the leaf, and the residual equality is correct if the labels satisfy weak persistency. The cited section on optimality conditions for unconstrained binary quadratic problems does not inspectably support the roof-duality weak-persistency premise. A roof-duality source with a specific persistency theorem or section is needed.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A pairwise term is graph-cut submodular exactly when \(a_{ij}\le0\); positive coefficients form the local non-submodular barrier to direct cut representation.

notation.meaning: The four values of the pairwise potential.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise submodularity boundary for minimization of binary quadratic objectives.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Optimality Conditions for Unconstrained Binary Quadratic Problems p. 38

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A pairwise potential \(\theta_{ij}\) is submodular precisely when
\[
\theta_{ij}(0,0)+\theta_{ij}(1,1)\le \theta_{ij}(0,1)+\theta_{ij}(1,0).
\]
For \(\theta_{ij}(x_i,x_j)=a_{ij}x_ix_j\), this condition is \(a_{ij}\le0\). Hence a positive interaction \(a_{ij}>0\) cannot be represented directly as a submodular source-sink cut term without a transformation or relaxation. Such terms are the local obstruction addressed by roof-dual constructions; their presence can cause half-integral labels, although it does not force every variable to be unlabeled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For quadratic binary minimization, positive product coefficients violate pairwise submodularity and block direct graph-cut representation, potentially creating half-integral roof-dual labels.
knowledge_statements.title: Non-Submodular Interaction Barrier

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Optimality Conditions for Unconstrained Binary Quadratic Problems p. 38

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary for removing non-submodular pair signs by complementing binary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=c+\sum_i a_i x_i+\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}b_{ij}x_ix_j\), where \(b_{ij}\ne0\). For \(s\in\{0,1\}^n\), substitute \(x_i=y_i\) if \(s_i=0\) and \(x_i=1-y_i\) if \(s_i=1\). The transformed pair coefficient is \(b'_{ij}=(-1)^{s_i+s_j}b_{ij}\). A complementation satisfying \(b'_{ij}<0\) for every edge exists if and only if every cycle of the interaction graph contains an even number of edges with \(b_{ij}>0\). If this condition fails, no variable complementation removes every non-submodular interaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All positive pair signs can be removed by complementing variables exactly when every interaction-graph cycle has an even number of positive edges.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is a quadratic pseudo-Boolean minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists s\;\forall\{i,j\}\in E:\;(-1)^{s_i+s_j}b_{ij}<0\iff\text{every cycle contains an even number of positive }b_{ij}.\)

notation.meaning: indicator that variable i is complemented

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Complementation Switching Criterion

assumptions_latex: \(q_1(x,z^1)\) and \(q_2(x,z^2)\) are exact quadratizations of the same pseudo-Boolean function \(f\).
Each quadratization is subjected to its own quadratic roof relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistency is representation invariant only under an additional equivalence condition on the induced projected relaxations; exact quadratization alone is insufficient.

notation.meaning: Original coordinates labeled persistently by the relaxation of quadratization k.
Quadratic extensions of the common objective.

review_flags: existence of strict examples and exact invariance criteria require a dedicated source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of representation-invariant persistency across exact quadratizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Exactness gives
\[
f(x)=\min_{z^1\in\{0,1\}}q_1(x,z^1)=\min_{z^2\in\{0,1\}}q_2(x,z^2)
\]
for binary \(x\), but it imposes no equality between the two roof-relaxed extensions. Therefore the sets \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) of persistently labeled original coordinates need not be inferred to coincide. Equality \(P_1=P_2\) is justified when the projected roof-relaxed value functions, together with the relevant persistency certificates, coincide. Thus persistency obtained after quadratization is a property of the objective-plus-extension unless representation invariance is established separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact quadratizations can induce different persistent labels after roof relaxation; invariance requires equivalence of the projected relaxations and their certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratization-Dependent Persistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but exact binary quadratization alone only establishes the common binary value function. The stronger assertion that roof-relaxed persistent-label sets can differ, and the proposed condition involving coincident persistency certificates, require a dedicated source and a precise certificate convention.

children.title: Linear-Programming Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Continuous relaxations obtained from binary linear formulations.

assumptions_latex: The objective is \(c^\top x\), and minimization is intended.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm{LP}}\le v_{\mathrm{IP}}\); equality holds when the LP has an optimal binary solution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous LP relaxation of a linear binary minimization formulation.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Linear Programming Relaxations p. 27

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The linear-programming relaxation replaces binary restrictions by their convex box constraints:
\[
P:=\{x\in[0,1]^n:Ax\le b\}.
\]
Its value is \(v_{\mathrm{LP}}:=\inf\{c^\top x:x\in P\}\), while the binary value is \(v_{\mathrm{IP}}:=\min\{c^\top x:x\in X\}\). Since \(X\subseteq P\),
\[
v_{\mathrm{LP}}\le v_{\mathrm{IP}}.
\]
The relaxation is exact for this instance and objective when it possesses a binary optimum, in which case \(v_{\mathrm{LP}}=v_{\mathrm{IP}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An LP relaxation replaces binary variables by values in the unit box while retaining linear constraints, giving a lower bound for minimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Programming Relaxations

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2 Linear Programming Relaxations p. 27

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial-Time Solvability of Rational LP Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoding-sensitive complexity distinction between the continuous relaxation and its binary source problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For rational \(A,b,c\), the relaxation \[\min\{c^Tx:Ax\le b,\ 0\le x\le1\}\] can be solved, or certified infeasible, in time polynomial in the row and column counts and the binary encoding length of \((A,b,c)\) by a polynomial-time linear-programming algorithm. This does not imply polynomial-time solvability of the associated binary problem or a polynomial bound on simplex pivots.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rational LP relaxations are polynomial-time solvable in input bit length, without implying tractability of the binary problem or polynomial simplex pivot counts.
assumptions_latex: All LP data are rational and explicitly encoded.
Complexity is measured in the standard bit model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: LP-relaxation optimization and infeasibility detection are polynomial in rational input encoding length.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial-Time Solvability of Rational LP Relaxations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual lower-bound, optimality, and infeasibility certificates for an LP relaxation in standard equality form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the LP relaxation as \[v_{\mathrm{LP}}=\min\{c^Tx:Gx=h,\ x\ge0\}.\] Every \(y\) satisfying \(G^Ty\le c\) certifies \[h^Ty\le v_{\mathrm{LP}}\le v_{\mathrm{IP}}.\] If primal and dual feasible \(x,y\) satisfy \(c^Tx=h^Ty\), both are LP-optimal. A vector \(y\) with \(G^Ty\le0\) and \(h^Ty>0\) certifies infeasibility of \(Gx=h,\ x\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual-feasible vectors certify lower bounds, matching primal and dual objectives certify LP optimality, and a Farkas vector certifies infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The LP relaxation has been converted to the displayed standard form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual feasibility gives a lower bound, equality certifies LP optimality, and the displayed Farkas condition certifies infeasibility.

notation.meaning: LP dual or Farkas certificate vector.

knowledge_statements.title: LP-Relaxation Dual Certificates

children.title: Structured Combinatorial Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Relaxations exploiting recognizable combinatorial substructures.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) is the feasible set of a binary minimization problem.
A tractable combinatorial family supplies a set \(R\subseteq[0,1]^n\) with \(X\subseteq R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimizing over \(R\) gives a valid lower bound, and integrality of an optimal relaxed solution certifies exactness for the instance.
review_flags: the node does not specify a unique combinatorial family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic relaxation induced by a tractable combinatorial superset or extended formulation.

source_refs.locator: Matrix relaxations in combinatorial optimization p. 483

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A structured combinatorial relaxation is a tractably optimizable set \(R\), possibly represented in an extended space and projected onto \(x\), such that \(X\subseteq R\subseteq[0,1]^n\). For an objective \(f\) defined on \(R\), its relaxed value is
\[
v_R:=\inf_{x\in R}f(x).
\]
Consequently,
\[
v_R\le\min_{x\in X}f(x).
\]
The structure may arise from flows, matchings, cuts, matroids, dynamic programs, or another specified tractable family. If an optimizer \(\bar x\in R\) also lies in \(X\), then \(\bar x\) is optimal for the original problem and the relaxation is exact for that instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured combinatorial relaxation optimizes over a tractable superset derived from problem structure, yielding a lower bound and becoming exact when an optimal relaxed point is feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Structured Combinatorial Relaxations

source_witnesses.locator: Matrix relaxations in combinatorial optimization p. 483

children.title: LP–Combinatorial Strength Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Dominance and incomparability between linear-programming and combinatorial bounds.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is contained in two relaxation sets \(R_1,R_2\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
Both relaxations minimize the same real-valued objective \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(R_1\subseteq R_2\), then \(v_1\ge v_2\); without set inclusion or another valid dominance map, no universal strength ordering follows.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-inclusion criterion for comparing minimization bounds from LP and combinatorial relaxations.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Fundamental concepts and results on polyhedra, linear inequalities, and linear programming p. 85
source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(k\in\{1,2\}\), let
\[
v_k:=\inf_{x\in R_k}f(x).
\]
If \(R_1\subseteq R_2\), every point feasible for the first relaxation is feasible for the second, and therefore
\[
v_1\ge v_2
\]
for minimization. Thus a smaller relaxation region gives a bound at least as strong. If an LP relaxation and a structured combinatorial relaxation are incomparable by inclusion, either may give the larger value on a particular objective; a universal dominance claim then requires an additional projection, containment, or objective-specific argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, containment orders relaxation strength: the smaller feasible relaxation gives the stronger lower bound. Incomparable regions have no automatic universal ordering.
knowledge_statements.title: LP–Combinatorial Strength Comparisons

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Fundamental concepts and results on polyhedra, linear inequalities, and linear programming p. 85
source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure family showing that incomparable relaxations have no universal strength order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{(0,0)\}\), \[R_1=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(1,0)\},\qquad R_2=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(0,1)\}.\] Neither relaxation contains the other. For \(c_1=(-1,0)\), \[\min_{R_1}c_1^Tx=-1<0=\min_{R_2}c_1^Tx,\] while for \(c_2=(0,-1)\), \[\min_{R_2}c_2^Tx=-1<0=\min_{R_1}c_2^Tx.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each of two incomparable relaxations can be stronger for a different objective, so one observed bound comparison does not establish universal dominance.
assumptions_latex: Strength is measured by linear minimization bounds.
Both regions are valid relaxations of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ordering of the two relaxation values reverses between \(c_1\) and \(c_2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Dependent Reversal for Incomparable Relaxations

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected Strength Comparison for Extended Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison rule when LP and combinatorial relaxations use different auxiliary spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_L\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+p}\) and \(Q_C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+q}\) be extended relaxations of a common set \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and define \[R_L:=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_L),\qquad R_C:=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_C).\] For objectives depending only on \(x\), \[R_L\subseteq R_C\implies \inf_{(x,u)\in Q_L}c^Tx\ge\inf_{(x,v)\in Q_C}c^Tx.\] Equality of the projections gives equal bounds for every such objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extended LP and combinatorial relaxations must be projected into their common variable space before containment and strength are compared.
assumptions_latex: Both projections contain the common original feasible set.
The compared objective depends only on the common variables \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_L)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_C)\) implies that \(Q_L\) gives no weaker minimization bounds for objectives in \(x\).

notation.meaning: Extended LP and combinatorial relaxation regions.
Their projections into the common variable space.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Strength Comparison for Extended Relaxations

children.title: Combinatorial Exactness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Binary problem classes where a structured combinatorial relaxation becomes exact.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), where \(X\) is the original feasible set and \(R\) is a relaxation.
The problem minimizes \(f:R\to\mathbb R\), and both optima are attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation is exact precisely when \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in R}f(x)\cap X\ne\varnothing\); for a bounded polyhedral \(R\) and linear objectives, the condition that every extreme point of \(R\) belongs to \(X\) is sufficient for objective-independent exactness.

notation.meaning: Original feasible set and its relaxation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instancewise exactness and an objective-independent extreme-point regime.

source_refs.locator: Part III. Polyhedra, Linear Inequalities, and Linear Programming p. 83
source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The relaxation is exact for the given instance exactly when
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in R}f(x)\cap X\ne\varnothing.
\]
Under the stated attainment assumptions, this condition is equivalent to
\[
\min_{x\in R}f(x)=\min_{x\in X}f(x).
\]
For a bounded polyhedral relaxation \(R\) and a linear objective, the stronger condition that every extreme point of \(R\) belongs to \(X\) guarantees exactness for every objective vector. Integrality of the extreme points is sufficient only in formulations where every such integral point is also feasible for \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation is exact when it has an optimizer feasible for the original problem. For bounded polyhedral relaxations and linear objectives, exactness for every objective is guaranteed when every extreme point is originally feasible; integrality alone suffices only when those integral points belong to the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Exactness Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: Part III. Polyhedra, Linear Inequalities, and Linear Programming p. 83
source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient geometric condition for a structured convex relaxation to be exact for every linear objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and compact and let \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex with \(X\subseteq R\). Then \[\min_{x\in R}c^Tx=\min_{x\in X}c^Tx\quad\text{for every }c\in\mathbb R^n\] if and only if \[R=\operatorname{conv}(X).\] When \(X\) is finite, this is equivalent to every extreme point of \(R\) belonging to \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact convex combinatorial relaxation is exact for every linear objective exactly when it equals the convex hull of the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Universal linear-objective exactness holds if and only if \(R=\operatorname{conv}(X)\).

notation.meaning: Convex hull of the original feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Independent Exactness Characterization

children.title: Surrogate Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds obtained by replacing multiple constraints with weighted surrogate constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty domain and the original problem minimizes \(f(x)\) subject to \(g_j(x)\le0\) for \(j=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s(\lambda)\le v^*\) for every admissible \(\lambda\), so \(\sup_{\lambda\ge0,\lambda\ne0}s(\lambda)\) is a valid surrogate-dual lower bound.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the surrogate relaxation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative aggregation of minimization constraints into one surrogate constraint.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4. Surrogate Duality Theory p. 97

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}\), define the surrogate relaxation
\[
s(\lambda):=\inf\left\{f(x):x\in X,\ \sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_jg_j(x)\le0\right\}.
\]
Every point satisfying all original inequalities satisfies their nonnegative aggregate. Hence the surrogate feasible set contains the original feasible set and
\[
s(\lambda)\le v^*:=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g_j(x)\le0\ \text{for all }j\}.
\]
The surrogate-dual value \(s^*:=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}}s(\lambda)\) is therefore also a lower bound on \(v^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative multipliers aggregate several constraints into one. Minimizing over the enlarged surrogate feasible set gives a lower bound, improved by maximizing over multipliers.
knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 4. Surrogate Duality Theory p. 97

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificates supplied by a globally solved surrogate relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda\ge0\), \(\lambda\ne0\), let \(S_\lambda=\{x\in X:\lambda^Tg(x)\le0\}\). If \(S_\lambda=\varnothing\), the original feasible set is empty. If \(\bar x\in\arg\min_{x\in S_\lambda}f(x)\) also satisfies \(g(\bar x)\le0\), then \(s(\lambda)=v^*=f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Surrogate infeasibility proves original infeasibility, and an originally feasible surrogate optimizer proves exactness and primal optimality.
assumptions_latex: The surrogate subproblem is solved globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_\lambda=\varnothing\Rightarrow F=\varnothing\), and \(\bar x\in F\cap\arg\min_{S_\lambda}f\Rightarrow s(\lambda)=v^*=f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate Exactness and Infeasibility Certificates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent normalized formulation of surrogate-dual search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}\) and \(\alpha>0\), the surrogate constraints formed by \(\lambda\) and \(\alpha\lambda\) have the same feasible set. Thus \(s(\alpha\lambda)=s(\lambda)\) and \[\sup_{\lambda\ge0,\lambda\ne0}s(\lambda)=\sup\{s(\lambda):\lambda\ge0,\mathbf1^T\lambda=1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive scaling does not change a surrogate relaxation, so multiplier search can be normalized to the simplex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s(\alpha\lambda)=s(\lambda)\), and simplex normalization is lossless.
review_flags: The zero multiplier is excluded because it gives the vacuous inequality.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Scale Normalization of Surrogate Multipliers

children.title: Aggregation Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds arising from structured combinations of binary constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative aggregation of inequalities for a binary minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and consider \(z^*=\min\{f(x):Ax\ge b,\ x\in X\}\). For any \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), the aggregated relaxation retains only \(\lambda^TAx\ge\lambda^Tb\) and has value \[z_{\mathrm{agg}}(\lambda)=\min\{f(x):\lambda^TAx\ge\lambda^Tb,\ x\in X\}.\] Because every feasible point of the original problem satisfies the aggregated inequality, \(z_{\mathrm{agg}}(\lambda)\le z^*\). The best bound over an admissible multiplier set \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R_+^m\) is \(z_{\mathrm{agg}}(\Lambda)=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}z_{\mathrm{agg}}(\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative weighted sum of valid inequalities defines a relaxation whose minimum is a lower bound; optimizing the weights gives the aggregation bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{agg}}(\lambda)\le z^*\) and \(z_{\mathrm{agg}}(\Lambda)\le z^*\).

notation.meaning: Value after aggregating constraints with multiplier λ.

review_flags: Exact aggregation-bound formulation lacks a supplied supporting locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The aggregation-bound definition and inequalities are mathematically precise, but no source and inspectable locator are supplied.

children.title: Lagrangian Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds produced by dualizing selected constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian dual bound for finite binary minimization with inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be nonempty, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) and \(g:X\to\mathbb R^m\), and suppose \(z^*=\min\{f(x):g(x)\le0,\ x\in X\}\) is feasible. For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), define \[q(\lambda)=\min_{x\in X}\bigl(f(x)+\lambda^Tg(x)\bigr).\] The Lagrangian dual value is \[z_{\mathrm{LD}}=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m}q(\lambda).\] Weak duality gives \(q(\lambda)\le z_{\mathrm{LD}}\le z^*\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\). Equality \(z_{\mathrm{LD}}=z^*\) is not asserted without additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible finite binary minimization problem with constraints written as g(x) at most zero, minimizing the Lagrangian at a fixed nonnegative multiplier gives a lower bound, and maximizing these bounds defines the Lagrangian dual value.
assumptions_latex: The primal minimization problem is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(\lambda)\le z_{\mathrm{LD}}\le z^*\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\).

notation.meaning: Lagrangian relaxation value at multiplier λ.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Lagrangian relaxation p. 25

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2 Lagrangian relaxation p. 25

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal Optimality from a Lagrangian Minimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-multiplier certificate closing the Lagrangian duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar\lambda\ge0\) and \(\bar x\in\arg\min_{x\in X}(f(x)+\bar\lambda^Tg(x))\). If \(g(\bar x)\le0\) and \(\bar\lambda^Tg(\bar x)=0\), then \[q(\bar\lambda)=f(\bar x)=z^*=z_{\mathrm{LD}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-feasible Lagrangian minimizer complementary to its multiplier certifies primal optimality and zero duality gap.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) globally minimizes the Lagrangian subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(\bar\lambda)=f(\bar x)=z^*=z_{\mathrm{LD}}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Optimality from a Lagrangian Minimizer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite binary-domain representation of the multiplier value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite nonempty \(X\), \(q(\lambda)=\min_{x\in X}(f(x)+\lambda^Tg(x))\) is finite-valued, concave, continuous, and piecewise affine on \(\mathbb R_+^m\). If \(x_\lambda\) minimizes the subproblem, then \[q(\mu)\le q(\lambda)+g(x_\lambda)^T(\mu-\lambda)\quad(\mu\ge0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The finite-domain Lagrangian value is concave and piecewise affine, and a minimizing solution's violation vector is a supergradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\) is finite, concave, continuous, and piecewise affine, with \(g(x_\lambda)\in\partial^+q(\lambda)\).

notation.meaning: A Lagrangian-subproblem minimizer at multiplier λ.

knowledge_statements.title: Concave Polyhedral Lagrangian Value Function

children.title: Bound-Dominance Relations
children.top_down_role: Relative strength and equivalence among surrogate, aggregation, and Lagrangian bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Dominance Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance induced by nesting admissible multiplier sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the Lagrangian function \(q(\lambda)=\min_{x\in X}(f(x)+\lambda^Tg(x))\), let \(D(\Lambda)=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)\). If \(\Lambda_1\subseteq\Lambda_2\subseteq\mathbb R_+^m\), then \[D(\Lambda_1)\le D(\Lambda_2)\le z^*.\] Thus the bound obtained from the larger multiplier family dominates the restricted-family bound for a minimization problem. In particular, every fixed-multiplier value satisfies \(q(\bar\lambda)\le D(\Lambda_2)\) whenever \(\bar\lambda\in\Lambda_2\). No ordering follows solely from the names of two relaxation families when their multiplier domains or retained constraints are not nested.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enlarging the admissible multiplier set cannot weaken a Lagrangian lower bound; unrelated relaxation families need not be comparable.
assumptions_latex: The primal problem and \(q\) use the minimization convention of Lagrangian relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(\Lambda_1)\le D(\Lambda_2)\le z^*\).

notation.meaning: Best Lagrangian bound over multiplier set Λ.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.3 Continuous bound versus Lagrangian bound p. 26

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.3 Continuous bound versus Lagrangian bound p. 26

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite binary-domain example showing strict surrogate dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{0,1\}\), with \((f(0),g(0))=(1,-1)\) and \((f(1),g(1))=(0,1)\). The constrained optimum and every positive-multiplier surrogate value equal \(1\), whereas \(q(\mu)=\min\{1-\mu,\mu\}\) has supremum \(1/2\) over \(\mu\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-point binary instance has an exact surrogate bound and a strictly weaker Lagrangian dual bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{LD}}=1/2<1=z_{\mathrm{SD}}=v^*\).
review_flags: Direct finite calculation; no external locator supplied.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Surrogate–Lagrangian Dominance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Surrogate-Dual Dominance over the Lagrangian Dual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of unrestricted surrogate and Lagrangian dual bounds formed from the same finite-domain inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite and nonempty, \(v^*=\min\{f(x):g(x)\le0,\ x\in X\}\), \(q(\mu)=\min_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\mu^Tg(x)\}\), and \(s(\lambda)=\min\{f(x):x\in X,\lambda^Tg(x)\le0\}\). Then \[\sup_{\mu\ge0}q(\mu)\le\sup_{\lambda\ge0,\lambda\ne0}s(\lambda)\le v^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a common inequality system, the optimized surrogate bound is never weaker than the optimized Lagrangian bound.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a feasible minimization problem with \(g(x)\le0\).
Both constructions use their full nonnegative multiplier domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{LD}}\le z_{\mathrm{SD}}\le v^*\).
knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate-Dual Dominance over the Lagrangian Dual

children.title: Multiplier-Restricted Regimes
children.top_down_role: Effects of multiplier restrictions on attainable bound quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Restricted Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of sign, support, or structural restrictions on Lagrangian multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q:\mathbb R_+^m\to\mathbb R\) be the Lagrangian value function and let \(\Lambda_R\subseteq\mathbb R_+^m\) impose prescribed restrictions, such as fixed zero coordinates, blockwise equality, or membership in a finite-dimensional parameterized cone. Define \[z_R=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda_R}q(\lambda),\qquad z_{\mathrm{LD}}=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m}q(\lambda).\] Then \(z_R\le z_{\mathrm{LD}}\le z^*\). If \(\Lambda_R\subseteq\Lambda_S\), then \(z_R\le z_S\). The restriction is lossless exactly when \(\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda_R}q(\lambda)=z_{\mathrm{LD}}\), whether or not either supremum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting admissible multipliers preserves validity but can weaken the best lower bound; nested restrictions induce a corresponding bound ordering.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) is the value function of a valid Lagrangian relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_R\le z_{\mathrm{LD}}\le z^*\), with equality in the first relation exactly for a lossless restriction.

notation.meaning: Best bound within the restricted regime.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure of weak duality outside the admissible multiplier orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the retained binary domain be \(X=\{0\}\), minimize \(f(x)=0\), and impose \(g(x)=x-1\le0\). The primal optimum is \(z^*=0\). For the inadmissible multiplier \(\lambda=-1\), \[q(-1)=\min_{x\in X}\{f(x)-g(x)\}=1>z^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative multiplier for a less-than-or-equal minimization constraint can make the Lagrangian value exceed the primal optimum.

children.title: Copying-Constraint Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds based on replicated variables or constraints linked through consistency structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Copying-Constraint Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bounds obtained by duplicating shared binary variables and relaxing consistency equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k=1,\ldots,K\), let \(\mathcal X_k\) be a nonempty finite set of local binary pairs \((x^k,y^k)\), where every \(y^k\) is a conformable copy of the same shared binary vector, and let \(f_k:\mathcal X_k\to\mathbb R\). Define \[z^*=\min\left\{\sum_{k=1}^K f_k(x^k,y^k):(x^k,y^k)\in\mathcal X_k,\ y^k=y^1\ \text{for }k=2,\ldots,K\right\}.\] For \(C\subseteq\{2,\ldots,K\}\), let \(z_C\) be the value obtained by removing the equalities \(y^k=y^1\) indexed by \(k\in C\). Then \(z_C\le z^*\). If \(C_1\subseteq C_2\), then \(z_{C_1}\ge z_{C_2}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Removing specified consistency equations between conformable binary copies defines a relaxation and a lower bound; removing additional equations cannot increase that lower bound.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\mathcal X_k\) is nonempty and finite.
All \(y^k\) are conformable copies of the same shared binary vector.
The fully consistent copied formulation is feasible.
The objective is additive across blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_C\le z^*\), and \(C_1\subseteq C_2\) implies \(z_{C_1}\ge z_{C_2}\).

notation.meaning: Block k's copy of the shared binary vector.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Connected-Component Decomposition of Retained Copy Links
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural representation of a copied relaxation retaining an arbitrary graph of pairwise consistency equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) index local blocks \((x^k,y^k)\in\mathcal X_k\), and retain equations \(y^i=y^j\) for \(ij\in E'\subseteq E\). If \(C_1,\ldots,C_r\) are the connected components of \((V,E')\), then copies agree within each component and remain unrelated across components. Consequently, \[z_{E'}=\sum_{\ell=1}^r\min\left\{\sum_{k\in C_\ell}f_k(x^k,y^k):(x^k,y^k)\in\mathcal X_k,\ y^i=y^j\ \forall i,j\in C_\ell\right\}.\] If \(E'=\varnothing\), then \(z_{E'}=\sum_k\min_{(x^k,y^k)\in\mathcal X_k}f_k(x^k,y^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A copied relaxation separates exactly over connected components of its retained consistency graph; deleting all links gives independent block minima.
assumptions_latex: The objective is additive across blocks.
Copies joined by retained links are conformable.
Every local block set is nonempty and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxed value is the sum of the componentwise consistent subproblem values.

notation.meaning: Connected components of the retained-link graph.

knowledge_statements.title: Connected-Component Decomposition of Retained Copy Links

children.title: Binary-Decomposition Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds obtained by decomposing binary structure into coordinated subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Binary-Decomposition Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable lower bounds produced after relaxing couplings among binary blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\in\mathbb N\), let \(X_k\subseteq\{0,1\}^{n_k}\) be nonempty, let \(f_k:X_k\to\mathbb R\), let \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{p\times n_k}\), and let \(b\in\mathbb R^p\). Suppose the problem \[z^*=\min\left\{\sum_{k=1}^K f_k(x^k):x^k\in X_k,\ \sum_{k=1}^K A_kx^k=b\right\}\] is feasible. For \(\pi\in\mathbb R^p\), define \[q(\pi)=-\pi^Tb+\sum_{k=1}^K\min_{x^k\in X_k}\bigl(f_k(x^k)+\pi^TA_kx^k\bigr)\] and \[z_D=\sup_{\pi\in\mathbb R^p}q(\pi).\] Then \(q(\pi)\le z_D\le z^*\) for every \(\pi\in\mathbb R^p\), and each \(q(\pi)\) is evaluated through independent block subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing equality constraints that couple finite binary blocks produces independent block subproblems; their optimized Lagrangian value is a lower bound on the coupled minimization problem.
assumptions_latex: The coupled minimization problem is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(\pi)\le z_D\le z^*\) for every \(\pi\in\mathbb R^p\).

source_refs.locator: 3.6.1 General Lagrangian decomposition schemes p. 88

source_witnesses.locator: 3.6.1 General Lagrangian decomposition schemes p. 88

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-iterate convergence for maximizing the decomposition bound on a bounded-distance multiplier region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Pi\) be nonempty, closed, and convex and contain a maximizer \(\pi^*\) of \(q\). Suppose \(\|\pi^0-\pi^*\|\le D\) and selected supergradients satisfy \(\|s(\pi^t)\|\le G\). With \[\pi^{t+1}=\operatorname{proj}_{\Pi}(\pi^t+\alpha s(\pi^t)),\qquad \alpha=\frac{D}{G\sqrt T},\] one has \[q(\pi^*)-\max_{0\le t<T}q(\pi^t)\le\frac{DG}{\sqrt T}.\] Each iteration solves the independent block subproblems and projects the multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected supergradient ascent has an O(T^{-1/2}) best-iterate dual-value guarantee under bounded distance and residual assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and contains a maximizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(\pi^*)-\max_{0\le t<T}q(\pi^t)\le DG/\sqrt T\).
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Supergradient Bound Optimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural characterization of the finite-block decomposition-dual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[q(\pi)=-\pi^Tb+\sum_{k=1}^K\min_{x\in X_k}\bigl(f_k(x)+\pi^TA_kx\bigr),\] where every \(X_k\) is nonempty and finite, \(q\) is finite-valued, concave, and polyhedral. If \(x^k(\pi)\) minimizes block \(k\), then \[s(\pi):=\sum_{k=1}^KA_kx^k(\pi)-b\] is a supergradient of \(q\) at \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The decomposition-dual value is a finite concave piecewise-linear function, and the coupling residual of optimal block solutions is a supergradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(\pi')\le q(\pi)+s(\pi)^T(\pi'-\pi)\) for every \(\pi'\).

notation.meaning: Coupling residual and supergradient at multiplier \(\pi\).

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Concavity and Supergradients

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal representation of the optimized finite-block decomposition bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(S_k:=\{(A_kx,f_k(x)):x\in X_k\}\). Under the seed assumptions, \[z_D=\min\left\{\sum_{k=1}^K\eta_k:(u_k,\eta_k)\in\operatorname{conv}(S_k),\ \sum_{k=1}^Ku_k=b\right\}.\] Equivalently, \[z_D=\min\left\{\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{x\in X_k}\lambda_{kx}f_k(x):\sum_{x\in X_k}\lambda_{kx}=1,\ \lambda_{kx}\ge0,\ \sum_{k,x}\lambda_{kx}A_kx=b\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The best finite-block decomposition bound equals a linear master problem that convexifies each block separately and enforces the coupling equation in aggregate.
assumptions_latex: The original coupled problem is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_D\) equals the optimum of the displayed blockwise-convexified master.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexified-Master Representation

children.title: Copying–Decomposition Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Relationship between replicated representations and decomposed binary models.

knowledge_statements.title: Copying–Decomposition Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between dualized copy consistency and a separable decomposition dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k=1,\ldots,K\), let \(\mathcal X_k\) be a nonempty finite set of local pairs \((x^k,y^k)\), where the vectors \(y^k\) are conformable copies, and let \(f_k:\mathcal X_k\to\mathbb R\). Attach unrestricted multipliers \(\pi^k\) to the consensus equations \(y^k-y^1=0\) for \(k=2,\ldots,K\), and define \[q_{\mathrm{copy}}(\pi^2,\ldots,\pi^K)=\min_{(x^k,y^k)\in\mathcal X_k}\left[\sum_{k=1}^K f_k(x^k,y^k)+\sum_{k=2}^K(\pi^k)^T(y^k-y^1)\right].\] For each \(k\), define \[q_k(\mu^k)=\min_{(x^k,y^k)\in\mathcal X_k}\bigl(f_k(x^k,y^k)+(\mu^k)^Ty^k\bigr).\] The copying dual and zero-sum decomposition dual have the same value: \[\sup_{\pi^2,\ldots,\pi^K}q_{\mathrm{copy}}(\pi^2,\ldots,\pi^K)=\sup_{\substack{\mu^1,\ldots,\mu^K\\\sum_{k=1}^K\mu^k=0}}\sum_{k=1}^Kq_k(\mu^k).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing consensus equations among conformable variable copies gives the same bound as maximizing the sum of blockwise Lagrangian values over zero-sum copy multipliers.
assumptions_latex: All blocks use conformable copies of the same shared binary vector.
Copy consistency is expressed by equality constraints.
Each \(\mathcal X_k\) is nonempty and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{\pi^2,\ldots,\pi^K}q_{\mathrm{copy}}(\pi^2,\ldots,\pi^K)=\sup_{\sum_{k=1}^K\mu^k=0}\sum_{k=1}^Kq_k(\mu^k)\).

notation.meaning: Lagrangian value obtained by dualizing the displayed consensus equations.
Zero-sum decomposition multiplier for block k's shared-variable copy.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incidence-matrix variant of the star-consensus copying–decomposition correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an oriented graph \(G=(V,E)\) index conformable copies \(y^k\), let \(B\) be its node-edge incidence matrix, and write consensus as \((B^T\otimes I)y=0\). Dualizing with edge multipliers \(\lambda\) induces node coefficients \[\mu=(B\otimes I)\lambda.\] If \(G\) is connected, \[\operatorname{im}(B\otimes I)=\left\{(\mu^k)_{k\in V}:\sum_{k\in V}\mu^k=0\right\}.\] Thus maximizing the edge-multiplier copying dual equals maximizing the sum of block Lagrangian values over zero-sum node multipliers. If \(G\) is disconnected, the zero-sum condition holds separately on each connected component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Edge prices on a connected consistency graph generate exactly the zero-sum block multipliers; disconnected graphs impose one zero-sum condition per component.
assumptions_latex: The graph is given an arbitrary orientation.
Every local block set is nonempty and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For connected \(G\), \(\operatorname{im}(B\otimes I)=\{\mu:\sum_k\mu^k=0\}\), so the two dual parametrizations have equal value.
knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Consensus Multiplier Correspondence

children.title: Consistency-Relaxation Gaps
children.top_down_role: Bound losses caused by relaxing links among copied or decomposed components.

knowledge_statements.title: Consistency-Relaxation Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value loss caused by removing agreement constraints between binary copies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq F_R\) be nonempty finite feasible sets for a copied binary minimization problem, where \(F\) enforces all consistency equations and \(F_R\) relaxes some or all of them. For a common objective \(f:F_R\to\mathbb R\), define \[z^*=\min_{u\in F}f(u),\qquad z_R=\min_{u\in F_R}f(u),\qquad \Delta_R=z^*-z_R.\] Then \(\Delta_R\ge0\), and \[\Delta_R=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in F_R}f(u)\cap F\ne\varnothing.\] Equivalently, \(\Delta_R>0\) exactly when every optimizer over \(F_R\) is inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The consistency-relaxation gap is the nonnegative difference between the fully consistent and relaxed minima; it is zero exactly when the relaxed problem has a consistent optimizer.
assumptions_latex: Both problems use the same objective \(f:F_R\to\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_R\ge0\), and \(\Delta_R=0\iff\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in F_R}f(u)\cap F\ne\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure family showing that binary consensus structure alone gives no uniform additive-gap bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(M>0\), let \(y^1,y^2\in\{0,1\}\), impose \(y^1=y^2\), and minimize \[f_M(y^1,y^2)=My^1+M(1-y^2).\] The consistent value is \(M\), whereas removing the equality permits \((y^1,y^2)=(0,1)\) with value \(0\). Hence \(\Delta_R=M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-copy binary family has arbitrary additive consistency gap, so consensus structure alone yields no uniform additive bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering of value loss under nested consistency relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq F_{R_1}\subseteq F_{R_2}\) be nonempty finite feasible sets with common objective \(f\), and define \[\Delta_{R_i}:=\min_{u\in F}f(u)-\min_{u\in F_{R_i}}f(u).\] Then \[0\le\Delta_{R_1}\le\Delta_{R_2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Removing additional consistency equations cannot decrease the consistency-relaxation gap.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq F_{R_1}\subseteq F_{R_2}\) are nonempty and finite.
All problems use the same objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le\Delta_{R_1}\le\Delta_{R_2}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Max-Cut Semidefinite Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard elliptope upper bound for weighted maximum cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and edge weights \(w_{ij}\ge0\). For \(y\in\{-1,1\}^n\), define the encoded cut weight by \[W(y)=\frac14\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-y_iy_j),\qquad z_{\mathrm{MC}}=\max_{y\in\{-1,1\}^n}W(y).\] The elliptope semidefinite bound is \[z_{\mathrm{SDP}}=\max\left\{\frac14\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-X_{ij}):X\succeq0,\ X_{ii}=1\ \text{for }i=1,\ldots,n\right\}.\] It satisfies \(z_{\mathrm{MC}}\le z_{\mathrm{SDP}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The elliptope semidefinite relaxation replaces products of cut signs by entries of a positive-semidefinite unit-diagonal matrix and gives an upper bound on weighted maximum cut.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{MC}}\le z_{\mathrm{SDP}}\).

notation.meaning: Sign vector encoding the two sides of a cut.
Positive-semidefinite surrogate for the cut sign-product matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Goemans–Williamson rounding of a feasible Max-Cut SDP Gram representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given feasible unit vectors \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\), choose a uniformly random hyperplane through the origin and place vertices on shores according to the signs of their projections onto its normal. If \(\theta_{ij}=\arccos(v_i^\top v_j)\), then \(\Pr[i\text{ and }j\text{ are separated}]=\theta_{ij}/\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random origin-centered hyperplane separates an edge with probability equal to its angular distance divided by pi.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr[i\text{ and }j\text{ are separated}]=\frac{\arccos(v_i^\top v_j)}{\pi},

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual feasibility certificate for an elliptope maximization objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the SDP objective as \(\langle C,X\rangle+\kappa\). Its dual is \[\min\{\mathbf1^\top u+\kappa:\operatorname{Diag}(u)-C\succeq0\}.\] Therefore every \(u\) satisfying \(\operatorname{Diag}(u)-C\succeq0\) certifies \(z_{\mathrm{MC}}\le z_{\mathrm{SDP}}\le\mathbf1^\top u+\kappa\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any feasible diagonal dual vector gives a checkable upper bound on the maximum cut value.
assumptions_latex: \(C\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(\kappa\in\mathbb R\) encode the chosen objective normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Diag}(u)-C\succeq0\Longrightarrow z_{\mathrm{MC}}\le\mathbf1^\top u+\kappa,

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relation between the seed objective and conventional cut weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a cut sign vector \(y\), the conventional contribution of an unordered edge \(\{i,j\}\) is \((1-y_i y_j)/2\). Consequently \(\frac14\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(1-y_i y_j)\) is one half of the conventional weighted cut value; multiplying both the integer and SDP objectives by two restores the conventional normalization without changing optimizers or approximation ratios.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With each unordered edge counted once, the seed's factor one quarter scales both the cut and SDP values by one half.
assumptions_latex: Each unordered edge is included once in the sum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W_{\mathrm{seed}}(y)=\frac12W_{\mathrm{conventional}}(y),

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gram-Vector Form of the Max-Cut SDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent vector representation of the elliptope relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symmetric matrix \(X\) satisfies \(X\succeq0\) and \(X_{ii}=1\) for all \(i\) if and only if there are unit vectors \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\) with \(X_{ij}=v_i^\top v_j\). Thus the Max-Cut SDP equivalently replaces each sign product \(y_i y_j\) by an inner product of unit vectors.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected guarantee for nonnegative weighted Max-Cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonnegative edge weights, random-hyperplane rounding of an optimal elliptope solution returns a cut \(C\) satisfying \[\mathbb E[W(C)]\ge\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}z_{\mathrm{SDP}}\ge\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}z_{\mathrm{MC}},\qquad \alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}=\min_{0\le\theta\le\pi}\frac{2\theta}{\pi(1-\cos\theta)}>0.87856.\] The statement is invariant under a common positive rescaling of the cut and SDP objectives.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Max-Cut quadratic formulation and semidefinite relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted Max-Cut represented as a sign-constrained quadratic program and relaxed by omitting the rank-one condition from its matrix lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\), \(n=|V|\), and \(w\in\mathbb{Q}_+^E\). The weighted Max-Cut value is
\[
z_I:=\max_{x\in\{-1,+1\}^n}\frac12\sum_{ij\in E}w_{ij}(1-x_ix_j).
\]
For every feasible \(x\), the matrix \(Y=xx^T\) satisfies \(Y\succeq0\), \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)=1\), and \(y_{jj}=1\). Dropping the rank-one condition yields
\[
z_{\mathrm{sdp}}:=\max\left\{\frac12\sum_{ij\in E}w_{ij}(1-y_{ij}):y_{jj}=1\ (j=1,\ldots,n),\ Y\succeq0\right\}.
\]
Thus \(z_{\mathrm{sdp}}\ge z_I\). This SDP and its dual have strictly feasible solutions and attain their optima, and \(z_{\mathrm{sdp}}\) can be computed in polynomial time to any prescribed precision by interior-point methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted Max-Cut is a quadratic optimization problem over sign vectors. Lifting a sign vector to xxᵀ and omitting the rank-one constraint gives a semidefinite relaxation whose optimum upper-bounds the maximum cut value. The primal and dual are strictly feasible and attain their optima, and the bound can be computed in polynomial time to any prescribed precision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_{\mathrm{sdp}}\ge z_I

knowledge_statements.title: QUBO Semidefinite Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order lifted semidefinite lower bound for unconstrained binary quadratic minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), let \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and replace \(Q\) by its symmetric part if necessary. Consider \[z^*=\min\{x^TQx+c^Tx:x\in\{0,1\}^n\}.\] For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(X\in\mathbb S^n\), define the lifted semidefinite bound \[z_{\mathrm{QSDP}}=\min\left\{\langle Q,X\rangle+c^Tx:\operatorname{diag}(X)=x,\ \begin{pmatrix}1&x^T\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\right\}.\] Then \(z_{\mathrm{QSDP}}\le z^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The first-order lifted semidefinite relaxation replaces binary quadratic products by a moment matrix, drops the rank-one condition, and gives a lower bound for QUBO minimization.
assumptions_latex: The QUBO uses the minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{QSDP}}\le z^*\).

notation.meaning: Lifted symmetric surrogate for the binary product matrix.
Trace inner product of Q and X.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank condition certifying recovery of an optimal binary QUBO point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible moment matrix \(M=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\), \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=1\) if and only if \(X=xx^\top\) and \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\). If an optimal SDP solution has rank one, then its vector \(x\) is QUBO-optimal and \(z_{\mathrm{QSDP}}=z^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-one optimal moment matrix certifies exactness and directly yields an optimal binary vector.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is feasible for the QUBO SDP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ optimal},\ \operatorname{rank}(M)=1\Longrightarrow x\in\{0,1\}^n,\ z_{\mathrm{QSDP}}=z^*,
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Exactness Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual lower-bound certificate for the first-order minimizing QUBO SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\begin{pmatrix}0&c^\top/2\\c/2&Q\end{pmatrix}\), \(A_0=E_{00}\), and \(A_i=E_{ii}-(E_{0i}+E_{i0})/2\). The moment SDP equals \(\min\{\langle C,M\rangle:\langle A_0,M\rangle=1,\ \langle A_i,M\rangle=0,\ M\succeq0\}\). Every \((\alpha,\beta)\) satisfying \(C-\alpha A_0-\sum_i\beta_iA_i\succeq0\) certifies the lower bound \(\alpha\le z_{\mathrm{QSDP}}\le z^*\); strict primal feasibility ensures equality with the corresponding dual optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite dual slack supplies a checkable lower bound for QUBO minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C-\alpha A_0-\sum_i\beta_iA_i\succeq0\Longrightarrow \alpha\le z_{\mathrm{QSDP}}\le z^*,

notation.meaning: Symmetric matrix-unit notation in the homogenized space.
Dual multipliers for the normalization and binary diagonal identities.

knowledge_statements.title: QUBO Moment-SDP Dual Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-posedness of the unconstrained first-order QUBO relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The feasible moment region is nonempty and compact. Indeed, \(0\le x_i=X_{ii}\le1\) and positive semidefiniteness gives \(|X_{ij}|\le\sqrt{x_i x_j}\le1\). Consequently every finite linear objective \(\langle Q,X\rangle+c^\top x\) attains a finite minimum.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact objective and moment-matrix transfer under binary/sign coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(y=\mathbf1-2x\), and \(M_x=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^\top\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\). For every unordered edge, \[\frac{1-y_i y_j}{2}=x_i+x_j-2x_i x_j.\] Thus conventional weighted Max-Cut equals the corresponding maximizing QUBO. With \(T=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\\mathbf1&-2I\end{pmatrix}\), the homogenized sign lift is \(M_y=T M_xT^\top\). Because \(T\) is invertible, \(M_x\succeq0\) if and only if \(M_y\succeq0\), and \(\operatorname{diag}(X)=x\) corresponds exactly to unit diagonal in the sign-correlation block. Hence the two unstrengthened first-order SDP relaxations have equal objective values after the same affine objective transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The binary/sign substitution converts conventional weighted Max-Cut exactly to a QUBO and gives an invertible congruence between their standard first-order semidefinite lifts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine transfer between weighted Max-Cut and binary quadratic formulations and their lifted bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) encode a cut and set \(y=\mathbf1-2x\). For each edge, \(\frac14(1-y_iy_j)=x_i+x_j-2x_ix_j\); hence weighted Max-Cut equals maximization of the QUBO \[\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(x_i+x_j-2x_ix_j).\] Under the lifted affine transformation induced by \(y=\mathbf1-2x\), rank-one matrices and their positive-semidefinite relaxations map to one another by congruence. Consequently an upper bound for the maximization QUBO transfers, with the same objective value, to an upper bound for the corresponding Max-Cut instance, and conversely.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper half of the Lovász sandwich theorem for stable-set theta.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every finite simple graph \(G\), the Lovász theta number satisfies \[\vartheta(G)\le\chi(\overline G),\] where \(\chi(\overline G)\) is the chromatic number of the complement, equivalently the minimum number of cliques covering \(V(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The theta number is no larger than the clique-cover number, equivalently the chromatic number of the complement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-optimization complexity of evaluating the graph theta SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite graph \(G\) and rational \(\varepsilon>0\), standard weak semidefinite-optimization algorithms approximate the trace-normalized theta value to additive error at most \(\varepsilon\) in time polynomial in the graph encoding length and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\), under the rational-data bit model and the usual weak-feasibility convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Semidefinite Form of the Theta Number
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual of the trace-normalized stable-set theta formulation and its bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\), let \(J\) be the all-ones matrix, and use the trace-normalized primal theta convention. Then \[\vartheta(G)=\min\{t:tI+Z-J\succeq0,\ Z_{ii}=0,\ Z_{ij}=0\text{ whenever }\{i,j\}\notin E\},\] where \(Z\) is symmetric and otherwise unrestricted on edges. Every primal-feasible \(X\) and dual-feasible \((t,Z)\) satisfy \(\langle J,X\rangle\le\vartheta(G)\le t\); matching values certify optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The trace-normalized theta SDP has an edge-supported matrix dual whose feasible solutions certify upper bounds.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is a finite simple graph}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \vartheta(G)=\min\{t:tI+Z-J\succeq0,\ Z\text{ is supported on }E\}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural behavior under edge addition in the trace-normalized convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E_G)\) and \(H=(V,E_H)\) be finite simple graphs on the same nonempty vertex set with \(E_G\subseteq E_H\). Every theta-primal matrix feasible for \(H\) is feasible for \(G\), so \[\vartheta(H)\le\vartheta(G).\] For \(|V|=n\), \(\vartheta(K_n)=1\) and \(\vartheta(\overline K_n)=n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding edges cannot increase the stable-set theta bound; complete and empty graphs have theta values one and n.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) and \(H\) are finite simple graphs on the same nonempty vertex set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \vartheta(H)\le\vartheta(G),\qquad\vartheta(K_n)=1,\quad\vartheta(\overline K_n)=n.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative vertex-weight variant of the trace-normalized theta SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\), let \(w\in\mathbb R_+^V\), and put \(s_i=\sqrt{w_i}\). Define \[\vartheta(G;w)=\max\{\langle ss^\top,X\rangle:\operatorname{Tr}(X)=1,\ X_{ij}=0\ \forall\{i,j\}\in E,\ X\succeq0\}.\] For every nonempty stable set \(S\) of positive total weight, set \(u_i=\sqrt{w_i}/\sqrt{\sum_{j\in S}w_j}\) on \(S\) and zero elsewhere. Then \(X=uu^\top\) is feasible with objective \(\sum_{i\in S}w_i\). Consequently \(\alpha(G;w)\le\vartheta(G;w)\). For \(w=\mathbf1\), this reduces to the ordinary trace-normalized theta bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing the all-ones objective by the outer product of square-root vertex weights gives an SDP upper bound on maximum stable-set weight.
assumptions_latex: G=(V,E)\text{ is a finite simple graph}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha(G;w)\le\vartheta(G;w)

notation.meaning: Vector of square roots of the vertex weights.
Maximum total weight of a stable set.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Stable-Set Theta Bound
Stable-Set Theta Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lovász theta semidefinite upper bound on the stability number.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite simple graph \(G=(V,E)\), let \(\alpha(G)\) be its maximum stable-set cardinality. Define \[\vartheta(G)=\max\{\langle J,X\rangle:\operatorname{Tr}(X)=1,\ X_{ij}=0\ \text{for all }\{i,j\}\in E,\ X\succeq0\}.\] If \(S\subseteq V\) is a nonempty stable set and \(u=\mathbf1_S/\sqrt{|S|}\), then \(X=uu^T\) is feasible and \(\langle J,X\rangle=|S|\). Taking a maximum-cardinality stable set therefore gives \(\alpha(G)\le\vartheta(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trace-normalized positive-semidefinite matrix with zeros on graph edges defines the Lovász theta upper bound on stable-set size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha(G)\le\vartheta(G)\).

notation.meaning: Maximum cardinality of a stable set in G.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Absence of a Universal Cross-Tier Order
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incomparability of projected relaxations under different objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=\{(0,0)\}\), the valid relaxations \(R_1=[0,1]\times\{0\}\) and \(R_2=\{0\}\times[0,1]\) are incomparable.
