Thus tier labels or formulation size alone cannot induce a universal strength order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incomparable relaxation regions can each give the stronger bound for a different objective.
assumptions_latex: Relaxations are projected into the same variable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_1\nsubseteq R_2,\quad R_2\nsubseteq R_1,
knowledge_statements.title: Absence of a Universal Cross-Tier Order

children.title: Spectral Eigenvalue Bounds
children.top_down_role: Binary bounds derived from eigenvalue structure and spectral transformations.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^\top Qz\leq n\lambda_{\max}(Q)\), with equality exactly when \(z\) belongs to the top eigenspace of \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rayleigh-quotient bound for an unconstrained sign quadratic problem.

source_refs.locator: 1.3 Preliminaries from linear algebra, matrix theory, and Euclidean geometry p. 4
source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(z\in\{-1,1\}^n\). Since \(z^\top z=n\), the Rayleigh-quotient inequality yields \[z^\top Qz\leq\lambda_{\max}(Q)z^\top z=n\lambda_{\max}(Q).\] Consequently, \(n\lambda_{\max}(Q)\) is an upper bound for \(\max\{z^\top Qz:z\in\{-1,1\}^n\}\). Equality for a particular sign vector holds if and only if that vector lies in the eigenspace associated with \(\lambda_{\max}(Q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sign vector has squared norm n, so the Rayleigh quotient bounds its quadratic value by n times the largest eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Eigenvalue Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3 Preliminaries from linear algebra, matrix theory, and Euclidean geometry p. 4
source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rayleigh-quotient lower bound for an unconstrained sign quadratic problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(z\in\{-1,1\}^n\). Then \[z^\top Qz\ge n\lambda_{\min}(Q).\] Hence \(n\lambda_{\min}(Q)\) lower-bounds \(\min\{z^\top Qz:z\in\{-1,1\}^n\}\), with equality for a sign vector exactly when it lies in the eigenspace of \(\lambda_{\min}(Q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The smallest eigenvalue gives the minimization analogue of the largest-eigenvalue sign-quadratic bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^\top Qz\ge n\lambda_{\min}(Q)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Smallest-Eigenvalue Lower Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eigenvalue-bound family obtained from diagonal identities of sign vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), \(d\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(z\in\{-1,1\}^n\), \[z^\top Qz=z^\top(Q-\operatorname{Diag}d)z+\mathbf1^\top d\le n\lambda_{\max}(Q-\operatorname{Diag}d)+\mathbf1^\top d.\] Consequently, taking the infimum of the right-hand side over \(d\) preserves a valid upper bound on the sign-quadratic maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting a diagonal and restoring its constant value on sign vectors yields an optimizable family of spectral upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{z\in\{-1,1\}^n}z^\top Qz\le\inf_{d\in\mathbb R^n}\{n\lambda_{\max}(Q-\operatorname{Diag}d)+\mathbf1^\top d\}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal-Shift Spectral Bounds

children.title: Semidefinite–Spectral Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Connections between matrix-positive-semidefinite relaxations and eigenvalue-based bounds.

assumptions_latex: The primal semidefinite program is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{\langle Q,X\rangle:X\succeq0,\operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1\}=\min\{\mathbf1^\top y:\operatorname{Diag}(y)-Q\succeq0\}\leq n\lambda_{\max}(Q)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual SDP identity and the constant spectral dual certificate.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 Semidefinite and Lagrangian relaxations p. 55
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), the sign-quadratic semidefinite relaxation and its dual are \[\max\{\langle Q,X\rangle:X\succeq0,\ \operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1\}=\min\{\mathbf1^\top y:\operatorname{Diag}(y)-Q\succeq0\}.\] The primal point \(X=I\) is positive definite, so strong semidefinite duality applies. Taking \(y=\lambda_{\max}(Q)\mathbf1\) is dual feasible because \(\lambda_{\max}(Q)I-Q\succeq0\), and gives the spectral upper bound \(n\lambda_{\max}(Q)\). Thus the eigenvalue bound is a particular dual certificate for the SDP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sign-quadratic SDP has a diagonal dual; assigning every dual coordinate the largest eigenvalue recovers the elementary spectral bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite–Spectral Correspondence

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 Semidefinite and Lagrangian relaxations p. 55
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tightness Certificate for the Scalar Spectral Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complementary-slackness characterization of equality between the SDP and constant spectral certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda=\lambda_{\max}(Q)\). The scalar spectral bound equals the SDP value if and only if there exists \(X\succeq0\) with \(\operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1\) and \((\lambda I-Q)X=0\). Equivalently, a feasible correlation matrix must have its range contained in the top eigenspace of \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The eigenvalue bound is SDP-tight exactly when a unit-diagonal correlation matrix is supported on the top eigenspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_{\mathrm{SDP}}=n\lambda_{\max}(Q)\iff \exists X\succeq0:\operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1,\ (\lambda_{\max}(Q)I-Q)X=0,
knowledge_statements.title: Tightness Certificate for the Scalar Spectral Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Improvement over Scalar Spectral Loading
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Example where optimized diagonal dual loading is strictly stronger.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q=\operatorname{Diag}(1,0)\), every feasible \(X\) with \(\operatorname{diag}(X)=\mathbf1\) satisfies \(\langle Q,X\rangle=1\), so \(z_{\mathrm{SDP}}=1\). Yet \(n\lambda_{\max}(Q)=2\). The optimized dual loading \(y=(1,0)\) is therefore strictly stronger than the constant loading \(y=(1,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-dimensional diagonal example shows that the SDP can strictly improve the elementary largest-eigenvalue bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_{\mathrm{SDP}}=1<2=n\lambda_{\max}(Q),
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Improvement over Scalar Spectral Loading

children.title: Weak-Linking Gaps
children.top_down_role: Relaxation gaps caused by insufficient coupling between binary choices and linked variables.

assumptions_latex: The binary variable \(y\) activates nonnegative variables \(x_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\mathrm{dis}}\subsetneq P_{\mathrm{agg}}\), and the example \(x_1=u_1\), \(x_i=0\) for \(i>1\) permits \(y=u_1/\sum_i u_i<1\) only in the aggregate relaxation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gap caused by replacing componentwise activation links with one aggregate inequality.

source_refs.locator: Generalized disjunctive programming: A framework for formulation and alternative algorithms for MINLP optimization p. 93

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u_i>0\) and relax \(y\in\{0,1\}\) to \(0\leq y\leq1\). The disaggregated links \(x_i\leq u_i y\) define \(P_{\mathrm{dis}}\), whereas the single aggregate link \(\sum_i x_i\leq(\sum_i u_i)y\), together with \(0\leq x_i\leq u_i\), defines \(P_{\mathrm{agg}}\). Summing the disaggregated links proves \(P_{\mathrm{dis}}\subseteq P_{\mathrm{agg}}\). For \(x_1=u_1\) and \(x_i=0\) for \(i>1\), the aggregate relaxation permits \(y=u_1/(\sum_i u_i)<1\), while the disaggregated link forces \(y=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An aggregate activation link can allow fractional activation where componentwise links force full activation, producing a strict relaxation gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Linking Gaps

source_witnesses.locator: Generalized disjunctive programming: A framework for formulation and alternative algorithms for MINLP optimization p. 93

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp Equality Boundary for Aggregate Activation Links
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary between equality and strict weakness of aggregate activation linking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u_i\ge0\), \(S=\sum_{i=1}^m u_i>0\), \(0\le y\le1\), and \(0\le x_i\le u_i\). Define \(P_{\mathrm{dis}}=\{(x,y):x_i\le u_i y\ \forall i\}\) and \(P_{\mathrm{agg}}=\{(x,y):\sum_i x_i\le Sy\}\). Then \(P_{\mathrm{dis}}=P_{\mathrm{agg}}\) if and only if at most one \(u_i\) is positive; otherwise \(P_{\mathrm{dis}}\subsetneq P_{\mathrm{agg}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate and componentwise activation links coincide only in the effectively one-component case; two or more positive capacities make aggregation strictly weaker.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\mathrm{dis}}=P_{\mathrm{agg}}\iff |\{i:u_i>0\}|\le1\); otherwise \(P_{\mathrm{dis}}\subsetneq P_{\mathrm{agg}}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Equality Boundary for Aggregate Activation Links

children.title: Indicator-Formulation Gaps
children.top_down_role: Gap regimes associated with relaxed indicator formulations.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The formulation \(0\leq y\leq1\), \(Ly\leq x\leq Uy\) is ideal for \(D\); an indicator-formulation gap can arise only after replacing this hull description by a weaker reformulation, such as one using looser activity bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for relaxation gaps in a bounded scalar on-off indicator disjunction.

source_refs.locator: Generalized disjunctive programming: A framework for formulation and alternative algorithms for MINLP optimization p. 93

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L<U\) be finite and define \[D=\{(0,0)\}\cup\{(1,x):L\leq x\leq U\}.\] Its convex hull is \[\operatorname{conv}(D)=\{(y,x):0\leq y\leq1,\ Ly\leq x\leq Uy\}.\] Thus the exact-bound scalar indicator formulation is ideal. An indicator-formulation relaxation gap is not intrinsic to this disjunction; it arises when an implementation replaces the hull description by a weaker reformulation, including one based on looser valid activity bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded scalar on-off indicator has an ideal formulation with its exact activity bounds; a relaxation gap arises only when the implementation uses a weaker reformulation, such as looser bounds.

children.title: Big-M Gaps
children.top_down_role: Relaxation weakness attributable to big-M formulation choices.

assumptions_latex: The model contains \(d\leq x\leq U\), \(x\leq My\), and minimizes \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The integer optimum is \(1\), the relaxation optimum is \(d/M\), and their ratio \(M/d\) is unbounded as \(M\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded multiplicative gap from an oversized activation coefficient.

source_refs.locator: Generalized disjunctive programming: A framework for formulation and alternative algorithms for MINLP optimization p. 93

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(0<d\leq U<M\) and consider \[\min\{y:d\leq x\leq U,\ x\leq My,\ y\in\{0,1\}\}.\] Every integer feasible solution has \(y=1\), so the integer optimum is \(1\). After relaxing \(y\) to \(0\leq y\leq1\), choosing \(x=d\) and \(y=d/M\) is optimal, giving value \(d/M\). The multiplicative integrality gap is therefore \(M/d\), which becomes arbitrarily large as the valid but oversized coefficient \(M\) increases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oversized big-M lets the relaxed activation variable shrink to demand divided by M, while every integer solution still requires full activation.
knowledge_statements.title: Big-M Gaps

children.title: Linking-Strength Comparisons

assumptions_latex: All compared formulations encode the same integer on-off condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\mathrm{hull}}=P_{\mathrm{dis}}\subseteq P_{\mathrm{agg}}\subseteq P_M\), yielding the corresponding relaxation-bound order.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Containment comparison for exact, disaggregated, aggregate, and oversized activation links.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the on-off set with \(0\leq x_i\leq u_i\) when \(y=1\) and \(x=0\) when \(y=0\), the exact hull and disaggregated relaxation use \(x_i\leq u_i y\). The aggregate relaxation replaces these by \(\sum_i x_i\leq(\sum_i u_i)y\). A big-M relaxation may instead use \(\sum_i x_i\leq My\) with \(M\geq\sum_i u_i\). Their projected feasible sets satisfy \[P_{\mathrm{hull}}=P_{\mathrm{dis}}\subseteq P_{\mathrm{agg}}\subseteq P_M.\] Thus minimization lower bounds weaken, and maximization upper bounds increase, along this containment chain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact componentwise links dominate aggregate links, which dominate any version using a still larger big-M coefficient; objective bounds weaken in the same order.

children.title: Dense-Quadratic Gaps

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense quadratic minimization family with a linearly growing additive independent-McCormick gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\ge3\), minimize \[f_n(x)=\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}x_ix_j-\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\] over \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\). If \(k=\sum_i x_i\), then \(f_n(x)=k(k-3)/2\), so the integer optimum is \(-1\). In the independent McCormick relaxation, \(x_i=1/2\) and \(y_{ij}=0\) are feasible and have value \(-n/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete quadratic instance has integer optimum −1 but an independent McCormick bound at most −n/2.
assumptions_latex: Every product is independently relaxed by its McCormick envelope on \([0,1]^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{int}}-z_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge n/2-1\).

Dense-Quadratic Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An unbounded gap for the standard pairwise McCormick relaxation of a dense binary quadratic maximization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each integer \(n\ge 2\), consider \(\max\{1+\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}x_i x_j: x\in\{0,1\}^n,\ \sum_i x_i\le 1\}\). Its integer optimum is \(1\). Replace every product by \(y_{ij}\) and impose \(0\le y_{ij}\le x_i\), \(y_{ij}\le x_j\), and \(y_{ij}\ge x_i+x_j-1\), with \(x\in[0,1]^n\). The assignment \(x_i=1/n\) and \(y_{ij}=1/n\) is relaxation-feasible and has value \((n+1)/2\). Thus the relaxation-to-integer value ratio is at least \((n+1)/2\), despite using all pairwise product envelopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense quadratic instance has integer value 1, while its pairwise McCormick relaxation attains at least (n+1)/2, giving a linearly growing ratio.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation applies each bilinear McCormick envelope independently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{rel}}/z_{\mathrm{int}}\ge (n+1)/2\), so the multiplicative gap is unbounded as \(n\to\infty\).

The second condition counts pair terms violating the binary quadratic submodularity criterion for minimization.

children.title: Relaxation Size Regimes
children.top_down_role: Representation-size regimes for binary relaxations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit count-based asymptotic size convention for finite linear extended relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X_n\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), let \(R_n=\{(x,z)\in\mathbb R^{n+r_n}:A_nx+B_nz\le b_n\}\) satisfy \(X_n\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(R_n)\), and define \(s(R_n)=m_n+r_n\), where \(m_n\) is the number of scalar inequalities and \(r_n\) the number of auxiliary variables. The family is polynomial-size if \(s(R_n)=n^{O(1)}\); quasipolynomial-size if \(s(R_n)=\exp(O((\log n)^k))\) for some fixed \(k\ge1\); strictly quasipolynomial-size if it is quasipolynomial-size but not polynomial-size; and exponential-size if \(s(R_n)=2^{\Omega(n)}\). These conditions are conventions for this count measure and do not exhaust all possible growth rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A declared row-plus-auxiliary-variable count supports polynomial, quasipolynomial, and exponential asymptotic regimes, without classifying every possible growth rate.
assumptions_latex: Each \(R_n\) is a finite linear extended relaxation.
The same size convention and indexing parameter \(n\) are used throughout the family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The asymptotic growth of \(s(R_n)=m_n+r_n\) determines which stated count-based size conditions the family satisfies.

notation.meaning: numbers of inequalities and auxiliary variables

review_flags: The size convention is explicit; alternative conventions such as inequality-only extension complexity or total encoding length must not be silently substituted.
knowledge_statements.title: Count-Based Relaxation Size Regimes

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Count Size Is Not Encoding Length
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates row-and-variable counts from rational binary input length.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For rational linear formulations represented in binary, the number of rows and variables does not determine total encoding length. The one-row descriptions \(2^k x\le1\) have constant row and variable counts, while the coefficient \(2^k\) requires \(\Theta(k)\) bits. Hence a polynomial bound on count size alone does not imply polynomial total encoding length unless coefficient encodings are also controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constantly many rows and variables can contain coefficients of unbounded bit length, so count size and encoding length are distinct measures.
assumptions_latex: The formulation data are rational and represented in binary.
Count size records rows and auxiliary variables but not coefficient bit lengths.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A polynomial bound on count size alone does not imply a polynomial bound on total binary encoding length.
knowledge_statements.title: Count Size Is Not Encoding Length
Relaxation Size Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size classes for extended relaxations, measured by inequalities and auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a binary feasible set \(X_n\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), let an extended relaxation be \(R_n=\{(x,z)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+r_n}:A_nx+B_nz\le b_n\}\) whose projection onto the original coordinates contains \(X_n\). Define \(s(R_n)=m_n+r_n\), where \(m_n\) is the number of scalar inequalities and \(r_n\) is the number of auxiliary variables. The family is polynomial-size if constants \(C,d>0\) satisfy \(s(R_n)\le Cn^d\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). It is quasipolynomial-size but not polynomial-size if \(s(R_n)\le\exp((\log n)^d)\) for some constant \(d>0\) and no polynomial upper bound holds. It is exponential-size if \(s(R_n)\ge 2^{cn}\) for some \(c>0\) along an infinite subsequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation size counts inequalities and auxiliary variables. Polynomial, strictly quasipolynomial, and exponential growth conditions define distinct size classes, without claiming that they exhaust every possible growth rate.
assumptions_latex: The formulation is finite-dimensional and linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The growth of \(s(R_n)=m_n+r_n\) determines whether the family meets the stated polynomial, strictly quasipolynomial, or exponential size condition.

notation.meaning: numbers of scalar inequalities and auxiliary variables

review_flags: A source fixing the formulation-size convention and asymptotic terminology is required.
standard_field_rationale: asymptotic growth classes with an explicitly declared size measure.

children.title: Relaxation Strength Regimes
children.top_down_role: Bound-strength regimes across binary relaxation families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected inclusion, exactness, and normalized additive and multiplicative family-gap conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_n\subseteq R_n\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty compact sets and let \(\mathcal C_n\) be a fixed normalized class of linear minimization objectives. Write \(z_S(c)=\min_{x\in S}c^\top x\). If \(X_n\subseteq R_n^{(1)}\subseteq R_n^{(2)}\), then \(z_{R_n^{(2)}}(c)\le z_{R_n^{(1)}}(c)\le z_{X_n}(c)\) for every \(c\in\mathcal C_n\). The relaxation is exact when \(R_n=\operatorname{conv}(X_n)\). Define the additive gap \(\Delta_n=\sup_{c\in\mathcal C_n}(z_{X_n}(c)-z_{R_n}(c))\). It is vanishing if \(\Delta_n\to0\), uniformly bounded if \(\sup_n\Delta_n<\infty\), and unbounded if \(\sup_n\Delta_n=\infty\). When \(z_{R_n}(c)>0\) throughout the declared objective class, define \(\Gamma_n=\sup_{c\in\mathcal C_n}z_{X_n}(c)/z_{R_n}(c)\), with analogous bounded and unbounded multiplicative regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected containment orders all normalized minimization bounds; exactness and explicitly normalized additive or positive-valued multiplicative gaps define asymptotic strength regimes.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C_n\) is a fixed normalized objective class.
For the multiplicative convention, \(z_{R_n}(c)>0\) for every admitted objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Containment gives uniform objective-bound dominance, while \(\Delta_n\) and, under positivity, \(\Gamma_n\) determine the stated family-gap regimes.

notation.meaning: minimum of objective c over S

review_flags: The objective normalization is deliberately parameterized but must be fixed before comparing families.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Strength and Gap Regimes
Relaxation Strength Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength comparison through set inclusion, objective bounds, exactness, and worst-case gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X
e\varnothing\) be a binary feasible set and let \(R_1,R_2\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be relaxations satisfying \(X\subseteq R_1\subseteq R_2\). For every linear minimization objective \(c\), \(\min_{x\in R_2}c^\top x\le\min_{x\in R_1}c^\top x\le\min_{x\in X}c^\top x\), whenever the minima are finite. Thus inclusion orders relaxations by strength. A relaxation is exact when \(R=\operatorname{conv}(X)\); otherwise additive or multiplicative worst-case gaps over a declared objective class distinguish bounded-gap, vanishing-gap, and unbounded-gap regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smaller valid relaxation gives at least as strong a minimization bound. Exactness and worst-case objective gaps classify stronger and weaker regimes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{R_2}(c)\le z_{R_1}(c)\le z_X(c)\) for every admissible minimization objective \(c\).

notation.meaning: minimum of the objective over set S

standard_field_rationale: monotonicity follows directly from feasible-set inclusion.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Neither relaxation uniformly dominates the other over all linear minimization objectives.

children.title: Separable Relaxation Structure
children.top_down_role: Decomposability and separability characteristics of relaxation designs.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Relaxation Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-separable extended relaxations with local block constraints and explicit coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\ge1\) and let \(x=(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(K)})\) be a partition of the variables. A relaxation is block-separable with explicit coupling if it has the form \(R=\{x:x^{(k)}\in R_k\text{ for }k=1,\ldots,K,\ \sum_{k=1}^K B_kx^{(k)}\le d\}\), where each nonempty local set \(R_k\) uses only block \(k\). An objective is conformably separable if \(f(x)=\sum_{k=1}^K f_k(x^{(k)})\). When the coupling rows are absent and every block infimum is finite, optimization decomposes as \(\inf_{x\in R}f(x)=\sum_{k=1}^K\inf_{x^{(k)}\in R_k}f_k(x^{(k)})\). When coupling rows are present, Lagrangian dualization of those rows yields blockwise subproblems for each fixed multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-separable relaxation consists of nonempty local block sets and explicit coupling rows. With a separable objective and no coupling, finite block problems optimize independently; dualizing coupling rows yields blockwise Lagrangian subproblems.
assumptions_latex: \(K\ge1\), and the variable blocks form a partition.
For the displayed decomposition identity, \(f(x)=\sum_{k=1}^K f_k(x^{(k)})\), the coupling rows are absent, and each block infimum is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without coupling rows, \(\inf_{x\in R}f(x)=\sum_{k=1}^K\inf_{x^{(k)}\in R_k}f_k(x^{(k)})\) under the stated finiteness assumptions.

notation.meaning: nonempty local relaxation for block k

children.title: Size–Strength–Separability Frontiers
children.top_down_role: Tradeoff boundaries connecting formulation size, bound strength, and separable structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterized three-criterion frontier under fixed comparison and measurement conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an admissible relaxation family \(\mathcal R\) and three common measures: formulation size \(s(R)\), relaxation loss \(g(R)\), and nonseparability \(\kappa(R)\), with smaller values preferred. A relaxation \(R\in\mathcal R\) dominates \(R'\in\mathcal R\) if \(s(R)\le s(R')\), \(g(R)\le g(R')\), and \(\kappa(R)\le\kappa(R')\), with at least one strict inequality. The size–strength–separability frontier is the set of undominated relaxations. This frontier is well defined only relative to the fixed family and measures; changing any of them can change frontier membership, while applying a strictly increasing transformation separately to any coordinate preserves dominance and the frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The frontier consists of relaxations not simultaneously improvable in fixed size, relaxation-loss, and nonseparability measures; changing the family or measures can change the frontier.
assumptions_latex: \(s\), \(g\), and \(\kappa\) use common conventions on \(\mathcal R\).
Smaller values of all three coordinates are preferred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\) is frontier-optimal exactly when no member of \(\mathcal R\) weakly improves all three coordinates and strictly improves at least one.
review_flags: Frontier membership is convention-relative; the definition does not assert a universal canonical scalar measure for any coordinate.
knowledge_statements.title: Size–Strength–Separability Pareto Frontier
Size–Strength–Separability Frontiers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto frontier for simultaneous formulation size, relaxation gap, and coupling complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an instance class, an objective normalization, and a relaxation family \(\mathcal{R}\). Assign each \(R\in\mathcal{R}\) a triple \((s(R),g(R),\kappa(R))\), where \(s\) is formulation size, \(g\) is its worst-case relaxation gap, and \(\kappa\) measures nonseparability, such as the number of coupling rows or maximum block-interface width. A relaxation \(R\) lies on the size–strength–separability frontier if no \(R'\in\mathcal{R}\) satisfies \(s(R')\le s(R)\), \(g(R')\le g(R)\), and \(\kappa(R')\le\kappa(R)\), with at least one strict inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The frontier consists of relaxations not simultaneously improvable in size, worst-case gap, and coupling complexity.
assumptions_latex: The size, gap, and nonseparability measures use fixed common conventions.
Smaller values of all three measures are preferred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\) is frontier-optimal exactly when its performance triple is Pareto-minimal in \(\mathcal{R}\).
review_flags: The three-axis frontier is a local synthesis requiring an explicit source or adopted convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Pareto-minimality definition is internally precise and fits the frontier container, but the proposed three-axis synthesis and the admissible measures have no inspectable source.

children.title: Variable Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching strategies centered on individual binary variables.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Depth of Nonrepeating Binary Variable Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Enumeration bounds for branching only on previously unfixed binary coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every root-to-leaf path branches only on a binary variable not previously fixed on that path, then a problem with \(n\) binary variables has depth at most \(n\), at most \(2^n\) leaves, and at most \(2^{n+1}-1\) total nodes before pruning. These are finite-enumeration bounds, not polynomial-time guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonrepeating branching on n binary variables has depth at most n, although the full unpruned tree can still have exponentially many leaves and nodes.
assumptions_latex: Each branch fixes a previously unfixed variable on its root-to-leaf path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{depth}(\mathcal T)\le n,\qquad |\mathcal L|\le2^n,\qquad |\mathcal T|\le2^{n+1}-1.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Depth of Nonrepeating Binary Variable Branching
Variable Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary branch-and-bound split on one fractional variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a branch-and-bound node with relaxation \(R\) and fractional solution \(\bar x\), choose an index \(j\) with \(0<\bar x_j<1\). Create the children \(R^0=R\cap\{x:x_j=0\}\) and \(R^1=R\cap\{x:x_j=1\}\). Solve or bound both children, prune any child proved infeasible or unable to improve the incumbent, and continue until every live node is integral or pruned. Because every binary point satisfies exactly one of the two branch equations, the split preserves all integer-feasible solutions while excluding \(\bar x\) from both children.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a fractional binary variable and create children fixing it to zero and one; together the children preserve every binary-feasible solution.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\bar x_j<1\) at the current relaxation solution.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports branch-and-bound variable branching.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary variable-branching algorithm and partition conclusion are correct and fit the terminal container, but no citation with a locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary-variable selection at a relaxation solution using distance from the variable's two bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat{x}\) be the solution of a convex nonlinear or polyhedral relaxation, let \(B\) be the set of binary-variable indices, and define \(\delta_i(\widehat{x})=\min\{\bar{x}_i-\widehat{x}_i,\widehat{x}_i-\underline{x}_i\}\). Choose \(i^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{i\in B}\delta_i(\widehat{x})\), with cut values \(\underline t=\underline{x}_{i^*}\) and \(\bar t=\bar{x}_{i^*}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a relaxation solution, select the binary variable having the greatest minimum distance from its two bounds, then create branches fixing it at its lower and upper bounds.
assumptions_latex: \widehat{x}\text{ solves a convex nonlinear or polyhedral relaxation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: i^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{i\in B}\delta_i(\widehat{x}),\qquad \underline t=\underline{x}_{i^*},\quad\bar t=\bar{x}_{i^*}.

children.title: Constraint Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching strategies derived from constraint structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage boundary for a floor-ceiling split on a constraint or aggregate activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A floor-ceiling split at a nonintegral value \(t\) covers a domain \(X\) only if every point that must be preserved satisfies \(h(x)\le\lfloor t\rfloor\) or \(h(x)\ge\lceil t\rceil\). The condition \(h(X)\subseteq\mathbb Z\) is sufficient. Without such discreteness, coverage can fail even on a binary domain: for \(X=\{0,1\}\), \(h(x)=x/2\), and \(t=1/2\), the children \(h(x)\le0\) and \(h(x)\ge1\) omit the feasible point \(x=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Floor-ceiling constraint branching needs an integer-valued or equivalently discrete activity on every point being preserved; otherwise a binary feasible point can fall between the children.
assumptions_latex: A two-child floor-ceiling split is proposed at a nonintegral activity value \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h(X)\subseteq\mathbb Z\text{ suffices for coverage; without an equivalent gap condition, coverage is not guaranteed.}

notation.meaning: domain whose relevant feasible points must be preserved

review_flags: The counterexample was revised to use a binary domain, matching the terminal topic scope.
knowledge_statements.title: Integral-Activity Requirement
Constraint Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branching on the integral activity induced by a selected constraint row or aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a\in\mathbb{Z}^n\) define an integer-valued activity \(a^\top x\) for every binary vector \(x\). At a relaxation solution \(\bar x\) with \(a^\top\bar x\notin\mathbb{Z}\), create \(R^-=R\cap\{x:a^\top x\le\lfloor a^\top\bar x\rfloor\}\) and \(R^+=R\cap\{x:a^\top x\ge\lceil a^\top\bar x\rceil\}\). Bound and prune the children as usual. The selected row may be an original constraint or a valid aggregate; integrality of its activity ensures that the two children cover every binary-feasible point and exclude the current fractional activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose an integer-valued constraint activity and branch below its floor or above its ceiling, preserving all binary points while cutting off the fractional activity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\cap\{0,1\}^n\subseteq R^-\cup R^+\) and \(\bar x\notin R^-\cup R^+\).
review_flags: Constraint-branching terminology varies and requires a supporting source.
standard_field_rationale: standard split on an integral row activity.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The integral-activity split is mathematically valid and algorithmically appropriate, but the exact meaning of constraint branching and its use for aggregates require a supporting branching reference.

children.title: Disjunction Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching families based on general disjunctive partitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunction Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General finite valid-disjunction branching for binary-feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node relaxation \(R\), choose sets \(D_1,\ldots,D_p\) such that every integer-feasible point in \(R\) belongs to \(\bigcup_{k=1}^pD_k\), while the current fractional solution is excluded from that union or from each selected branch. Create child relaxations \(R_k=R\cap D_k\), compute valid bounds, and prune or continue each child. Overlap is permitted, although disjoint alternatives avoid duplicate search. Validity of the covering disjunction guarantees that no integer-feasible solution is lost; variable and integral-row branching are two-term special cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersect the node relaxation with each term of a finite disjunction covering all integer-feasible points, then bound and search the resulting children.
assumptions_latex: \(R\cap X_I\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^pD_k\), where \(X_I\) is the integer domain.
Each child relaxation can be validly bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\cap X_I\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^p(R_k\cap X_I)\), so branching preserves every integer-feasible point.

notation.meaning: child relaxation associated with term k

review_flags: No supplied locator supports general disjunctive branching.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite covering-disjunction construction is valid and the algorithm kind fits, but no inspectable source supports the general formulation or its claimed special cases.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic parent-bound consequence of a covering disjunction; deferred because its canonical home is the broader disjunctive-branching theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization over \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^pF_k\), assigning \(L_k=+\infty\) to an infeasible child and any valid lower bound to a nonempty child gives \(\min_k L_k\le\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\). If all children are infeasible, then \(F\) is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum child lower bound is a parent lower bound under exhaustive coverage, and infeasibility of every child proves parent infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Each nonempty child has a valid minimization lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_kL_k\le\inf_{x\in F}f(x),\qquad(\forall k,\ F_k=\varnothing)\Rightarrow F=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: valid child lower bound, with +infinity for an infeasible child

children.title: Branching-Object Selection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes favoring variable, constraint, or disjunction branching.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative score forms for ranking valid two-child branching objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For predicted nonnegative child-bound improvements \(\Delta_1,\Delta_2\), representative monotone scores are \(S_{\mathrm{lin}}=(1-\mu)\min\{\Delta_1,\Delta_2\}+\mu\max\{\Delta_1,\Delta_2\}\), where \(0\le\mu<1\), and \(S_{\mathrm{prod}}=\max\{\Delta_1,\varepsilon\}\max\{\Delta_2,\varepsilon\}\), where \(\varepsilon>0\). Different scores can rank the same valid candidates differently; scoring affects selection, not branch validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted min-max and safeguarded product scores rank predicted gains from two children. They may choose different candidates and do not themselves certify branch validity.
assumptions_latex: Each candidate already defines a valid two-child covering branch.
The predicted child-bound gains are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_{\mathrm{lin}}\text{ and }S_{\mathrm{prod}}\text{ may induce different rankings without changing the validity of any candidate branch.}
review_flags: The original claim was narrowed: at \(\mu=1\) the linear score would ignore the smaller gain, so the stated range is \(0\le\mu<1\).
Score conventions and parameter choices are solver-dependent.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Child Gain Scores
Branching-Object Selection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection regimes determined by the accuracy and computational cost of estimating child-bound improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{B}(R)\) be the admissible branching objects at node \(R\), and let \(S(b;R)\) estimate the aggregate improvement of the child bounds produced by \(b\). Selection takes the form \(b^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{b\in C(R)}S(b;R)\), where \(C(R)\subseteq\mathcal{B}(R)\) is the set affordable under the node budget. Exact strong branching evaluates candidate children; sampled strong branching evaluates a subset; reliability branching uses exact evaluations until stored estimates become reliable; pseudocost branching primarily uses historical estimates. These regimes trade evaluation cost against score fidelity without changing branching validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branching objects maximize an estimated child-bound gain over an affordable candidate set; strong, sampled, reliability, and pseudocost regimes differ in evaluation effort.
assumptions_latex: Every \(b\in\mathcal{B}(R)\) defines a valid covering branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{b\in C(R)}S(b;R)\), with regimes distinguished by how \(S\) is estimated.

notation.meaning: candidates evaluated under the node budget

review_flags: Strong, reliability, and pseudocost regime taxonomy requires a branching reference.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the selection-regime container, but the strong, sampled, reliability, and pseudocost taxonomy and their descriptions require a branching reference.

children.title: Branching Score Families
children.top_down_role: Families of scoring criteria for ranking branching candidates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scoring through tentative solution of both child relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a minimization node with relaxation bound z_N, tentatively form both children of candidate b, obtain comparable bounds z_b^- and z_b^+, set \Delta_b^\pm=\max\{0,z_b^\pm-z_N\}, and rank b by a fixed two-gain aggregation \Phi(\Delta_b^-,\Delta_b^+). Full strong branching evaluates every candidate to the prescribed accuracy; restricted variants limit candidates, iterations, or total work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong branching measures the two tentative child-bound improvements and aggregates them into a candidate score.
assumptions_latex: Parent and tentative-child bounds use the same minimization convention.
\Phi and the tentative-solve accuracy are fixed for the comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected candidate maximizes the specified aggregation of measured child gains.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Branching Scores

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid use of tentative child solves and pseudocost predictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an observation threshold \eta\ge1. For candidate i, perform tentative child evaluation whenever a required directional pseudocost has fewer than \eta compatible observations, and update its statistics. Once both directions meet the threshold, score i from pseudocost predictions without a mandatory tentative solve. Pure pseudocost branching is obtained by using initialized estimates without reliability tests; persistent tentative evaluation approaches strong branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reliability branching measures gains until both directional pseudocosts are sufficiently observed, then normally uses their predictions.
assumptions_latex: Directional counts and estimates are maintained consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy interpolates between tentative strong-branching evaluation and pseudocost prediction.
knowledge_statements.title: Reliability Branching

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxation-only scoring of binary branching candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a binary candidate i with relaxation value \bar x_i\in(0,1), the fractionality score m_i=\min\{\bar x_i,1-\bar x_i\} ranks values nearest 1/2 highest. It uses no child solve or historical observation and predicts neither child-bound gain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Most-fractional branching ranks binary variables by proximity of their relaxation values to one half.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_i\in(0,1/2], with its maximum attained at \bar x_i=1/2.
knowledge_statements.title: Fractionality Scores

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Historical prediction of directional child gains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fractional integer variable i, let p_i^- and p_i^+ be empirical average bound gains per unit downward and upward displacement. Predict \widehat\Delta_i^-=p_i^-(\bar x_i-\lfloor\bar x_i\rfloor) and \widehat\Delta_i^+=p_i^+(\lceil\bar x_i\rceil-\bar x_i), then apply a fixed two-gain aggregation. A measured child updates only its corresponding directional statistics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pseudocost branching predicts child gains from historical gain-per-displacement observations.
assumptions_latex: i is fractional in the current relaxation solution.
Each used pseudocost is initialized or based on compatible directional observations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\widehat\Delta_i^-,\widehat\Delta_i^+) is a history-based surrogate for strong-branching gains.
knowledge_statements.title: Pseudocost Scores
Branching Score Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gain-based score families with an optional symmetry-invariance requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a two-child branching object \(b\), let \(\Delta_b^-\ge0\) and \(\Delta_b^+\ge0\) be the child-bound improvements over the parent. Common score families include \(S_{\min}(b)=\min\{\Delta_b^-,\Delta_b^+\}\), \(S_{\mathrm{prod}}(b)=\max\{\Delta_b^-,\varepsilon\}\max\{\Delta_b^+,\varepsilon\}\), and \(S_\mu(b)=(1-\mu)\min\{\Delta_b^-,\Delta_b^+\}+\mu\max\{\Delta_b^-,\Delta_b^+\}\), where \(0\le\mu\le1\) and \(\varepsilon>0\). Under a symmetry group \(G\) acting on branching objects, a symmetry-aware score satisfies \(S(gb)=S(b)\) for every \(g\in G\), permitting selection by orbit representatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum-gain, product-gain, and weighted min–max scores combine two child improvements; symmetry-aware versions assign equal scores to equivalent branching objects.
assumptions_latex: The group action preserves the underlying subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(S(gb)=S(b)\) for all \(g\in G\), scoring one representative per orbit preserves the set of attainable score values.

notation.meaning: bound improvements of the two children
symmetry group acting on branching objects

review_flags: No supplied locator supports branching-score formulas or symmetry invariance.
