children.top_down_role: Interface concerns for restarting binary search while retaining selected solver state.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Guarantees supplied and not supplied by root restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Canceling non-root assignments while retaining only globally entailed learned constraints and valid root deductions preserves the solution set. This proves soundness of a restart but not termination, which additionally requires fair or progressive coordination. Retaining a local or state-dependent constraint after its validity scope disappears can remove feasible solutions; deleting such transient information merely forfeits inference.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restarts are sound when retained deductions remain globally valid, but termination needs separate progress and expired local information cannot be retained.
assumptions_latex: Retained root assignments are consequences of the permanent model.
Retained learned constraints are globally entailed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A restart preserves feasible solutions but does not alone guarantee termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Restart Soundness Versus Completeness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restart budgets growing by a fixed factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given T_0\in\mathbb N_{>0} and \rho>1, a geometric restart schedule uses budgets T_r=\lceil T_0\rho^r\rceil. These budgets are positive, nondecreasing, and unbounded; each restart is triggered after its current counted budget unless search terminates first.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A geometric restart policy increases successive conflict budgets multiplicatively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_r\to\infty and every scheduled epoch has a finite positive budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Restart Schedule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recurrent schedule interleaving short and arbitrarily long budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define u_k=2^{m-1} when k=2^m-1; otherwise set u_k=u_{k-2^{m-1}+1} for the unique m satisfying 2^{m-1}\le k<2^m-1. For a positive scale T, the budgets Tu_1,Tu_2,\ldots begin T,T,2T,T,T,2T,4T,\ldots. The schedule repeatedly returns to short epochs while containing arbitrarily long epochs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Luby schedule recurrently mixes short restart budgets with unbounded longer budgets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every power-of-two multiple of T occurs, and the sequence is unbounded but nonmonotone.
review_flags: No universal-runtime optimality claim is made without a specified randomized-runtime model.
knowledge_statements.title: Luby Restart Schedule
Restart Policy Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-driven restart scheduling that preserves sound learned information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a conflict counter \(k\), a restart threshold sequence \((T_r)_{r\ge0}\), and restart index \(r\). After each conflict, increment \(k\). When \(k\ge T_r\), cancel all trail assignments above decision level zero, restore reversible state to its root snapshot, retain every currently valid learned constraint and root-level deduction, set \(k=0\), increment \(r\), and resume branching. The threshold sequence may be fixed in advance or selected from solver statistics, but each trigger must occur only between completed conflict analyses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restart trigger clears non-root assignments, preserves valid learning and root deductions, advances its schedule, and resumes search from the root state.
assumptions_latex: Restart thresholds are positive and finite whenever a restart is scheduled.
Learned constraints retained across restarts remain globally valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A restart changes the search trajectory without enlarging the feasible set or invalidating retained deductions.

notation.meaning: conflicts accumulated in the current epoch

review_flags: specific schedules and completeness conditions need a supporting source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is suitable for a restart-policy interface, but the scheduling convention, preservation rules, and any completeness implications require an inspectable source.

children.title: Backtracking–Restart Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination boundaries between nonchronological backtracking and restart policies.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness boundary for coordinating backjumps and repeated restarts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a finite Boolean problem, sound restoration and entailed learning preserve correctness but do not alone ensure termination. Completeness requires a fair or progressive policy: no unresolved search alternative may be postponed forever, and an infinite sequence of restorations may not repeat the same effective search state without persistent progress such as learning a genuinely new consequence or permanently exhausting an alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backjumps and restarts need fairness or persistent progress, in addition to sound restoration, to guarantee complete finite search.
assumptions_latex: The Boolean search space is finite.
Every retained learned constraint is entailed by the permanent problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restoration is sound, while termination additionally requires exclusion of infinite no-progress cycles.
knowledge_statements.title: Progress Condition Across Restarts

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of termination under repeated restoration without persistent progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a satisfiable finite instance and a deterministic branching rule whose first decision is always x=0. If a coordination policy repeatedly restores the root before the current path produces any persistent inference, learned constraint, completed solution, or exhausted alternative, then the same decision is selected after every restoration. The execution remains sound but can repeat forever without finding a solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly restarting before persistent progress can reproduce the same first decision forever on a finite satisfiable instance.
assumptions_latex: No persistent search state changes between restorations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Correct restoration alone does not imply termination or completeness.
knowledge_statements.title: Restart Livelock
Backtracking–Restart Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-consistency invariant shared by backjumps and global restarts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_d\) denote the solver state at decision level \(d\), partitioned into permanent data, globally valid learned data, and trail-dependent reversible data. A backjump to \(b\) must restore the reversible component to \(S_b\); a restart is the special restoration target \(b=0\). Before either transition, conflict analysis and insertion of its learned constraint must finish. After restoration, propagation must reach a fixpoint before a new decision. Consequently, both operations preserve permanent and valid learned constraints while discarding precisely those assignments and cached consequences whose levels exceed the target.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backjumps and restarts use one restoration invariant: finish learning, roll back level-dependent state, preserve valid constraints, then propagate before branching.
assumptions_latex: Every reversible datum is tagged by level or recoverable from a level snapshot.
Retained learned constraints are globally valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each transition produces a state equivalent to the retained database under the target-level trail.

notation.meaning: solver state associated with decision level \(d\)

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard reversible-state invariant for conflict-driven search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the coordination leaf, but “state equivalent” and the claim that precisely all higher-level cached consequences are discarded require formal interface semantics and a supporting source.

children.title: Conflict-Graph Management
children.top_down_role: Storage, traversal, and lifecycle concerns for conflict-graph data.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implicit management that materializes reason edges only for a realized conflict.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Store with each propagated trail literal its decision level, trail position, and reason reference without eagerly materializing every reason edge. Upon conflict, initialize a worklist with the assignments falsifying the conflicting constraint and recursively expand stored reasons until the chosen analysis frontier is reached. Under the same antecedent convention, this materializes exactly the conflict-reachable portion of the eager reason graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The implication graph can be stored implicitly on the trail and expanded only along reasons relevant to the current conflict.
assumptions_latex: Reason references remain valid while their explained trail literals remain assigned.
Lazy and eager representations use the same antecedent convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G_{\mathrm{lazy}}=G[A(\kappa)\cup\{\kappa\}]\text{ for the realized traversal.}
knowledge_statements.title: Trail-Indexed Lazy Conflict Graph

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reachability reduction for an already realized implication-graph conflict.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In an acyclic reason graph with conflict sink \(\kappa\), every reason chain used to derive that conflict lies in the subgraph induced by \(A(\kappa)\cup\{\kappa\}\). Vertices outside this subgraph cannot affect a graph cut separating the relevant decisions from \(\kappa\) for the current analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only ancestors of the current conflict sink are needed for that conflict's traversal and cut analysis.
assumptions_latex: The graph represents an already realized conflict.
Reason edges point from antecedent assignments to propagated consequences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Current conflict analysis may be restricted to }G[A(\kappa)\cup\{\kappa\}].

notation.meaning: directed ancestors of the conflict sink

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Ancestor Sufficiency

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete lifecycle failure when a reason is reclaimed while its propagated literal remains on the trail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the active clauses include (
eg a\lor b) and (
eg a\lor
eg b). After deciding a=1, suppose unit propagation first assigns b=1 with reason (
eg a\lor b); the second clause then conflicts. If that reason record is reclaimed while b remains assigned, the conflicting trail remains but the dependency edge a	o b is lost, so graph traversal cannot reconstruct the resolution step yielding 
eg a.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting a live reason can leave a conflict on the trail while destroying the dependency information needed to analyze and certify it.
assumptions_latex: Reason records are the sole stored justifications for propagated trail literals.
The propagated literal remains assigned after reclamation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Live reason reclamation can make the maintained conflict graph incomplete.}
review_flags: Corrects the Builder trace, whose clause (\neg b) would ordinarily force b=0 before the stated decision-level propagation.
knowledge_statements.title: Premature Reason Reclamation Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precise eager graph convention for a current trail, with a conflict sink only after conflict realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a trail \(\tau=(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_k)\), create a vertex \(v_p\) for each assigned literal \(\ell_p\), labeled by its decision level, trail position, and either a decision marker or reason \(R_p\). For a propagated literal, add \((v_q,v_p)\) from each earlier assignment in a specified sufficient antecedent set that made \(R_p\) forcing. When a constraint is falsified, add a sink \(\kappa\) with edges from a specified sufficient set of falsifying assignments. Edges increase trail position or enter \(\kappa\), so the graph is acyclic. Backtracking to position \(h\) deletes vertices after \(h\), their incident edges, and the conflict sink.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The eager reason graph contains trail assignments, forward dependency edges, and an optional realized-conflict sink; backtracking deletes the abandoned suffix.
assumptions_latex: Every propagated assignment has a stored valid reason and a sufficient antecedent set.
Every antecedent precedes its propagated consequence on the trail.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G_\tau\text{ is a finite DAG representing the selected dependencies of the current trail and any realized conflict}.

notation.meaning: recorded reason at trail position p

review_flags: Different analyzers may choose different sufficient antecedent sets; the selected convention must remain fixed during traversal.
knowledge_statements.title: Eager Trail-Ordered Reason Graph
Conflict-Graph Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level-annotated reason graph maintained for conflict analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At any search state, maintain a directed acyclic graph \(G=(V,E)\). Each vertex represents an assigned literal and stores its decision level, trail position, and either a decision marker or a valid reason constraint. For each propagated vertex \(v\), add edges \((u,v)\) from the falsifying assignments participating in the recorded reason. A conflict is represented by a sink \(\kappa\) whose predecessors falsify a constraint. On backtracking, delete vertices above the target level and their incident edges; globally valid reason constraints may remain in the learned database.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conflict graph records assignments, levels, order, and reasons; a conflict sink supports analysis, while backtracking removes the abandoned suffix.
assumptions_latex: Every recorded reason was unit or forcing when its consequent was assigned.
Trail order is acyclic and every reason edge points forward in that order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\) is a sound finite representation of the implication dependencies leading to the current conflict.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard implication-graph representation used in conflict analysis

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation matches conflict-graph management, but the statement begins at any search state while concluding that the graph leads to the current conflict, which need not yet exist. A source is also required for the exact reason-edge convention.

children.title: Learned-Constraint Management
children.top_down_role: Retention, deletion, aging, and prioritization concerns for learned constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Logical Redundancy Does Not Guarantee Propagation Redundancy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on using entailment alone to rank learned constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even when retained constraints semantically entail a learned constraint \(C\), deleting \(C\) need not preserve deductions made by a fixed incomplete propagator. Semantic redundancy therefore certifies feasible-set preservation but not equality of propagation closures or search trees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An entailed learned constraint is logically safe to delete, but deletion may weaken propagation and enlarge search.
assumptions_latex: The propagation procedure need not be deductively complete.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\models C\not\Rightarrow\operatorname{cl}_P(D,\alpha)=\operatorname{cl}_P(D\cup\{C\},\alpha).
knowledge_statements.title: Logical Redundancy Does Not Guarantee Propagation Redundancy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical redundancy test for deleting a weaker learned constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the retained database and \(C_1,C_2\) active learned constraints. If \(P\cup\{C_1\}\models C_2\), deleting \(C_2\) preserves the active feasible set. For clauses, \(L(C_1)\subseteq L(C_2)\) implies \(C_1\models C_2\), so the subsumed clause \(C_2\) is logically redundant, provided it is not left as a dangling live reason.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A learned constraint entailed by retained constraints can be deleted; literal-set inclusion gives the standard clause-subsumption test.
assumptions_latex: All constraints use a common binary-variable interpretation.
Any live reference to \(C_2\) is removed or protected before deletion.
knowledge_statements.title: Entailment-Based Subsumption Deletion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe certificate lifecycle for learned constraints used by retained derivations or live trail reasons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent learned derivations by a directed acyclic dependency graph whose leaves are permanent inputs and whose internal nodes are learned constraints justified from predecessors. A learned constraint may be removed from certificate storage only after it is not a live trail reason and either no retained certificate depends on it or every such dependency has been expanded into retained predecessors. Under this invariant, each retained learned constraint still has a checkable derivation from permanent inputs. A propagation database may delete a constraint while proof storage retains its derivation node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certificate deletion is safe only after live reason references and retained proof dependencies are removed, retained separately, or expanded.
assumptions_latex: Every learned constraint initially has a valid finite derivation from earlier constraints.
Certificate dependency edges point from premises to conclusions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall C\in D_{\mathrm{retained}},\quad D_{\mathrm{permanent}}\models C\text{ remains checkable after certificate reclamation}.
review_flags: Propagation-database deletion and proof-log deletion are distinct lifecycle operations.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Dependency Retention Invariant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic sound reduction procedure with explicit scheduling and ranking parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain for each active learned constraint \(C\) an activity score \(a(C)\), age, size, and protection flags. On each declared use event, update \(a(C)\) by a fixed scoring rule and optionally apply a fixed decay rule. At a scheduled reduction, form the eligible set from constraints that are neither locked nor permanent, rank it by a fixed total order from declared quality keys, and propagation-delete the prescribed fraction \(\rho\in[0,1]\) of lowest-ranked eligible constraints. Update propagation indices and apply the certificate-dependency retention invariant separately to proof storage. If every inserted constraint is entailed by the permanent database, the cycle preserves the feasible set, although deletion may weaken propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduction cycle updates declared scores, protects live reasons and permanent constraints, deletes a fixed low-ranked eligible fraction, and manages proof storage separately.
assumptions_latex: Every inserted learned constraint is entailed by the permanent database.
Scoring, decay, scheduling, quality ordering, and tie-breaking rules are fixed parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(D_{\mathrm{after}})=F(D_{\mathrm{before}})\quad\text{although propagation closures may weaken}

notation.meaning: Fraction of eligible constraints selected for propagation deletion.

review_flags: No universal search-performance claim is made for any ranking policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Parameterized Learned-Database Reduction Cycle

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lifecycle States of a Learned Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational distinctions among propagation presence, protection, live use, and proof retention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A learned constraint \(C\) is active when indexed for propagation; dormant when retained but not currently propagated; locked when referenced as a live trail reason; permanent when exempt from ordinary database reduction; propagation-deleted when absent from the active propagation database; and proof-retained when its derivation node remains in certificate storage. These are independent attributes except where their meanings conflict. In particular, a propagation-deleted constraint may remain proof-retained, and a locked constraint must remain available until its live reason reference is released or replaced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Management separately tracks propagation activity, deletion protection, live reason use, and proof storage.
assumptions_latex: Every live trail reason refers to an available constraint representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{propagation deletion}\not\Rightarrow\text{proof deletion},\qquad\text{locked}\Rightarrow\text{available as a live reason}

notation.meaning: A learned constraint managed by the solver.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifecycle States of a Learned Constraint
Learned-Constraint Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound insertion, scoring, retention, and deletion of learned constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each learned constraint \(C\), verify or inherit an entailment certificate, insert \(C\) into the propagation database, and maintain an activity score \(a(C)\) updated when \(C\) participates in propagation or conflict analysis. At scheduled reductions, retain every locked constraint currently serving as a reason and every constraint designated permanent; rank the remaining constraints using activity, size, or a fixed quality measure, and delete a selected low-ranked subset. Removing learned constraints is sound because it only weakens the active database. Output the reduced database together with updated propagation indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Learned constraints are validated, indexed, scored, and periodically reduced, while active reasons and permanent constraints remain protected from deletion.
assumptions_latex: Every inserted learned constraint is entailed by the permanent database.
A locked constraint is not deleted while it explains a trail assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Insertion and deletion preserve all feasible solutions, and deletion cannot create an invalid inference.
review_flags: ranking and retention policy require a supporting source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits learned-constraint management and its soundness invariant is plausible, but certificate inheritance, locking, scoring, ranking, and deletion policies require a specific source and locator.

children.title: Conflict-Data Retention Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Memory and search-value tradeoffs across retained conflict artifacts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates logical deletion safety from unsafe removal of permanent or referenced data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the permanent constraints and \(D\) learned constraints satisfying \(P\models C\) for every \(C\in D\). Replacing \(D\) by any \(R\subseteq D\) preserves the feasible set of \(P\). Deleting a constraint not entailed by \(P\) can change that set. Deleting a constraint referenced as a live propagation reason is operationally unsafe unless the dependent assignments and references are first removed or reconstructed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Entailed learned constraints may be discarded logically, but permanent constraints and live reason objects cannot be deleted under the same rule.
assumptions_latex: Every safely deletable learned constraint is entailed by \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(P\cup R)=F(P)\text{ for every }R\subseteq D;\text{ live references impose an additional lifecycle condition.}
knowledge_statements.title: Correctness Boundary for Conflict-Data Deletion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy-independent tradeoff governing retained conflict artifacts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Retaining an entailed conflict artifact can preserve future propagation, conflict-analysis reuse, or avoidance of repeated derivation, while consuming storage, indexing, and inspection time. Deleting such an artifact can reduce those costs but may weaken incomplete inference and enlarge later search. Consequently, neither retaining every artifact nor deleting every unlocked artifact universally dominates in runtime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping conflict data can save future inference but costs memory and processing; safe deletion can still enlarge search, so no universal runtime ordering exists.
assumptions_latex: Retained artifacts are inspected or indexed by the solver.
The inference procedures may be incomplete.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Logical redundancy does not determine the runtime-optimal retention set.}
knowledge_statements.title: Retention Resource–Inference Tradeoff
Conflict-Data Retention Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource–inference tradeoff under a bounded learned-data budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the current set of learned constraints, let \(m(C)>0\) be the storage and indexing cost of \(C\), and let \(v(C)\ge0\) estimate its future propagation or conflict-analysis value. Under budget \(B\), a retention policy selects \(R\subseteq D\) with \(\sum_{C\in R}m(C)\le B\), subject to retaining locked reasons. Increasing \(R\) can preserve more reusable inference but raises memory and propagation-scanning cost; deleting \(D\setminus R\) preserves correctness because all learned constraints are redundant consequences, though it may increase subsequent search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within a memory budget, retaining more useful learned data can strengthen future inference but costs storage and propagation time; safe deletion may enlarge search.
assumptions_latex: Every member of \(D\) is entailed by the permanent constraints.
Locked reason constraints must remain until their explained assignments leave the trail.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Retention affects resource use and search effort, but sound deletion of unlocked learned consequences does not change the feasible set.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: learned consequences may be deleted soundly, with performance tradeoffs
quantitative retention model lacks an exact supporting source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the retention-tradeoff leaf, but the budget model and performance claims are not supported by a cited source. Safe deletion of entailed unlocked constraints is plausible but likewise needs a locator.

children.title: Bit-Flip Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Neighborhoods generated by changing selected binary values.

knowledge_statements.title: Bit-Flip Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hamming-radius neighborhoods for feasible binary points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), let \(x\in F\), and let \(k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\). The radius-\(k\) bit-flip neighborhood of \(x\) is
\[N_k^{\mathrm{flip}}(x)=\left\{y\in F:\sum_{i=1}^n |y_i-x_i|\le k\right\}.\]
Equivalently, every \(y\in N_k^{\mathrm{flip}}(x)\) is obtained by complementing the coordinates in some set \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with \(|S|\le k\), provided the resulting vector remains in \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The radius-k bit-flip neighborhood contains feasible binary vectors obtained by complementing at most k coordinates of the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_k^{\mathrm{flip}}(x)=\{y\in F:\|y-x\|_1\le k\}\).

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bit-Flip Ball Size and Enumeration Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial size and direct enumeration complexity before feasibility filtering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=\{0,1\}^n\), exactly \(\binom nj\) vectors have Hamming distance \(j\) from \(x\), so \(|N_k^{\mathrm{flip}}(x)|=\sum_{j=0}^k\binom nj\). For arbitrary \(F\) this is an upper bound and direct subset enumeration uses at most this many feasibility tests. For fixed \(k\) the count is \(O(n^k)\); when \(k=n\) it is \(2^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full-cube radius-k ball has the binomial-sum size, is polynomially enumerable for fixed radius, and can contain the entire binary cube when the radius varies with dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |N_k^{\mathrm{flip}}(x)|\le\sum_{j=0}^k\binom nj,\quad \sum_{j=0}^k\binom nj=O(n^k)\text{ for fixed }k.
knowledge_statements.title: Bit-Flip Ball Size and Enumeration Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linear representation around a fixed binary incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) and binary \(y\), \(\|y-x\|_1=\sum_{i:x_i=0}y_i+\sum_{i:x_i=1}(1-y_i)\). Therefore \(N_k^{\mathrm{flip}}(x)=F\cap\{y:\sum_{i:x_i=0}y_i+\sum_{i:x_i=1}(1-y_i)\le k\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bit-flip neighborhood is represented by one linear Hamming-distance inequality intersected with the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_k^{\mathrm{flip}}(x)=F\cap\left\{y:\sum_{i:x_i=0}y_i+\sum_{i:x_i=1}(1-y_i)\le k\right\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Hamming-Ball Representation

children.title: Exchange Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Neighborhoods generated by exchanging selected and unselected elements.

knowledge_statements.title: Exchange Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General deletion-insertion exchanges relative to a binary incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), \(x\in F\), \(I_1(x)=\{i:x_i=1\}\), and \(I_0(x)=\{i:x_i=0\}\). For nonnegative integers \(p,q\), define
\[N_{p,q}^{\mathrm{ex}}(x)=\left\{y\in F:\left|I_1(x)\setminus I_1(y)\right|\le p,\ \left|I_1(y)\setminus I_1(x)\right|\le q\right\}.\]
Thus a neighbor deletes at most \(p\) selected elements and inserts at most \(q\) unselected elements; feasibility is tested against the original set \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exchange neighbor removes up to p selected items and inserts up to q unselected items while preserving feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{p,q}^{\mathrm{ex}}(x)\) is the feasible deletion-insertion neighborhood defined by the displayed inequalities.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Candidate count and direct enumeration complexity before feasibility filtering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s=|I_1(x)|\). Exactly \(\binom sa\binom{n-s}{b}\) full-cube vectors delete \(a\) selected coordinates and insert \(b\) unselected coordinates. Hence \(|N_{p,q}^{\mathrm{ex}}(x)|\le\sum_{a=0}^{\min(p,s)}\sum_{b=0}^{\min(q,n-s)}\binom sa\binom{n-s}{b}\), with equality for \(F=\{0,1\}^n\). Direct enumeration has the same feasibility-test bound, is \(O(n^{p+q})\) for fixed \(p,q\), and reaches \(2^n\) when both budgets are unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exchange candidates are counted by independent deletion and insertion choices; fixed budgets give polynomial enumeration, while unrestricted budgets recover the full cube.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |N_{p,q}^{\mathrm{ex}}(x)|\le\sum_{a=0}^{\min(p,s)}\sum_{b=0}^{\min(q,n-s)}\binom sa\binom{n-s}{b}.
knowledge_statements.title: Exchange Neighborhood Enumeration Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orientation reversal for asymmetric deletion-insertion neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x,y\in F\), \(y\in N_{p,q}^{\mathrm{ex}}(x)\) if and only if \(x\in N_{q,p}^{\mathrm{ex}}(y)\). Thus a fixed \((p,q)\) relation need not be symmetric when \(p\ne q\), while equal-budget exchange neighborhoods are symmetric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reversing an exchange swaps its deletion and insertion budgets; equal-budget exchange neighborhoods are symmetric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y\in N_{p,q}^{\mathrm{ex}}(x)\iff x\in N_{q,p}^{\mathrm{ex}}(y).
knowledge_statements.title: Reversal Symmetry of Exchange Budgets

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact deletion and insertion inequalities around a fixed incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) and binary \(y\), deletions equal \(\sum_{i:x_i=1}(1-y_i)\) and insertions equal \(\sum_{i:x_i=0}y_i\). Therefore \(N_{p,q}^{\mathrm{ex}}(x)=F\cap\{y:\sum_{i:x_i=1}(1-y_i)\le p,\ \sum_{i:x_i=0}y_i\le q\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exchange neighborhood is represented by separate linear budgets for selected coordinates turned off and unselected coordinates turned on.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{p,q}^{\mathrm{ex}}(x)\text{ equals }F\text{ intersected with the two displayed inequalities}.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Exchange-Budget Representation

children.title: Swap Neighborhoods
children.top_down_role: Neighborhoods generated by structured swaps among binary assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: Swap Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality-preserving one-for-one exchanges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) and \(x\in F\). The swap neighborhood is
\[N^{\mathrm{swap}}(x)=\left\{y\in F:\exists i,j\text{ with }x_i=1,\ x_j=0,\ y_i=0,\ y_j=1,\ y_\ell=x_\ell\text{ for all }\ell\notin\{i,j\}\right\}.\]
Every swap preserves the number of selected coordinates, so \(\sum_{\ell=1}^n y_\ell=\sum_{\ell=1}^n x_\ell\), while membership in \(F\) enforces all remaining constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A swap neighbor replaces one selected coordinate by one unselected coordinate, preserving cardinality and feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N^{\mathrm{swap}}(x)\subseteq N_{1,1}^{\mathrm{ex}}(x)\) and every member has the same cardinality as \(x\).

notation.meaning: selected coordinate removed by the swap
unselected coordinate inserted by the swap

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality relative to feasible one-for-one swaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization of \(f:F\to\mathbb R\), \(x\in F\) is swap-locally optimal exactly when \(f(y)\ge f(x)\) for every \(y\in N^{\mathrm{swap}}(x)\). Exhaustive feasible-neighbor evaluation certifies only this neighborhood-relative property, not global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absence of an improving feasible swap certifies swap-local, not global, optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ is swap-local}\iff \forall y\in N^{\mathrm{swap}}(x),\ f(y)\ge f(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Swap-Local Optimality Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Raw one-for-one swaps before feasibility filtering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) has \(r\) selected coordinates, it has exactly \(r(n-r)\) distinct raw one-for-one swap candidates. They can be generated once each in \(O(r(n-r))\) time, excluding feasibility and objective-evaluation costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cardinality-r vector has r times n-minus-r raw swap candidates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left|\{x-e_i+e_j:x_i=1,\ x_j=0\}\right|=r(n-r).
knowledge_statements.title: Swap-Neighborhood Candidate Count

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Side Constraints Can Disconnect the Swap Graph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of Johnson-graph connectivity after feasibility filtering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{(1,1,0,0),(0,0,1,1)\}\). Both points have cardinality two but differ in four coordinates, so neither is a one-swap neighbor of the other. The feasible swap graph has two isolated vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal cardinality does not ensure swap connectivity when side constraints remove intermediate points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G_{N^{\mathrm{swap}}}[F]\text{ is disconnected}.
knowledge_statements.title: Side Constraints Can Disconnect the Swap Graph

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Johnson-Graph Structure of a Fixed-Cardinality Layer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Swap geometry without additional side constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F_r=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:\sum_i x_i=r\}\), the swap graph is the Johnson graph \(J(n,r)\). For \(x,y\in F_r\), \(d_{\mathrm{swap}}(x,y)=\tfrac12\|x-y\|_1\); consequently it is connected and has diameter \(\min\{r,n-r\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a complete fixed-cardinality layer, swaps form a Johnson graph and swap distance is half the Hamming distance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_{\mathrm{swap}}(x,y)=\frac12\|x-y\|_1,\qquad \operatorname{diam}J(n,r)=\min\{r,n-r\}.

notation.meaning: Johnson graph on the r-subsets of an n-element set

knowledge_statements.title: Johnson-Graph Structure of a Fixed-Cardinality Layer

children.title: Move-Class Connectivity
children.top_down_role: Reachability and connectivity characteristics induced by the different move classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Move-Class Connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connectivity of a feasible set under a specified move class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) and let \(N:F\rightrightarrows F\) be a symmetric neighborhood map. Form the graph \(G_N=(F,E_N)\), where
\[E_N=\bigl\{\{x,y\}:x,y\in F,\ x\ne y,\ y\in N(x)\bigr\}.\]
The move class \(N\) is connected on \(F\) exactly when, for every \(x,y\in F\), there exist \(m\ge0\) and \(x^0,\ldots,x^m\in F\) such that \(x^0=x\), \(x^m=y\), and \(x^{t+1}\in N(x^t)\) for every \(t<m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A move class is connected when every pair of feasible binary points can be joined by a finite sequence of feasible moves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\) is connected on \(F\iff G_N\) is a connected graph.

notation.meaning: graph induced by the move class

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connectivity test when the finite move graph is explicitly represented.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty finite \(F\), choose \(x^0\in F\) and run breadth-first or depth-first search in \(G_N\). The graph is connected exactly when every vertex is reached. With adjacency lists, the test uses \(O(|F|+|E_N|)\) time and \(O(|F|)\) auxiliary space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One graph traversal tests connectivity of an explicitly represented move graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R(x^0)=F\iff G_N\text{ is connected}.

notation.meaning: vertices reached from the starting point

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Move-Graph Connectivity Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificates for an explicitly represented finite move graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A spanning tree on vertex set \(F\) certifies connectivity of \(G_N\). A nonempty proper set \(S\subset F\) with no edge between \(S\) and \(F\setminus S\) certifies disconnection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spanning tree certifies connectivity; an empty nontrivial edge cut certifies disconnection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\text{ spanning}\Rightarrow G_N\text{ connected};\quad \varnothing\ne S\subsetneq F,\ E_N\cap\delta(S)=\varnothing\Rightarrow G_N\text{ disconnected}.

notation.meaning: pairs with one endpoint in S and one outside S

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Move-Graph Connectivity Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility Preservation Does Not Imply Connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure of reachability under feasible one-bit moves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{(0,0),(1,1)\}\) and permit only feasible one-bit flips. Both vertices have empty neighborhoods, so the move graph has two isolated vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility-preserving move class can leave feasible points in distinct components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G_N\text{ is disconnected}.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Preservation Does Not Imply Connectivity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of symmetric move classes on the same feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N_1,N_2:F\rightrightarrows F\) be symmetric move classes with \(N_1(x)\subseteq N_2(x)\) for every \(x\in F\). Every component of \(G_{N_1}\) lies in a component of \(G_{N_2}\). Hence connectivity of \(N_1\) implies connectivity of \(N_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding feasible moves may merge components but cannot split them.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G_{N_1}\text{ connected}\Rightarrow G_{N_2}\text{ connected}.

notation.meaning: graph induced by move class i

knowledge_statements.title: Connectivity Monotonicity under Move-Class Inclusion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified Local Optimality in a Local-Branching Ball
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conclusion available from globally closing the restricted subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the local-branching subproblem is globally solved and its certified optimum is at least \(f(\bar x)\), then no feasible point within Hamming distance \(k\) improves \(\bar x\). If it is stopped without a valid closing bound or infeasibility certificate, failure to find an improvement proves no such claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally closed local-branching subproblem certifies radius-k local optimality; an unsuccessful truncated run does not.
assumptions_latex: The restricted minimization problem is solved with a valid global certificate for the positive conclusion
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{f(x):x\in F,\Delta(x,\bar x)\le k\}\ge f(\bar x)\Rightarrow \bar x\text{ is radius-}k\text{ locally optimal}.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Local Optimality in a Local-Branching Ball

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact complementary branch for a binary Hamming-ball inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(\Delta(x,\bar x)\) is integer on \(\{0,1\}^n\), the alternatives \(\Delta(x,\bar x)\le k\) and \(\Delta(x,\bar x)\ge k+1\) are disjoint and exhaustive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The local Hamming ball and its greater-than-k complement form an exact binary disjunction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{0,1\}^n=\{x:\Delta(x,\bar x)\le k\}\,\dot\cup\,\{x:\Delta(x,\bar x)\ge k+1\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Local-Branching Complement Partition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical binary local-branching restriction around an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), \(\bar x\in F\), and \(k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}\), define \(\Delta(x,\bar x)=\sum_{i:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)+\sum_{i:\bar x_i=0}x_i\). The local-branching subproblem is \(\min\{f(x):x\in F,\Delta(x,\bar x)\le k\}\). For binary \(x\), \(\Delta(x,\bar x)=\|x-\bar x\|_1\), so the inequality describes the Hamming ball of radius \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local branching optimizes the original binary model within a Hamming ball around an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x\in F:\Delta(x,\bar x)\le k\}=\{x\in F:\|x-\bar x\|_1\le k\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Local-Branching Hamming-Ball Subproblem
Local Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary local-branching constraint around an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a binary feasible region \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), objective \(f:F\to\mathbb R\), incumbent \(\bar x\in F\), and radius \(k\in\{0,ldots,n\}\), the local-branching subproblem is
\[\min\left\{f(x):x\in F,\ \sum_{i:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)+\sum_{i:\bar x_i=0}x_i\le k\right\}.\]
The added inequality is equivalent to \(\|x-\bar x\|_1\le k\) for binary \(x\), and therefore restricts exact optimization to the Hamming ball of radius \(k\) centered at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local branching solves the original binary model inside a Hamming ball centered at an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequality represents \(\{x\in F:\|x-\bar x\|_1\le k\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The standard local-branching formulation requires a specific authoritative citation. In addition, the statement contains `\{0,ldots,n\}` instead of `\{0,\ldots,n\}`; this must be repaired when a sourced replacement is prepared.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic relaxation-guided neighborhood construction, allowing standard signal-selection variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), an incumbent \(\bar x\in F\), and information from a relaxation solution \(z\), select a release set \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) by an explicitly declared relaxation-based rule and search \[N_J(\bar x)=\{x\in F:x_i=\bar x_i\text{ for every }i\notin J\}.\] Standard rules may rank coordinates by incumbent discrepancy \(|z_i-\bar x_i|\), fractionalness, reduced-cost information, or a combination with structural scores. Every returned candidate must be feasible for the original set \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use relaxation information to choose binary variables to release, fix all remaining variables to the incumbent, and search the resulting original-model neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: The rule selecting \(J\) is declared before interpreting the resulting neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_J(\bar x)\subseteq F\quad\text{and}\quad x_i=\bar x_i\ \forall i\notin J\text{ for every }x\in N_J(\bar x).

notation.meaning: solution or information supplied by a relaxation

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Induced Variable-Fixing Neighborhood

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate delivered by exact optimization of a relaxation-induced neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x^J\in\arg\min\{f(x):x\in N_J(\bar x)\}\), then \(x^J\) is certified optimal only over \(N_J(\bar x)\). It is globally optimal over \(F\) only when \(N_J(\bar x)=F\) or independent valid global evidence proves \(f(x^J)=\min_{x\in F}f(x)\). Failure to improve \(\bar x\) is therefore inconclusive outside the selected neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact neighborhood solve certifies only neighborhood optimality; failure to improve does not establish global optimality.
assumptions_latex: The restricted problem over \(N_J(\bar x)\) is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^J\text{ is optimal on }N_J(\bar x)\text{, but not necessarily on }F.

notation.meaning: exact optimizer of the restricted neighborhood

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Neighborhood Optimality Boundary
Relaxation-Induced Neighborhood Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighborhood construction guided by a relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), objective \(f\), incumbent \(\bar x\in F\), relaxation point \(z\in[0,1]^n\), and a selected index set \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), solve
\[\min\{f(x):x\in F,\ x_i=\bar x_i\text{ for every }i\notin J\}.\]
Choose \(J\) from relaxation information, for example as indices having the largest discrepancies \(|z_i-\bar x_i|\). Return an improving feasible optimizer if one is found; otherwise return \(\bar x\). A time or node limit may terminate the restricted solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation information selects variables to release; the original model is then searched exactly or approximately with all other binary variables fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output belongs to \(F\) and differs from \(\bar x\) only on \(J\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is coherent, but selecting released variables by relaxation discrepancy is only one realization of this method family. A specific source is needed to establish the intended method and variant.

children.title: Large-Neighborhood Search
children.top_down_role: Search over neighborhoods that release or reconsider substantial portions of a binary solution.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Destroy-and-repair search using released-variable subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from \(x^0\in F\), iteration \(t\) selects a substantial released set \(J_t\), searches or approximately solves \(\min\{f(y):y\in F_{J_t}(x^t)\}\), validates any returned candidate, and applies a declared acceptance rule. The method stops at a prescribed resource limit and returns the best feasible point encountered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Large-neighborhood search repeatedly releases many variables and repairs the resulting restricted model.
assumptions_latex: Candidate validation, acceptance, and stopping rules are declared
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^{\mathrm{best}}\in F.
knowledge_statements.title: Binary Large-Neighborhood Search Framework

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conclusion from exactly closing one repair subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A certified global solution of \(\min\{f(y):y\in F_J(x)\}\) proves optimality only over \(F_J(x)\). It proves global optimality over \(F\) when \(J=[n]\), but not generally for a proper released set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact repair certifies restricted optimality; only full release converts it into global optimality.
assumptions_latex: The restricted subproblem is solved globally with a valid certificate
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: J=[n]\Rightarrow F_J(x)=F;\qquad J\subsetneq[n]\text{ gives only }F_J(x)\text{-optimality}.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Neighborhood Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restricted Repair Can Miss Every Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when jointly necessary coordinates are not all released.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixing the wrong coordinate can exclude every improving feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in\arg\min_{y\in F_J(x)}f(y)\centernot\Rightarrow x\in\arg\min_{y\in F}f(y).
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Repair Can Miss Every Improvement

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted feasible set underlying binary destroy-and-repair search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), incumbent \(x\in F\), and released set \(J\subseteq[n]\), define \(F_J(x)=\{y\in F:y_i=x_i\text{ for every }i\notin J\}\). If \(J_1\subseteq J_2\), then \(F_{J_1}(x)\subseteq F_{J_2}(x)\), with \(F_\varnothing(x)=\{x\}\) and \(F_{[n]}(x)=F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Releasing more variables enlarges the restricted neighborhood from the incumbent alone to the full feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: J_1\subseteq J_2\Rightarrow F_{J_1}(x)\subseteq F_{J_2}(x).

notation.meaning: feasible points agreeing with x outside J

knowledge_statements.title: Released-Variable Neighborhood
Large-Neighborhood Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Destroy-and-repair search over restricted binary subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), objective \(f\), incumbent \(x^0\in F\), and an iteration limit \(T\). For \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\), select a released set \(J_t\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), approximately solve
\[\min\{f(y):y\in F,\ y_i=x_i^t\text{ for every }i\notin J_t\},\]
and set \(x^{t+1}=y\) when the returned feasible \(y\) satisfies \(f(y)<f(x^t)\); otherwise set \(x^{t+1}=x^t\). Output \(x^T\). Each repair solve may use a prescribed time or node budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Large-neighborhood search repeatedly releases many variables, repairs the restricted model, and accepts improving feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^T\in F\) and \(f(x^{t+1})\le f(x^t)\) under the stated acceptance rule.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited generic local-search section is not sufficiently specific to support this particular improvement-only large-neighborhood-search algorithm. A dedicated LNS source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Adaptive Neighborhood Search
children.top_down_role: Search frameworks that vary neighborhood choice using observed performance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract performance-driven selection without prescribing one score formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal N=\{N_1,\ldots,N_m\}\) be neighborhood operators and let \(x^0\in F\). At iteration \(t\), a controller selects an operator using the search history, searches \(N_{j_t}(x^t)\), applies a declared acceptance rule, records the observed outcome, and updates its selection state. It returns the best verified feasible point encountered at a prescribed stopping limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive neighborhood search uses observed outcomes to alter subsequent neighborhood choices.
assumptions_latex: \(N_j(x)\subseteq F\) for feasible \(x\) and every j, or returned candidates are independently validated
Selection, acceptance, update, and stopping rules are declared
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^{\mathrm{best}}\in F.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Neighborhood-Selection Framework

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition required for claims that every portfolio operator remains available indefinitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an infinite selection sequence \((j_t)\), persistent exploration means \(|\{t:j_t=j\}|=\infty\) for every operator \(j\). A controller that can permanently assign zero selection probability or priority to an operator need not satisfy this condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistent exploration requires every neighborhood operator to be selected infinitely often.
assumptions_latex: The search generates an infinite operator-selection sequence
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall j\in\{1,\ldots,m\},\quad |\{t:j_t=j\}|=\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Exploration Condition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adaptation Alone Gives No Convergence Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of unspecified performance-driven adaptation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: History-dependent neighborhood selection alone implies neither global convergence, local convergence, nor persistent exploration. Such conclusions require additional assumptions on operator coverage, selection frequencies or probabilities, acceptance, neighborhood search accuracy, and stopping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive selection by itself supplies no optimization-convergence guarantee.
assumptions_latex: Only history-dependent neighborhood selection is specified
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{adaptation alone}\centernot\Rightarrow\text{global convergence, local convergence, or persistent exploration}.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptation Alone Gives No Convergence Guarantee
Adaptive Neighborhood Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online selection of neighborhoods using observed search performance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal N=\{N_1,\ldots,N_m\}\) be neighborhood operators, let \(x^0\in F\), and initialize scores \(s_j^0\in\mathbb R\). At iteration \(t\), choose \(j_t\) according to a rule depending on \(s^t\), search \(N_{j_t}(x^t)\), and accept a feasible candidate according to a fixed acceptance rule. After observing reward \(r_t\), update
\[s_j^{t+1}=\begin{cases}(1-\alpha)s_j^t+\alpha r_t,&j=j_t,\\s_j^t,&j\ne j_t,\end{cases}\]
where \(0<\alpha\le1\). Stop at a prescribed iteration or resource limit and return the best feasible point encountered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive neighborhood search updates operator scores from observed rewards and uses them to choose subsequent neighborhoods.
assumptions_latex: \(N_j(x)\subseteq F\) for all feasible \(x\) and all \(j\)
A selection, reward, and acceptance rule are fixed
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns the best feasible point encountered before its stopping limit.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The score update is one particular adaptive operator-selection scheme rather than a universal definition of adaptive neighborhood search. Its selection, reward, and update conventions require a specific source.

children.title: Neighborhood Scale Adaptation
children.top_down_role: Regimes governing changes in neighborhood size during search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract feedback control of a neighborhood-size parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{N_k:k\in K\}\) be a parameterized family of neighborhoods. A neighborhood-scale adaptation rule chooses \(k_{t+1}\in K\) from the current scale and observed search history, subject to declared bounds or admissibility rules. The definition does not prescribe whether success causes expansion, contraction, or another update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Neighborhood-scale adaptation changes a neighborhood-size parameter using observed search information.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a declared set of admissible scales
The scale-update and stopping rules are declared
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: k_t\in K\text{ for every generated iteration}.
knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood-Scale Adaptation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scale Does Not Determine Search Effort or Success
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating neighborhood inclusion from computational behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even when \(N_k(x)\subseteq N_{k+1}(x)\), nestedness alone implies no monotone relation between scale and search time, and no monotone relation between scale and the probability of finding an improvement under a resource limit. Therefore shrink-on-success and expand-on-failure are policies, not universal consequences of nestedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Larger neighborhoods improve opportunity but need not be easier or more successful under a resource limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_k(x)\subseteq N_{k+1}(x)\centernot\Rightarrow\text{monotone computational effort or success probability}.
knowledge_statements.title: Scale Does Not Determine Search Effort or Success

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural consequence when increasing scale enlarges the neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(N_k(x)\subseteq N_{k+1}(x)\) and \(v_k(x)=\min\{f(y):y\in N_k(x)\}\), with \(+\infty\) for an empty neighborhood, then \(v_{k+1}(x)\le v_k(x)\) for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nested neighborhoods, increasing scale cannot worsen the best available objective value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_{k+1}(x)\le v_k(x).

notation.meaning: best objective value available at scale k

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Value Monotonicity for Nested Scales
Neighborhood Scale Adaptation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feedback control of a neighborhood-size parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N_k(x)\subseteq F\) be neighborhoods indexed by \(k\in\{k_{min},\ldots,k_{max}\}\), and initialize \(x^0\in F\) and \(k_0\). At iteration \(t\), search \(N_{k_t}(x^t)\). If an improving feasible point \(yj\) is found, set \(x^{t+1}=y\) and \(k_{t+1}=\max\{k_{min},k_t-\delta_-\}\); otherwise set \(x^{t+1}=x^t\) and \(k_{t+1}=\min\{k_{max},k_t+\delta_+\}\). Stop at a prescribed resource limit and return the best feasible point found.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Neighborhood scale shrinks after successful searches and expands after failures, within fixed bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(N_k(x)\subseteq F\) for every admissible \(k\) and \(x\in F\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k_t\in\{k_{min},\ldots,k_{max}\}\) and \(x^t\in F\) at every iteration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The shrink-on-success and expand-on-failure policy is only one possible scale-adaptation rule and lacks a source. The statement also says an improving point `\(yj\)` is found but subsequently assigns the undefined variable `\(y\)`.

children.title: Feasibility-Pump Interface
children.top_down_role: Integration points between feasibility-pump mechanisms and binary neighborhood search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Required validation before accepting a binary pump output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rounded point \(u\in\{0,1\}^n\) may be used as an incumbent only after verifying \(u\in F\). Binary integrality, proximity to a relaxation point, or feasibility-pump termination alone does not certify the original constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pump point must pass the original feasibility checks before becoming an incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(u\in\{0,1\}^n\) is produced by rounding or pumping
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u\in\{0,1\}^n\centernot\Rightarrow u\in F.
knowledge_statements.title: Pump-Output Validation Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restricted Pump Repair Need Not Reflect Global Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for repair rules that freeze pump coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(J\subseteq[n]\), the restricted repair set \(F_J(u)=\{x\in F:x_i=u_i\text{ for }i\notin J\}\) may be empty even when \(F\ne\varnothing\). Thus certified restricted infeasibility proves neither global infeasibility nor failure of unrestricted Hamming repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Freezing pump coordinates can make repair infeasible although the original model is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_J(u)=\varnothing\centernot\Rightarrow F=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: feasible repair points agreeing with u outside J

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Pump Repair Need Not Reflect Global Feasibility

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hamming Repair Target for a Pump Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Source-independent mathematical repair target for a binary pump output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) and \(u\in\{0,1\}^n\), let \(d_F(u)=\min\{\|x-u\|_1:x\in F\}\), with \(d_F(u)=+\infty\) if \(F=\varnothing\). Then \(d_F(u)=0\) exactly when \(u\in F\), and any optimizer is a nearest feasible point in Hamming distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repair may seek a feasible binary point nearest to the pump output; zero distance is equivalent to feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_F(u)=0\iff u\in F.

notation.meaning: minimum Hamming distance from u to F

knowledge_statements.title: Hamming Repair Target for a Pump Point
Feasibility-Pump Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Handoff from feasibility-pump output to neighborhood search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a binary feasible region \(F\), objective \(f\), relaxation point \(z\in[0,1]^n\), and a feasibility-pump output \(u\in\{0,1\}^n\), define \(J\) from pump diagnostics, such as fractional, unstable, or repeatedly flipped coordinates. If \(u\in F\), use \(u\) as the neighborhood-search incumbent and solve
\[\min\{f(x):x\in F,\ x_i=u_i\text{ for }i\notin J\}.\]
If \(u\notin F\), pass \(u\), \(z\), and \(J\) to a repair neighborhood. Return only a point explicitly verified to belong to \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface converts feasibility-pump points and diagnostics into an incumbent or a restricted repair neighborhood, returning only verified feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any accepted output \(x\) satisfies \(x\in F\).

notation.meaning: coordinates released for search or repair

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed handoff and diagnostic construction are implementation-dependent and are not a standard source-free algorithmic contract. A solver or methodological source must support the pump outputs, released-index rule, and repair behavior.

children.title: Diving Interface
children.top_down_role: Integration points between diving heuristics and binary neighborhood search.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restricted Dive Infeasibility Is Not Model Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary for a fixing-induced repair subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F(D\setminus R,v)=\varnothing\), one may conclude only that no feasible solution satisfies all retained fixings. Unless all fixings are released, this does not imply \(F=\varnothing\). Termination without a valid infeasibility certificate does not even establish emptiness of the restricted region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure of a dive repair invalidates retained fixings, not the entire model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(D\setminus R,v)=\varnothing\centernot\Rightarrow F=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Dive Infeasibility Is Not Model Infeasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical state that a dive may pass to a neighborhood repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), fixing set \(D\subseteq[n]\), assignments \(v\in\{0,1\}^D\), and released set \(R\subseteq D\), define \(F(D\setminus R,v)=\{x\in F:x_i=v_i\text{ for every }i\in D\setminus R\}\). If \(R_1\subseteq R_2\), then \(F(D\setminus R_1,v)\subseteq F(D\setminus R_2,v)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Releasing more dive fixings enlarges the feasible repair region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_1\subseteq R_2\Rightarrow F(D\setminus R_1,v)\subseteq F(D\setminus R_2,v).

notation.meaning: feasible points satisfying all retained dive fixings

knowledge_statements.title: Retained Dive-Fixing Region
Diving Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of a diving state into a repairable neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), let \(z\in[0,1]^n\) be the current relaxation point, and let \(D\) contain coordinates fixed by a diving heuristic to values \(v_i\in\{0,1\}\). Choose a release set \(R\subseteq D\) and solve the neighborhood subproblem
\[\min\{f(x):x\in F,\ x_i=v_i\text{ for every }i\in D\setminus R\}.\]
The interface may enlarge \(R\) after infeasibility or a resource-limit failure. It hands off only feasible solutions, together with their objective values and retained fixings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diving interface retains selected dive fixings, releases others for repair, and passes only verified feasible solutions onward.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned solution lies in \(F\) and satisfies \(x_i=v_i\) for all \(i\in D\setminus R\).

notation.meaning: diving value assigned to coordinate i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The retained-fixing and release policy is implementation-dependent and unsupported by a citation. The objective \(f\) is also used in the subproblem without being introduced or typed.

children.title: Primal-Heuristic Handoff
children.top_down_role: Transfer of candidate solutions and search state across primal heuristic components.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implementation-independent validity boundary for transferring heuristic output to neighborhood search or incumbent management.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A handoff must distinguish a search hint from a claimed feasible solution. A receiver may use a transmitted binary vector \(x\) and explicitly identified neighborhood information as search guidance, but it may admit \(x\) as an incumbent only after verifying \(x\in F\) and recomputing its value under the original objective \(f\). Unverified feasibility, objective values, or provenance metadata cannot constitute incumbent evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heuristic vector may guide neighborhood search, but it becomes an incumbent only after the receiver verifies original-model feasibility and recomputes its objective value.
assumptions_latex: The receiver can evaluate original constraints, integrality, and \(f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ may enter the incumbent set only after }x\in F\text{ and its original-model objective value are verified.}
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Heuristic Handoff Validation
Primal-Heuristic Handoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity contract for transferring heuristic candidates to neighborhood search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a binary model with feasible set \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) and objective \(f\), a primal-heuristic handoff is admissible only if the transmitted record \((x,f(x),M)\) satisfies
\[x\in F,\qquad x\in\{0,1\}^n,\qquad f(x)\text{ is evaluated using the original objective}.\]
The metadata \(M\) must identify any fixed or preferred coordinates and must not assert feasibility for an unchecked candidate. Neighborhood search may use \(x\) as its center; acceptance into the incumbent pool requires independent feasibility and objective validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A handoff supplies a validated binary solution, its original objective value, and neighborhood metadata; the receiver independently checks feasibility and value.
assumptions_latex: The receiving procedure can validate feasibility and objective value
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A candidate enters the incumbent pool only after verifying \(x\in F\) and the transmitted value equals \(f(x)\).

notation.meaning: objective value under the original model

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Independent validation is a reasonable safety principle, but the required metadata and incumbent-pool handoff rules are solver-interface conventions rather than a source-free mathematical condition. A specific implementation or solver-framework source is required.

children.title: Branch-Cut Solver Interface
children.top_down_role: Solver-orchestration boundaries for branching with dynamically generated cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Branch-Cut Solver Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract solver contract for exact minimization of a binary linear program by branching and dynamically separated valid inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a rational binary program \\(\min\{c^\top x:Ax\le b,\ x\in\{0,1\}^n\}\\), a valid-cut separator, and termination tolerances. Maintain a search tree whose nodes carry local bounds and an LP relaxation augmented by globally or locally valid cuts. At each selected node, solve the relaxation; prune it if infeasible or if its bound cannot improve the incumbent. Otherwise invoke permitted callbacks, add accepted cuts and reoptimize, or branch on a disjunction valid for every integer completion. Update the incumbent only with feasible binary points. Return an incumbent \\(x^*\\) and bound \\(L\\); exact termination requires \\(c^\top x^*=L\\), or a declared rational tolerance convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface repeatedly solves node relaxations, accepts valid cuts, branches when needed, prunes certified nodes, and returns an incumbent with a matching global bound at exact termination.
assumptions_latex: \\(A,b,c\\) are rational and the binary feasible set is nonempty or infeasibility is certifiable.
Every submitted cut is valid on its declared global or node-local domain.
Node selection is exhaustive unless bound pruning applies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At exact termination, the returned incumbent is globally optimal, or the solver certifies infeasibility.

notation.meaning: global lower bound for this minimization problem

children.title: Callback Lifecycle Interface
children.top_down_role: Callback events, permitted interventions, and solver-state visibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Callback Lifecycle Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-machine contract for callbacks executed during an exact branch-and-cut search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A callback invocation receives an immutable event state \\(s\\), its declared context \\(q\in\{\mathrm{relaxation},\mathrm{candidate},\mathrm{node}\}\\), and only the operations authorized for \\(q\\). It may inspect exposed values, submit admissible globally or locally valid constraints, reject a candidate with a validity certificate, or request an allowed branching action. Each submission is validated, installed with its declared scope, and followed by reoptimization or node processing as required. Callback-local handles expire when the invocation returns; persistent state must be copied through the documented channel. A callback must not modify solver-owned state except through authorized operations, and repeated invocations must preserve validity independently of event order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each callback receives a typed solver event, may perform only context-authorized actions, and loses event-local handles on return while accepted actions enter the solver lifecycle.
assumptions_latex: The solver declares the contexts and operations available at each event.
Every callback-generated constraint or rejection is valid for its declared scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted callback action preserves the correctness invariants of the branch-and-cut search.

source_refs.locator: 7.5 Using a Branch-and-Bound/Cut System p. 123

source_witnesses.locator: 7.5 Using a Branch-and-Bound/Cut System p. 123

These implementation-neutral API claims need a callback-specific source.

children.title: Cut-Separation Callback Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Correctness and capability limits for cut generation through callbacks.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Separation Callback Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and scope conditions separating permissible cut generation from unsafe solver-state mutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \\(X_N\\) be the integer-feasible completions permitted at the current node and let a callback propose \\(\alpha^\top x\le\beta\\). A globally scoped cut is admissible only if \\(\alpha^\top x\le\beta\\) for every original feasible point \\(x\in X\\); a node-local cut is admissible only if it holds for every \\(x\in X_N\\). Separation may depend on the exposed relaxation point \\(\bar x\\), but violation \\(\alpha^\top\bar x>\beta\\) does not establish validity. The callback may neither infer validity from floating-point samples alone nor exclude an integer candidate without a constraint or certificate valid on the applicable domain. Any dependence on node assumptions must be recorded as local scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut callback may exclude the current relaxation only with an inequality valid for every feasible point in its declared global or node-local domain.
assumptions_latex: \\(X\\) denotes the original feasible set and \\(X_N\subseteq X\\) the current node domain.
The solver distinguishes global from node-local constraint scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Installing an admissible cut cannot remove a feasible integer solution from its declared domain.

notation.meaning: integer-feasible domain at the current node

1.2.2 The Cutting Plane Method p. 11
