children.title: Binary-Master Interface
children.top_down_role: Orchestration of binary master models within decomposed optimization workflows.

knowledge_statements.title: Binary-Master Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master-side representation for decomposition with binary complicating variables and oracle-generated cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \\(Y\subseteq\{0,1\}^p\\), represent the decomposed problem as \\[\min_{y\in Y,\,\theta\in\mathbb R}\ d^\top y+\theta\quad\text{subject to}\quad \theta\ge \ell_k(y)\ \ (k\in K),\qquad g_j(y)\le0\ \ (j\in J).\] The master exposes a candidate \\(\hat y\\) to a subproblem oracle. The oracle returns either a feasible value and an optimality cut \\(\theta\ge\ell(y)\\), or an infeasibility certificate and feasibility cut \\(g(y)\le0\\). Each returned cut must be valid for every \\(y\in Y\\). The master installs cuts, resolves, and reports its lower bound, candidate, and termination status through the coordination interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The binary master optimizes complicating variables and an epigraph variable, sends candidates to an oracle, and receives globally valid feasibility or optimality cuts.
assumptions_latex: The subproblem value is bounded below whenever it is feasible.
All oracle cuts are valid on \\(Y\\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed master is a valid outer approximation of the decomposed problem, becoming exact when its cut families describe the subproblem value and feasibility domain.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
source_refs.locator: 4.4 Benders decomposition p. 52

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
source_witnesses.locator: 4.4 Benders decomposition p. 52

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound-matching certificate for a decomposed optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\hat y,\hat\theta)\) be optimal for the current binary master with value \(L=d^\top\hat y+\hat\theta\). If \(\hat y\) has a feasible subproblem completion of value \(Q(\hat y)\), \(\hat\theta=Q(\hat y)\), and every installed cut is globally valid, then \(L\) is both a master lower bound and the value of a feasible decomposed solution. Hence that solution is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master optimum is globally certified when its candidate has feasible recourse and its certified recourse value matches the master estimate and lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The current master is solved exactly.
Every installed cut is globally valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L=d^\top\hat y+Q(\hat y)\Longrightarrow L=z^*.

notation.meaning: master recourse estimate at the selected candidate

knowledge_statements.title: Binary-Master Exactness Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound monotonicity under accumulation of valid cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, let \(M_{t+1}\) be obtained from \(M_t\) by adding globally valid feasibility or optimality cuts. Then \(F(M_{t+1})\subseteq F(M_t)\), so exact master values satisfy \(L_{t+1}\ge L_t\). Because each master remains an outer approximation of the decomposed problem, every finite \(L_t\) is a global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding valid Benders cuts shrinks the master relaxation, so exact master lower bounds remain valid and nondecreasing.
assumptions_latex: The problem is in minimization form.
Every added cut is globally valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(M_{t+1})\subseteq F(M_t),\qquad L_t\le L_{t+1}\le z^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Binary-Master Lower Bounds

children.title: Benders Coordination Interface
children.top_down_role: Exchange boundaries between binary master decisions and Benders subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Benders Coordination Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative coordination protocol between a binary master and a dual-certified subproblem oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the master with \\(K=J=\varnothing\\), a valid lower model for the recourse value, and no incumbent. At iteration \\(t\\), solve the binary master to obtain \\(y^t,\theta^t\\) and lower bound \\(L_t\\). Query the subproblem at \\(y^t\\). If it is infeasible, obtain a certified feasibility cut violated by \\(y^t\\) and add it to \\(J\\). If it is feasible, obtain value \\(Q(y^t)\\), update the incumbent bound with \\(d^\top y^t+Q(y^t)\\), and add an optimality cut underestimating \\(Q\\) to \\(K\\) when \\(\theta^t<Q(y^t)\\). Stop when the incumbent and master bounds satisfy the prescribed gap; return the incumbent and both bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the binary master, certify its candidate through the subproblem, exchange feasibility or optimality cuts, and stop when master and incumbent bounds meet.
assumptions_latex: Each subproblem response supplies a valid dual or infeasibility certificate.
The master is solved exactly at every iteration.
The selected Benders model admits valid finite-valued lower cuts on feasible master points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon zero-gap termination, the returned incumbent is globally optimal for the decomposed formulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions required for the standard finite-candidate exactness guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A globally invalid cut can remove an optimum, an ineffective response can permit repeated deficient candidates, and an incumbent accepted without certified feasible recourse and its objective value can yield an invalid upper bound. Global cut validity, candidate-level progress, and feasible-value certification are therefore required by the standard finite-candidate termination and bound argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The usual exact Benders guarantee requires valid cuts, progress on deficient candidates, and certified recourse values for incumbents.
assumptions_latex: The claimed guarantee is the finite-candidate exact coordination guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Without these interface invariants, finite exact coordination is not guaranteed.}
knowledge_statements.title: Benders Progress and Validity Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination of exact coordination over a binary master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\subseteq\{0,1\}^p\) be finite. Suppose each nonterminating oracle call at \(y^t\) adds a globally valid cut that either excludes infeasible \(y^t\) or raises its master recourse estimate to the exact finite value \(Q(y^t)\), and the master is solved exactly. If a subsequently selected exact candidate triggers termination rather than an ineffective duplicate cut, the loop performs at most one nonterminating correction per master candidate. At zero gap the incumbent is globally optimal; if every candidate is excluded, the decomposed problem is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact Benders coordination over finitely many binary candidates terminates when each unsuccessful visit excludes its candidate or makes its recourse estimate exact.
assumptions_latex: Every installed cut is globally valid.
Every nonterminating response makes the selected candidate exact or excludes it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{There are at most }|Y|\text{ nonterminating candidate corrections, followed by exact termination.}

notation.meaning: subproblem value at a feasible master candidate

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Candidate Benders Termination

children.title: No-Good Exchange Interface
children.top_down_role: Communication and management of no-good constraints across solver components.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exclusion of every completion of a certified-infeasible partial binary assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\) and \(\hat y_F\in\{0,1\}^F\). If no admissible solution agrees with all fixings \(y_i=\hat y_i\), \(i\in F\), then \[\sum_{i\in F:\hat y_i=1}(1-y_i)+\sum_{i\in F:\hat y_i=0}y_i\ge1\] is valid and excludes exactly the binary vectors agreeing with \(\hat y_F\) throughout \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infeasible partial assignment yields one no-good inequality excluding all of its binary completions.
assumptions_latex: No admissible solution agrees with \(\hat y_F\) on every index in \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every admissible vector satisfies the inequality, while every completion of the certified partial assignment violates it.

notation.meaning: indices fixed by the partial assignment

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Assignment No-Good Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact exclusion message for one certified-inadmissible binary master assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\hat y\in\{0,1\}^p\), the inequality \[\sum_{i:\hat y_i=1}(1-y_i)+\sum_{i:\hat y_i=0}y_i\ge 1\] has left-hand side equal to the Hamming distance from \(\hat y\) on the binary domain. It therefore excludes exactly \(\hat y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard no-good inequality requires a future binary vector to differ from the rejected assignment in at least one coordinate.
assumptions_latex: The excluded assignment is certified inadmissible for the maintained search target, or its removal is an explicitly valid enumeration step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality excludes \(\hat y\) and no other binary vector.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Assignment No-Good Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination bound for assignment-by-assignment no-good exchange.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an exact oracle classifies every queried \(y\in\{0,1\}^p\), every rejected assignment receives a permanent exact no-good, and excluded assignments are never queried again, then at most \(2^p\) distinct assignments are queried before an admissible assignment is returned or the binary domain is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permanent exact no-goods give finite exhaustive enumeration with at most \(2^p\) distinct oracle queries.
assumptions_latex: The master domain is contained in \(\{0,1\}^p\).
Oracle classifications and installed no-goods are exact.
Previously excluded assignments are not returned again.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At most \(2^p\) distinct assignments are queried.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Enumeration by Exact No-Goods

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and strength boundary of assignment-specific exclusion messages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact-assignment no-good for \(\hat y\) removes only \(\hat y\) from \(\{0,1\}^p\), supplies no objective bound, and excludes no distinct assignment. Installing it without a valid rejection or enumeration justification can remove a required feasible solution; assignment-by-assignment exchange may require \(2^p\) exclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact no-good carries only assignment-specific exclusion information and may be exponentially weak.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sound use requires a valid exclusion justification, and exact no-goods alone need not provide compact progress.
knowledge_statements.title: Information Limit of Exact No-Goods
No-Good Exchange Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact exclusion certificate communicated after a binary master assignment is rejected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rejected assignment \\(\hat y\in\{0,1\}^p\\), define \\(S_1=\{i:\hat y_i=1\}\\) and \\(S_0=\{i:\hat y_i=0\}\\). The no-good inequality is \\[\sum_{i\in S_1}(1-y_i)+\sum_{i\in S_0}y_i\ge1.\] For binary \\(y\\), its left side is the Hamming distance from \\(\hat y\\); hence it excludes exactly \\(\hat y\\). A subproblem may return this inequality only after certifying that \\(\hat y\\) is inadmissible, or when deliberate enumeration permits unconditional exclusion of an already processed assignment. The exchange record contains \\(\hat y\\), the rejection status, the inequality, and whether any stronger validity claim is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A no-good message excludes exactly one rejected binary assignment using a Hamming-distance inequality and must carry the status justifying that exclusion.
assumptions_latex: The assignment \\(\hat y\\) has been certified inadmissible or is intentionally removed after exhaustive processing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality removes \\(\hat y\\) and no other binary vector.

notation.meaning: indices assigned one and zero in the rejected vector

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports the exact no-good inequality interface.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Hamming-distance no-good inequality and its exact-one-assignment exclusion claim are mathematically correct, but no inspectable source and locator are supplied for this certificate interface.

children.title: Master–Subproblem Handoff
children.top_down_role: Transfer of candidate decisions, certificates, and feedback between master and subordinate components.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical validity contract for conclusive subordinate responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a master candidate \(\hat y\), a conclusive subordinate response is sound if it contains at least one checkable consequence of the appropriate type: a feasible completion with its objective value; a globally valid feasibility inequality satisfied by every extendable master decision and violated by \(\hat y\); or a globally valid lower function \(\ell(y)\le Q(y)\). Incumbent acceptance additionally requires a certified feasible completion and its value. Only certified consequences may update incumbents, prune candidates, or strengthen global bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The handoff may change global solver state only through a verified completion, a globally valid feasibility cut, or a globally valid recourse lower bound.
assumptions_latex: Master and subordinate components use consistent variable, feasibility, and objective conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Accepted conclusive responses preserve incumbent feasibility and global-bound validity.}
knowledge_statements.title: Sound Handoff Response Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by discarding a returned constraint's validity scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y=\{0,1\}\) and minimize \(Q(y)\), where \(Q(0)=1\) and \(Q(1)=0\). Under a local context fixing \(y=0\), the inequality \(y\le0\) is valid. If the handoff omits that scope and the master installs \(y\le0\) globally, it removes the unique optimum \(y=1\). Thus the validity domain is part of the returned certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint valid only under a local context can remove the true optimum when installed globally.
assumptions_latex: The problem is in minimization form.
The local context \(y=0\) is not globally valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A scope mismatch can invalidate the master even when the returned local statement is true.}
knowledge_statements.title: Local-Scope Cut Installed Globally

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe behavior when the subordinate component supplies no certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a subordinate response supplies neither a feasible completion nor a valid feasibility or optimality certificate, it establishes no new global bound, no infeasibility of the candidate, and no permission to prune. The master may retry or terminate with unresolved status, but treating absence of a certificate as feasibility, infeasibility, or optimality is unsound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A timeout, numerical failure, or unresolved call cannot by itself justify pruning, bound strengthening, or incumbent acceptance.
knowledge_statements.title: Unresolved-Response Noninference Rule
Master–Subproblem Handoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Typed request-response contract preserving bounds and validity across a decomposition boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The master sends a request \\(r=(y^t,\eta_t,\sigma_t)\\), containing a binary candidate, the relevant master estimate, and a model-version identifier. The subproblem returns exactly one typed response: certified infeasibility with a valid feasibility cut; certified feasibility with value \\(Q(y^t)\\), a recoverable completion, and optionally a valid optimality cut; or unresolved status with no pruning claim. The master accepts a response only when its version matches \\(\sigma_t\\), verifies its declared scope, installs valid cuts, and updates an incumbent only from a feasible completion. An unresolved or stale response may trigger recomputation but must not exclude \\(y^t\\) or strengthen a bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The handoff sends a versioned binary candidate and accepts only certified feasibility, infeasibility, value, cut, and completion data; unresolved responses cannot prune.
assumptions_latex: Master and subproblem use consistent objective and feasibility conventions.
Every conclusive response includes a checkable certificate or a solver-trusted exact status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted responses preserve master-bound validity and incumbent feasibility.

notation.meaning: master estimate relevant to the request

children.title: Set-Partitioning Master Interface
children.top_down_role: Binary master-model interfaces for set-partitioning structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Partitioning Master Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-master representation for selecting columns that partition every item exactly once.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \\(I\\) be the item set and \\(\mathcal P\\) a family of feasible columns, with incidence \\(a_{ip}\in\{0,1\}\\) and cost \\(c_p\\). The set-partitioning master is \\[\min\left\{\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}c_p\lambda_p:\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}a_{ip}\lambda_p=1\ \forall i\in I,\ \lambda_p\in\{0,1\}\ \forall p\in\mathcal P\right\}.\] A restricted master uses \\(\mathcal P'\subseteq\mathcal P\\), exposes dual multipliers \\(\pi_i\\) from its LP relaxation, and accepts a new column \\(p\\) with its incidence vector, cost, and reduced cost \\(\bar c_p=c_p-\sum_{i\in I}\pi_i a_{ip}\\). Columns enter only after feasibility and duplicate checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master selects feasible columns so every item is covered exactly once, while its LP dual prices define the reduced costs used by pricing.
assumptions_latex: Each column represents a feasible atomic structure.
The complete column family admits a partition whenever the original instance is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Binary feasible master solutions are precisely partitions expressible by the supplied columns.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Set-Partitioning LP Dual and Pricing Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual representation and full-master LP optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^\top\lambda:A\lambda=\mathbf1,\lambda\ge0\}\), the dual is \[\max\{\mathbf1^\top\pi:A^\top\pi\le c,\ \pi\in\mathbb R^I\}.\] Column \(p\) has reduced cost \(\bar c_p=c_p-a_p^\top\pi\). An optimal restricted-master dual vector that satisfies \(a_p^\top\pi\le c_p\) for every omitted column certifies full-master LP optimality. Equality of restricted and full optimal values holds exactly when some optimal restricted-master dual vector is feasible for the full dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The LP dual assigns unrestricted item prices, and a full-dual-feasible restricted-master optimum certifies full-master LP optimality.
assumptions_latex: The full master LP is feasible and has a finite optimum.
The stated restricted-master primal and dual solutions are optimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certified nonnegative reduced cost for every omitted column proves equality of the restricted and full LP optimal values.

notation.meaning: free dual vector for the equality rows

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Partitioning LP Dual and Pricing Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of infeasibility inference from an incomplete active column family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mathcal P'\subsetneq\mathcal P\), infeasibility of \(A_{\mathcal P'}\lambda=\mathbf1,\lambda\ge0\) does not imply infeasibility of the full master. Such an implication requires consideration of every full-master column or an exact feasibility-pricing certificate ruling out every omitted column capable of restoring feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infeasible restricted set-partitioning master does not by itself certify full-master infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master may omit columns from \(\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Initialization requires a feasible active column set, artificial variables, or certified feasibility pricing.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Feasibility Boundary

children.title: Branch-Price Coordination Interface
children.top_down_role: Coordination of branching decisions with dynamic column generation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-level coordination of restricted-master optimization, exact pricing, fathoming, and branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each search node \(N\), solve a feasible restricted-master LP and price over every column admissible under the node restrictions. Add negative-reduced-cost columns and repeat. When exact pricing certifies that no admissible omitted column has negative reduced cost, the restricted-master value is the full node-LP bound. Prune only by certified infeasibility or incumbent dominance; accept only an integer-feasible master solution; otherwise create children whose integer-feasible sets cover the unresolved parent solutions and whose restrictions are enforced during pricing. Exhaustion of all active nodes proves global optimality or infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch-price alternates restricted-master solves with exact node pricing, then safely prunes, accepts an integer solution, or branches using restrictions understood by pricing.
assumptions_latex: Every node restricted master is made feasible or its full node infeasibility is certified.
Pricing is exact over all node-admissible columns.
Branching covers every unresolved parent integer solution.
Node processing is exhaustive except for certified fathoming.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exhausting the valid search tree returns a globally optimal integer master solution or certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Branch-Price Coordination
Branch-Price Coordination Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-level coordination of restricted-master optimization, pricing, branching, and global bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each branch-and-bound node \\(N\\), initialize a restricted column set compatible with the node restrictions. Repeatedly solve the restricted-master LP, send its dual vector and branching restrictions to the pricing oracle, and add every returned compatible column of negative reduced cost. When pricing certifies that no such column exists, the restricted-master value is the complete node-LP bound. Prune \\(N\\) if infeasible or dominated by the incumbent; update the incumbent from an integral feasible master solution; otherwise impose a pricing-compatible disjunction and create child nodes. Columns may be shared only with nodes where they satisfy all local restrictions. Return an optimal incumbent when all nodes are fathomed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every search node, alternate restricted-master solves with certified pricing, then prune, accept an integral solution, or branch using restrictions understood by pricing.
assumptions_latex: The pricing oracle solves its reduced-cost problem exactly or provides a valid lower-bound certificate.
All generated columns satisfy the node restrictions.
The node search is exhaustive except for valid fathoming.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When all nodes are fathomed, the returned incumbent is optimal for the full integer master.

children.title: Pricing-Compatible Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching regimes that preserve a usable pricing structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical together-or-separate branching for fractional set-partitioning solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For distinct items \(i,j\), define \(z_{ij}=\sum_{p:a_{ip}=a_{jp}=1}\lambda_p\). In every binary set-partitioning solution, \(z_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\). If \(0<z_{ij}<1\) at a node LP solution, create children \(z_{ij}=0\) and \(z_{ij}=1\). In the separate child, pricing forbids columns containing both items. In the together child, pricing forbids columns containing exactly one of the two items. When these predicates are enforceable by the pricing oracle, the branching is pricing-compatible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ryan–Foster branching requires two items to occur in the same selected column or in different selected columns, enforcing the corresponding restrictions during pricing.
assumptions_latex: The master is a binary set-partitioning model.
Pricing can enforce the together and separate predicates for the selected pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two children are disjoint, cover every parent integer solution, and retain implicit column generation.

notation.meaning: total master weight on columns containing both items

review_flags: A direct scholarly locator for the named branching rule remains desirable.
knowledge_statements.title: Ryan–Foster Pair Branching

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General correctness and oracle-compatibility criterion for branching in an implicit-column master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_N\) be the parent node's integer-feasible master solutions and let children have feasible sets \(F_{N,k}\). A branching rule is search-correct when the children form an exhaustive disjoint partition, \[F_N=\mathbin{\dot\bigcup}_k F_{N,k}.\] It is pricing-compatible relative to a specified oracle when each child's restrictions can be imposed so that the oracle optimizes reduced cost over exactly that child's admissible columns, without enumerating the full parent column family. No equality or partition of the individual child column families is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing-compatible branching partitions the parent integer solutions and leaves each child's restricted pricing problem exactly solvable by the chosen oracle.
assumptions_latex: The parent and child integer-feasible solution sets are well defined.
The pricing oracle has an exact formulation for every child restriction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The children preserve search completeness and permit exact implicit pricing at every child.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Compatible Branching Criterion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Empty Total Intersection Does Not Define a Branch Partition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to using only child coverage and empty total intersection as branching correctness conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_N=\{a,b,c\}\) and define \(F_{N,1}=\{a,b\}\), \(F_{N,2}=\{b,c\}\), and \(F_{N,3}=\{a,c\}\). Then \(\bigcup_kF_{N,k}=F_N\) and \(\bigcap_kF_{N,k}=\varnothing\), yet every pair of children overlaps. Thus coverage plus empty total intersection does not make the children a disjoint branch partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Three overlapping children can cover the parent and have empty total intersection, so those conditions do not ensure valid disjoint branching.
assumptions_latex: A branch partition is required to assign every parent integer solution to exactly one child.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pairwise disjointness, or an equivalent unique-child condition, must be imposed separately.
knowledge_statements.title: Empty Total Intersection Does Not Define a Branch Partition
Pricing-Compatible Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion ensuring that branch disjunctions remain enforceable inside the pricing problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \\(\mathcal P_N\\) be the columns allowed at node \\(N\\), and let branching create children indexed by \\(k\\) with column families \\(\mathcal P_{N,k}\\). The branching rule is pricing-compatible when \\[\mathcal P_N=\bigcup_k\mathcal P_{N,k},\qquad \bigcap_k F_{N,k}=\varnothing,\] where \\(F_{N,k}\\) denotes the integer master solutions satisfying child \\(k\\), every parent integer solution belongs to at least one \\(F_{N,k}\\), and membership in \\(\mathcal P_{N,k}\\) can be enforced by the pricing oracle without enumerating \\(\mathcal P_N\\). Thus each child pricing problem generates exactly columns satisfying its branch restrictions, while the children collectively preserve all parent integer solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branching rule is pricing-compatible when its children cover all parent integer solutions and each child restriction can be enforced directly by the pricing oracle.
assumptions_latex: The parent node has a well-defined admissible column family \\(\mathcal P_N\\).
Each child restriction has a corresponding enforceable pricing predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Branching preserves search completeness without requiring enumeration of the full column family.

notation.meaning: columns admissible in child \\(k\\) of node \\(N\\)
integer master solutions admitted by child \\(k\\)

review_flags: Supplied locators do not identify a source for the exact pricing-compatible branching criterion.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied, and the displayed criterion is unreliable: requiring only the total intersection of child solution sets to be empty does not make the children mutually exclusive, while equality of parent and child column-family unions is neither the standard solution-space coverage condition nor generally necessary. A sourced, variant-specific branching criterion is required.

children.title: Column-Pool Handoff
children.top_down_role: Exchange and retention of generated columns across search components.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer and reuse of generated columns among restricted masters and compatible search nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A receiving restricted master may admit a pooled column only after verifying that it is a valid full-master column and satisfies the receiving node's restrictions. Its reduced cost must be recomputed from the receiving master's current dual vector. Duplicate columns may be coalesced, and valid inactive columns may remain cached. A column generated under another node may be reused wherever these checks succeed; generation scope alone neither guarantees nor forbids reuse. Failure of a finite pool scan to find an improving column is not a pricing certificate unless all admissible omitted columns were searched exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The receiver validates every pooled column against its own model and node, reprices it under current duals, and never treats an unproductive pool scan as exact pricing.
assumptions_latex: Transferred columns carry enough structural data to test full-master validity and node admissibility.
Reduced costs are evaluated using the receiving restricted master's current dual solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted columns are valid at the receiving node, while pool exhaustion alone makes no full-pricing claim.
knowledge_statements.title: Validity-Preserving Column-Pool Handoff
Column-Pool Handoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Typed transfer of generated columns between pricing, restricted masters, and compatible search nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A column-pool record is \\(h=(a,c,\kappa,\sigma)\\), containing an incidence vector, objective cost, canonical key, and validity scope. On receipt, the master verifies structural feasibility, recomputes the cost and reduced cost under its current dual vector, rejects duplicate keys, and checks that the current node satisfies \\(\sigma\\). Accepted columns are inserted into the restricted master; inactive valid columns may remain cached. A column generated under local branching restrictions must not be exported outside their descendant scope. Changes in dual multipliers alter reduced cost but not structural validity, so cached columns may be repriced. Pool exhaustion is not a pricing optimality certificate unless the pricing oracle separately certifies absence of improving columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A column handoff carries structure, cost, identity, and scope; the receiver validates and reprices it, while pool exhaustion alone never certifies pricing optimality.
assumptions_latex: Canonical keys identify structurally identical columns.
Every local column carries all branching restrictions needed to determine its scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The handoff cannot introduce an invalid or out-of-scope column when all acceptance checks succeed.
